The proposed method retains analytical updates for the prediction covariance and two reliability probabilities, while adopting CVI to estimate the state and baseline measurement covariance. The covariance update combines the analytical contribution from clean measurements with Monte Carlo gradient estimates for corrupted measurements. Numerical results on a re-entry tracking benchmark demonstrate the superior accuracy of the proposed method in both state and noise covariance estimation. Remarkably, even built upon the linear Kalman filtering (KF) framework that is originally designed for linear systems, our method achieves more accurate estimation performance than dedicated nonlinear filtering algorithms based on the cubature Kalman filter (CKF).

The goal of this article is to introduce the category of effective filtered multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and the category of multivariable $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules of finite $E_Δ$-height over the rigid-analytic open polydisk $\mathcal{O}_Δ$, and to establish an exact tensor equivalence between them. This generalizes Kisin's analytic classification of filtered $(\varphi, N)$-modules and provides the rigid-analytic foundation for multivariable $p$-adic Hodge theory.
Quantitative homogenization of Stokes flow in a perforated domain under low regularity of data and geometry

We study the homogenization of the steady Stokes equations with no-slip conditions in a domain perforated by $\varepsilon$-periodic obstacles, whose limit is Darcy's law for the homogenized pressure $p^\ast$. We prove the quantitative error estimate with rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, natural in the presence of a boundary layer, only assuming that $f-\nabla p^\ast\in H^1$. Such estimates were previously available only under strong smoothness assumptions, such as $f\in C^{1,1/2}$. Our geometrical assumptions are also less stringent than in the previous analyses. The outer domain and the reference fluid cell need only be Lipschitz, the perforations may deviate from periodicity in a layer of width $O(\varepsilon)$ near the outer boundary, and the solid part may be connected (in three dimensions) and attached to the outer wall. In the absence of a boundary layer, the same argument yields the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ assuming only $f\in H^1$.
Learning Morse Lyapunov functions through invertible neural networks

Towards data-driven stability certificates of dynamical systems, we are witnessing renewed interest in studying and exploiting the structure of Lyapunov functions. Especially Lyapunov functions that are locally quadratic (i.e., Morse) gained popularity ever since it was understood that they can be written as the norm squared of a diffeomorphism. This topological representation alludes to parametrizations using invertible neural networks. In this note we discuss when and how such functions can be learned. In particular, using neural ODEs (NODEs), we characterize Sobolev approximation of these diffeomorphisms on compact sets and show how this naturally relates to stability. We also connect our results to PLNets and supply numerical experiments for illustration.
Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality implies superreflexivity

We prove that if \(X\) is a Banach space for which Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality holds, then \(X\) is superreflexive. We also present an example of a superreflexive Banach space for which the vector-valued Stein property fails.
Classes of non-invertible simple derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $n\geq 3$ be an integer. For $2\leq j\leq n-1$, let $a_j\in k$, and $g_j(x_j)\in k[x_j]\setminus k.$ We give two classes of simple and non-invertible $k$-derivations of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n].$ The first class consists of the $k$-derivations $(1 +x_1^{m_2}x_2)\partial_{x_1}+x_1^{m_1}\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $m_1$ and $m_2$ are two positive integers such that $m_2$ does not divide $m_1$. The second class consists of $k$-derivations $(1-x_2^α x_1^β)\partial_{x_1} +x_1^m\partial_{x_2}+(a_2 x_3 +g_2(x_2))\partial_{x_3}+\cdots+(a_{n-1}x_n + g_{n-1}(x_{n-1}))\partial_{x_n},$ where $α\geq 1,β\geq 1$ and $m\geq β+1$ are integers, under the assumption that $a_j=0,$ for all $2\leq j\leq n-1$ or deg$_{x_2}g_2(x_2)=1$.
Angular-Pole Flag Curvature and Conformal Control of Radial Jacobi Fields in Diagonal Conic Finsler Optics

We study diagonal conic Finsler optical structures with radial coefficients and an arbitrary angular Finsler norm. We obtain the spray curvature block and identify the angular-pole radial-transverse flag curvature at a critical radius with the negative optical-arclength radial Jacobi coefficient. We prove that a compactly supported radial conformal two-jet determines the critical radius and any signed radial coefficient. A navigation Randers sphere yields unequal oriented periods with a common radial coefficient.
The least Carmichael numbers with $k$ prime factors

Let $S_k$ denote the least Carmichael number with exactly $k$ prime factors. Like the later searches of Pinch, our algorithm builds the prime factors of a candidate in increasing order and stops as soon as the preproduct $P$ satisfies $Pλ(P) > B$. At that point there is at most one possible cofactor, and we recover all of its prime factors at once in polynomial time. We prove an unconditional bound on the number of candidates the search examines, in terms of how far $B$ exceeds the product of the first $k$ primes. When the search is run in doubling passes, this gives a running time of $e^{O(k)} = S_k^{O(1/\log k)}$ under a natural conjecture on the size of $S_k$. We also show that the constant in the exponent is sharp for the set of square-free numbers that the bound counts. Finally, we compute $S_k$ for every $k \leq 64$; Pinch had computed it for $k \leq 35$.
Two-Dimensional Kowalevski Top Problem as the Genus Two Full Jacobi Inversion Problem -Formulation Using Kolossoff Variables-

For the Kowalevski top, we introduce another variable in addition to time variable, and formulate as the two-dimensional model. In this paper, since the results for the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem for the two variables Kowalevski top are already known, we utilize these results in reverse, introducing Kolossoff variables, to derive a more transparent formulation of the genus two full Jacobi inversion problem. Since there are two implicit equations of motion using Kowalevski variables, we derived two explicit equations of motion using Kolossoff variables, which is different from the Kolossoff method to derive only one explicit equation and to use Hamiltonian-Jacobi theory.
The Singular LeBrun Transform: Complex Conformal and Contact Geometry

A holomorphic conformal structure is rigid in the presence of rational curves: a complex conformal manifold that is not conformally flat contains no immersed rational null geodesic. So a natural compactification of such a manifold, on which its null geodesics close up, must degenerate along the boundary. We study this phenomenon for the complex conformal manifold that LeBrun attached to a complex contact manifold $Z$ in inverting Salamon's twistor construction: the space $M_{\mathbb{C}}$ of balanced conics of $Z$ transverse to the contact distribution, with its holomorphic Riemannian metric of holonomy contained in $\mathrm{Sp}(n,\mathbb{C})\mathrm{Sp}(1,\mathbb{C})$. Its compactification by the degenerate conics of $Z$ forces the metric to become singular at the boundary. We develop a framework, the singular LeBrun transform, in which these singularities are a source of information rather than an obstacle: the singularities of the metric and of its curvature are read off from the degenerate rational curves of $Z$, locally through the contact neighbourhood of a curve and globally through the incidence variety. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture that all positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds are symmetric, which was recently claimed by OpenAI and by Hu, Liu and Wan. The emphasis of the paper, however, is less on this result than on the framework developed here, which should apply to other problems of the same kind; we conclude with two such directions, negative quaternionic-Kähler manifolds and a singular Merkulov transform for Legendre moduli spaces.
The Odd Shift is not sofic in dimensions $d \ge 3$

In this paper, we prove that the Odd Shift $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimensions $d \ge 3$. Our proof uses lower bounds from communication complexity, specifically the result of Raz and Spieker on the nondeterministic communication complexity for the connectivity problem. We also prove that $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimension $d=2$ under the assumption we call Mute Ocean.
Radial symmetry for the positive Kähler--Einstein Dirichlet problem on the ball

We prove radial symmetry for every strictly plurisubharmonic function $u$ on the unit ball in $\C^n$, $n\ge2$, that is smooth up to the boundary, vanishes there, and has complex Hessian determinant $μe^{-u}$ for a constant $μ>0$. The known Fubini--Study family therefore exhausts all such solutions. For the corresponding complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation, this establishes the Berman--Berndtsson symmetry conjecture in the smooth class and gives uniqueness throughout the known existence range. The classification also yields the sharp Moser--Trudinger inequality on the ball in Cegrell's finite-energy class.
The Exact Optimal Delivery Scheme for the Cyclically $L$-Separated Placement in Multi-Access Coded Caching
Kai Wan; Huimei Wei; Minquan Cheng; Giuseppe Caire

This paper investigates the $(K, L, M, N)$ multi-access coded caching (MACC) system introduced by Hachem et al. The system consists of a server storing $N$ equal-sized files, $K$ cache nodes, each with a storage capacity of $M$ files, and $K$ users, each accessing $L$ consecutive cache nodes in a cyclic wrap-around topology. The server transmits coded information to the users via an error-free capacitated broadcast channel, such that each user obtains its own requested file as a combination of the server transmission and the accessible caches' content. Our objective is to minimize the worst-case transmission load over all possible user demands. First, for the cyclically $L$-separated placement, we derive a new converse bound using the acyclic index coding bound. By carefully counting all valid cache supports, the proposed converse improves upon an existing bound for the same placement. We then develop a linear coded caching scheme based on a novel determinant-based interference alignment strategy, which achieves the new converse bound exactly. Exploiting the determinant structure of a random generating matrix (each of whose columns corresponds to one user), this scheme simultaneously aligns interference across all users into low-dimensional subspaces, while preserving the decodability of their desired packets. Furthermore, by averaging acyclic index coding bounds over cyclic user permutations, we derive a general converse bound applicable to arbitrary uncoded cache placements. By combining the proposed scheme with memory sharing, we demonstrate that the achievable transmission load is within a factor of two of the global bound under uncoded placement. Finally, theoretical and numerical comparisons demonstrate that the proposed scheme generally achieves a strictly lower load than existing schemes.
Optimal Quadrature and the Curse of Dimensionality for a Veronese Class

We study integration on a $3^d$-dimensional trigonometric space whose unit ball has all coordinate mixed partial derivatives bounded by one. With evaluations anywhere in $\mathbb{R}^d$, we determine the exact minimal worst-case error among all deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ function values. An optimal quadrature formula is obtained by truncating an exact product quadrature formula on $\{1/2, 1/2+π\}^d$. All weights are positive. For each error tolerance $0<\varepsilon<1$, the information complexity grows exponentially in $d$ with the common base $Λ\approx 1.10546546$. The correction of order $\sqrt{d}$ to the logarithm of the information complexity and the corresponding error limit are determined by the standard normal distribution function. For $b\ge 1$ and $n=\lceil b^d\rceil$, the error tends to one, one half, or zero according as $b<Λ$, $b=Λ$, or $b>Λ$.
Null flag curvature of anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics
Marcelo Inagaki; Miguel Ángel Javaloyes; Patrícia Marçal

We consider the Zermelo navigation problem for a time-dependent Finsler metric, which can be recast as the study of lightlike geodesics of a Lorentz--Finsler metric on a non-relativistic spacetime. To control how such geodesics separate, we introduce a null flag curvature, defined for any pseudo-Finsler metric with a lightlike cone, and show that it governs the Taylor expansion of the norm of a Jacobi field. We then prove a formula relating the null flag curvatures of two anisotropically conformal pseudo-Finsler metrics. Applying it to the spacetime associated with a time-independent Randers metric, which is anisotropically conformal to a stationary spacetime, we obtain compact expressions for the flag curvature of Randers metrics, both in terms of their $(α,β)$ data and of their Zermelo data $(h,W)$. These expressions allow us to compute explicitly the flag curvature when $W$ is conformal, affine or projective, and when $α$ is a Kähler metric. We also introduce a Weyl-type curvature, invariant under anisotropic conformal changes, whose vanishing characterizes Finsler manifolds of scalar flag curvature, and we obtain the flag curvature of $F + \mathrm{d}f$, showing in particular that $F$ has scalar flag curvature if and only if $F + \mathrm{d}f$ does.
Curvature condition on the Wasserstein space over a closed Riemannian manifold

We establish regularity results for the solution flow of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDE) on the Wasserstein space $\mathscr{P}(M)$ over a closed Riemannian manifold, under suitable assumptions on the driving vector fields. We derive the SDE governing the associated tangent process and prove its well-posedness by means of the framework developped in \cite{Martin2025} for Covariant SDEs on Inverse Limit Hilbert vector bundles over the diffeomorphism group. We introduce the $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$ condition, a geometric curvature-type condition which generalizes, in the setting of SDEs on $¶(M)$, both the $\mathrm{H.C.K.}$ condition introduced in \cite{cattiaux:hal-00805299} and the ergodicity condition of \cite[Section 4]{wang2020}. Finally, combining this condition with the theory of entropic interpolations (see \cite{Leonard2014}), we establish several consequences of $\mathrm{IWC}(K)$, including control of the distance between two trajectories, gradient estimates for the associated Markov semigroup and a local Poincar{é} inequality. In the case $K >0$, we further obtain the existence and uniqueness of an ergodic invariant measure for the associated semigroup.
The monoid of orientation preserving mappings on a chain
Paul M. Catarino; Peter M. Higgins
We introduce new kinds of regular monoids of transformations consisting of mappings which preserve or reverse the orientation of a finite cycle.
A Rollout-Based Approach to Real-Time Topology and Dispatch Control in the AI4RealNet L2RPN Benchmark
David Krame Kadurha; Robbert van der Burg; Alessandro Zocca; Sandjai Bhulai

Operating transmission networks under uncertain outages requires coordinating discrete network topology actions with continuous adjustments to generation and storage, while respecting operational constraints and real-time computational limits. We present a rollout-based controller that combines discrete and continuous decisions under the uncertain contingency policy of the L2RPN AI4RealNet 2026 challenge. Power-flow approximations and convex optimization identify the most promising actions, followed by short-horizon simulations to predict their effect on congestion, renewable curtailment, and redispatching costs. A further policy exploits the benchmark's specific attack protocol: keeping selected lines disconnected prevents some adversarial outages from being initiated. On the benchmark's $118$-bus network, the controller completed $189$ of $208$ final-test scenarios (score $64.39$) and achieved the second-best ratio of score to computation time among the five top-ranked entries, behind one that scored lower. Our results show that combining structured optimization with simulation-based action selection is effective even without a learned decision rule, and fast enough for real-time control. Code and reproduction material: https://github.com/DavidKrame/RAD_agent__AI4RealNet_competition.
Relaxation of one-dimensional variational problems without growth constraints

We study the integral representation of the relaxation of integral functionals of the form u-> \int f(x,u(x),u'(x)) dx, for Sobolev functions u\,: (a, b) $\rightarrow$ RN with fixed Dirichlet boundary conditions. Unlike classical works on the subject, we require a very mild growth condition on the Lagrangian f to make our statement as natural and general as possible. We state four different situations in which we manage to obtain an explicit expression for the relaxation on BV , which is usually the natural framework for such weak growth conditions. Our goal is also to express a few unifying assumptions on the Lagrangian to obtain the expected relaxation formula.
Projective planes with abelian collineation groups of type (F) are Desarguesian

We use prime ideal factorization and residue class fields of cyclotomic integer rings to prove that every abelian direct product difference set is classical. This implies that every projective plane of order $n$ with an abelian collineation group of order $n(n-1)$ is Desarguesian, proving a conjecture of Jungnickel and de Resmini. As a consequence, we obtain the classification of circular Costas maps and of Costas polynomials conjectured by Muratovic-Ribic, Pott, Thomson and Wang and by Torres and Rubio.
Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states

Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,\varphi)$ has a unique equilibrium state $μ$ and $μ(f)=0$. The system $(T,μ)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for Hölder observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem. The main results have been formalised in Lean 4.
Global bound-state spectrum and spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement in an inverse-$3/2$ magnetic quantum dot

We investigate the bound-state spectrum and confinement thresholds of a two-dimensional electron governed by the Schrödinger--Pauli equation in an inverse-$3/2$ radial magnetic-field profile. The radial problem reduces to the biconfluent Heun equation, but instead of restricting the solution to the quasi-exact polynomial sector, we impose the bound-state condition globally through a spectral Wronskian between the endpoint-selected Frobenius solution and the subdominant asymptotic solution. The resulting spectrum contains continuous nonpolynomial bound-state branches on which the known quasi-exact solutions appear as isolated exact points. In this global description, the polynomial index $N$ remains a termination index within the quasi-exact sector but does not uniquely label the spectral branches. An independent exact analysis of the continuum edge yields spin- and angular-momentum-dependent critical couplings that can lie below the quasi-exact restriction $U_0a>4$, where $U_0$ is the Coulomb-strength parameter and $a$ is the magnetic-profile length scale. These results establish quasi-exact solvability as a set of special analytic points embedded in a broader biconfluent-Heun spectrum with spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement thresholds.
Discriminants and resultants of orthogonal polynomials
Mourad E. H. Ismail; Jihyeug Jang; Jang Soo Kim; Dennis Stanton

The concept of a linked pair of two sequences of polynomials, one of which is orthogonal, is introduced. Such a pair always has a resultant that factors. Two methods for producing such linked pairs are given: one for general orthogonal polynomials and the other for any polynomial in the Askey scheme. Generalized discriminants are introduced and evaluated, including a general product formula for each operator in the Askey scheme. A new notion of companion orthogonal polynomials is also introduced and used to evaluate the discriminants of orthogonal polynomials. These methods recover all known formulas for the generalized discriminants of classical polynomials and provide new ones.
Jim Geelen; Bert Gerards; Geoff Whittle

We prove that, if $X$ is a four-element independent set in a vertically $5$-connected representable matroid $M$, then either there is a circuit of $M$ that contains at least three elements of $X$, or there is a representation $A$ of $M$ such that each column of $A$ has at most two non-zero elements and each of the columns indexed by $X$ has exactly one non-zero element. We also prove a version of this result without the connectivity assumptions.
Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling
Yixuan Ma; Weikang Li; Dong-Ling Deng

Scrambling, the process by which initially localized quantum information spreads across an interacting many-body system, is a hallmark of quantum chaos and plays a central role in understanding black hole dynamics. In thermal systems, the chaos bound of Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford limits the exponential growth rate of out-of-time-order correlations to $2π/β$, assuming that time-ordered correlation functions factorize after a dissipation time. Establishing the corresponding rigorous logarithmic lower bounds on scrambling times at arbitrary fixed temperature has remained an open problem, most notably in disordered systems, where the Gibbs state depends on the same random couplings that drive the dynamics. Here we prove such bounds at every fixed temperature for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and for random $k$-local spin systems, without assuming real-time factorization. Our approach uses the operator-size distribution of the square root of the Gibbs state to quantify how local probes modify its structure. This static information bounds the thermal correlator uniformly in time along the edges of its analytic strip in complex time, and analyticity then limits how rapidly scrambling can develop. For both families of models, we prove that with probability tending to one the scrambling time is at least $(1-ε)[β/(2π)]\log N$ for any $0<ε<1$, with the coefficient $β/(2π)$ suggested by the chaos bound. The bound holds for each fixed pair of distinct Majorana modes in the SYK model and for the target average of any fixed single-site source in the spin model. These results place the thermal fast-scrambling timescale on a rigorous footing and show how static properties of the Gibbs state can constrain real-time information spreading.
Branch-and-Cut for Maximum $k$-Independent Sets with Spectral Bounds
Aida Abiad; Julian Golak; Arne Schulz

We develop a branch-and-cut method for finding maximum distance-independent sets in graphs. Our approach solves a sequence of fixed-size clique problems, combining graph reductions with combinatorial and spectral bounds. We give a compact formulation, derive strengthened inequalities, establish conditions for using spectral information, and evaluate them in a comprehensive computational study.
A Convergence Analysis of the Random Feature Method for Linear PDEs
Jingrun Chen; Yixin Luo; Xiaojun Peng

The Random Feature Method (RFM) distinguishes itself among machine learning approaches to partial differential equations (PDEs) through its superior accuracy and computational efficiency. Nevertheless, the theoretical underpinnings of RFM remain incompletely elucidated. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of RFM within the framework of kernel methods, focusing on two principal aspects: (i) approximation by finitely many random features in Sobolev norms and the PDE residual seminorm, and (ii) estimation over the induced reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) from finitely many noiseless collocation observations. We relate both problems to kernel ridge regression (KRR) and establish upper and lower bounds in terms of the eigenvalues of the associated integral operators under the respective assumptions. Combining the approximation and estimation lower bounds, we establish a lower bound under simultaneous restrictions on the numbers of random features and collocation observations. We further quantify how activation regularity affects these eigenvalues, obtaining algebraic upper bounds for finitely smooth activations and stretched-exponential upper bounds for analytic activations.

A circular-arc graph takes a set of nonempty closed arcs on a circle as its vertex set, and two vertices are adjacent when their corresponding arcs intersect on the circle. We show the chromatic number of any circular-arc graph equals its list chromatic number. Our methodology is an application of Schauz's coefficient formula within the Alon-Tarsi and Combinatorial Nullstellensatz framework.
Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism

The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.
Vanishing geodesic distance phenomenon and boundedness of curvatures

This article concerns a conjecture proposed by Michor and Mumford in their 2005 paper, in which the vanishing of the geodesic distance is associated to the local unboundedness of the sectional curvature. In this article, we consider a Riemannian Banach manifold with all of its curvature tensors locally bounded. We derive several properties regarding the local boundedness of curvature tensors, and give a sufficient condition for a non-degenerate geodesic distance, which partially verifies the conjecture in its converse form.
Convergence rates of moment--SOS hierarchies with correlative sparsity via gluing and projection

This paper studies convergence rates of moment--SOS hierarchies with correlative sparsity. Following the method proposed in~\cite{tran}, we bound the Hausdorff distance between the set of sparse truncated moment sequences and sparse truncated pseudo-moment sequences. The central step is a quantitative gluing lemma on a clique tree: local moment errors and separator discrepancies in total variation control the error of a joint approximating measure. Over hypercube, polynomial kernels give the convergence rates $O((\log_2r)^3/r^2)$ for the correlative sparse quadratic module and $O(r^{-2})$ for the correlative sparse preordering, where the certificate degree is $2r$. On compact basic semialgebraic sets, slack variable lifting and global atom projection yield $O((\log_2r)^{3\Lo/2}/r^{\Lo})$ and $O(r^{-\Lo})$ with a Łojasiewicz exponent $0<\Lo \le1$. These bounds hold for fixed-degree Hausdorff distances and polynomial objective gaps. We also extend to result to the correlative sparse quadratic-module rate for scalar objectives with clique-local polynomial matrix constraints.
Affine pairs of minimizing units in totally real non-Galois cubic fields

Let $Γ$ be a rank-two subgroup of the integral norm-one units in a totally real non-Galois cubic field. We prove that two distinct affinely equivalent minima of Godwin's spread on $Γ\setminus\{1\}$ generate $Γ$ and determine its complete minimum set: a pair with sum $\pm2$ or a triple of integral translates of product one. Every minimum generates the order $\mathbb{Z}[Γ]$. For an order whose norm-one units have such a pair, the order generated by its units is the smallest suborder with the same minimum value. We also give explicit families and a maximal order with minima in two distinct affine classes.
Advancing Cognitive Pairwise Comparisons for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework

Human-centric artificial intelligence and data science (HCAD) systems increasingly involve human-in-the-loop (HITL) interventions to overcome the limitations of fully automated machine learning algorithms, such as automation bias and the inability to incorporate tacit domain knowledge, and continuously improve predictive performance. Data transformations, feature selection, feature weighting, and model selection usually require laborious human involvement across iterations of artificial intelligence and data science (AI&DS) pipelines, making development a challenging and time-consuming process. The Cognitive Pairwise Comparison (CPC) framework is proposed as a human-centric methodology to elicit preferences and priorities in a structured format. To establish essential facets of human-centricity, this research advances the CPC methodology so that user preference elicitation can be systematically quantified in these challenging AI&DS tasks. To demonstrate the usability and validity of these facets, this study presents several applications within movie recommender systems using the MovieLens dataset. It exemplifies how the extended CPC framework can facilitate interactions between human judgments and data across supervised learning, dimensionality reduction, and unsupervised learning algorithms.

We introduce Eckmann-Hilton operators on bands, which allow for a suite of matroidal constructions, in particular, matroid unions and matroid stable intersections. This enables the construction of general linear monoids over bands. Geometrically, we show that matroid stable intersection extends the transverse intersection of linear spaces over fields and the stable intersection of tropical linear spaces, lending new insight into intersection theory on bands.

Jamming is a major threat to space telemetry downlinks, which operate under severe power and bandwidth constraints. For pulsed jamming with jamming state information (JSI) at the receiver, we derive a two-state protograph-based extrinsic information transfer (PEXIT) recursion that tracks the messages originating from clean and jammed symbols separately and merges them at the check nodes through a mutual-information-matched Gaussian approximation. We develop an algebraic framework for homogeneous metric flows with closed three-form flux on reductive homogeneous spaces. The geometric data are encoded by the complete reductive bracket $μ$ on $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak k\oplus\mathfrak m$, while the flux is treated as an additional invariant datum $H$ satisfying $d_μH=0$. For the metric equation \[ \partial_tg =
-2\operatorname{Ric}_g +
\frac12\mathcal K_{g,H}, \] we derive the corresponding bracket evolution \[ \dotμ=
-π(P_{μ,H})μ, \qquad P_{μ,H} =
\operatorname{Ric}_μ^{\sharp} -
\frac14\mathcal K_{μ,H}^{\sharp}. \]

For a prescribed closed invariant three-form, we compute explicitly the quadratic flux operator, the induced three-parameter metric system, and the evolution of the transported bracket coefficients. Noise-induced manifolds: reduction of slow--fast SDEs to switching processes
Jeremy R. Worsfold; Patrick Ryan; Richard G. Morris

When constituents copy one another, as in reaction networks, collective behaviour and opinion dynamics, the noise of copying vanishes at consensus and can make a system bistable. More generally this noise vanishes on whole manifolds, along which slower variables keep moving and set the switching rates, yet no general method derives these switching dynamics. Here we reduce slow--fast stochastic differential equations whose fast noise acts in a single direction to a switching diffusion or piecewise-deterministic Markov process (PDMP), using the absorption probabilities of the fast noise in place of an invariant measure, and derive a first-order correction for the finite duration of switches. For the two-species Togashi--Kaneko model the reduction recovers our earlier PDMP, and the correction captures how the stationary composition depends on the timescale separation. In a model of foraging ants with a depleting food source, the hazard of leaving a source rises through every stay, which makes the colony unlikely to leave a source soon after arriving there.
Sharp Fourier Extension Inequalities on $ \mathbb{S}^2 $ for All $q>4$

For the ordinary Fourier extension operator on $\mathbb S^2$, we determine the optimal $L^2(\mathbb S^2)\to L^q(\mathbb R^3)$ constant for every real $q>4$, and characterize the nonzero complex extremizers. The result extends the sharp quartic theorem of Foschi and the even-exponent results of Oliveira e Silva--Quilodrán to exponents for which the usual convolution identities are unavailable. The proof has two stages. A continuous inequality for the moments of $\sin r/r$, combined with a trace estimate along the symmetry orbit of a maximizer, reduces the problem to $4\leq q\leq6$. On this interval, the second variation imposes a scalar necessary condition. We contradict it by spectral estimates for spherical harmonics, moment comparisons, and, near $q=4$, a quantitative use of the quartic deficit. The resulting constant is attained exactly by scalar multiples of characters.
A note on finite length for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
Andrea Dotto; Daniel Le; Bao Viet Le Hung; Stefano Morra

Let $p>2$ be a prime and $F/\mathbf{Q}_p$ be a finite extension. We prove that every admissible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, with a central character, and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition, has finite length.
Parameter Recovery for the Modified Leray-alpha Model via Continuous Data Assimilation
Débora A. F. Albanez; Maicon J. Benvenutti; Jing Tian

In this study, we extend the recursive length-scale recovery method for the simplified Bardina model to the three-dimensional modified Leray-alpha model. The main difficulty is that the unknown parameter also occurs in the nonlinear convection term, so estimating the error in the parameter update requires control of second spatial derivatives of the velocity error. We combine continuous data assimilation with a recursive update of the squared length scale, using observed low Fourier modes and computed high Fourier modes. Under uniform regularity bounds on the reference solution and suitable conditions on the observations and the recovery procedure, we prove geometric convergence of both the parameter and velocity errors at the update times. When the update-window lengths are uniformly bounded, this convergence is exponential in time at the update times.
Resurgent Analysis of the Single-Orbit Term in the Selberg Trace Formula

We study the large-time asymptotic expansion, the Borel-Laplace transforms and the Stokes phenomenon of the single-orbit term in the Selberg trace formula. By a single-orbit term we mean the contribution from a primitive closed geodesic orbit and its iterations on a compact hyperbolic surface, and its formal large-time expansion is divergent. We prove that the divergent formal series is uniformly $1$-Gevrey asymptotic to the convergent single-orbit term and recover the single-orbit term by a Laplace integral along the positive real axis. Other directions for the Laplace integration are also explored by analyzing the singularities of the Borel transform of this $1$-Gevrey formal series. It turns out that the series obtained by Borel transform is meromorphic on the two-sheeted Riemann surface of $\sqrtξ$, with simple poles corresponding to the resonance spectra of the hyperbolic cylinder. The Laplace transform can be performed along almost every direction on the two-sheeted Riemann surface. Finally, the Stokes structure as the limit of the difference between Laplace integrals along different directions can be computed by a convergent sum of the exponential of resonance spectrum. These results demonstrate the phenomenon that the resurgent structure of a single-orbit term in the Selberg trace formula is reflected by its associated cylinder resonance spectra.
Quantitative approximation for Fourier neural operators in controlled ordinary differential equations
Dean Zenner; Andreas Rupp; Thomas Schuster

Fourier neural operators (FNOs) avoid the curse of parametric complexity when approximating the solution operator of certain partial differential equations (PDEs). While recent studies primarily focus on PDEs, in this article we derive upper error bounds for approximating the solution operator of controlled ordinary differential equations (CODEs) $\dot{y}=f(y,u)$ using a FNO. Under a Carathéodory setting and suitable regularity assumptions, including a smallness condition, we prove that the size of the FNO grows at most algebraically in $1/\varepsilon$, namely like $\varepsilon^{-(1+d/(2(s-1)))}$ up to logarithmic factors for GELU networks, and is thus sub-quadratic for sufficiently smooth $f$, where $d=1+n_y+n_u$ and $s$ denotes the Sobolev regularity of $f$. Our proof is based on emulating the Picard iteration through the layers of the FNO while exploiting the differentiation formula of the discrete Fourier transform. This result contributes to the quantitative approximation theory of FNOs for physically motivated problems and provides a theoretical foundation for leveraging a FNO as efficient forward surrogate for the solution operator of CODEs, especially in inverse parameter estimation where repeated evaluations of the forward operator are needed.
Entropy and frame measures for self-affine measures

Let $M$ be a real expanding $d\times d$ matrix and let $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\R^d$ consist of $N\ge2$ distinct vectors. We study the existence of frame measures for the self-affine probability measure $μ$ generated by the maps $S_i(x)=M^{-1}(x+d_i)$ with equal weights $1/N$. Extending the entropy obstruction for self-similar measures with a common scalar contraction, we prove that $μ$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy of the first symbol given the spatial point is positive. In particular, this holds whenever $N>|\det M|$, without assuming absolute continuity or imposing arithmetic conditions. When $M$ has integer entries, $\mathscr D\subset\Z^d$, and $N=|\det M|$, the measure $μ$ admits a frame measure if and only if $μ$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor.
Positive Regulation of an Axial Dispersion Tubular Reactor by Optimal Boundary Feedback Control

The dynamics of the reactant in an isothermal axial dispersion tubular reactor is considered. Our goal consists in designing the inlet reactant concentration, under the form of a state feedback law, in order to modify the state behavior according to relevant process requirements, while keeping the positivity and stability properties of the uncontrolled dynamics. The designed control is also constrained to be positive to respect physical requirements. First, we state and analytically solve a parameterized optimal feedback design problem. Next, we address a positive observer-based feedback stabilization problem. The results are illustrated by means of numerical simulations.
Sobolev regularity for nondivergence form nonlocal equations with irregular kernels

We consider the nonlocal elliptic equation $L_Ku-λu=f$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $L_K$ is a nondivergence form operator of order $σ\in(0,2)$ with kernel $K(x,y)$. We assume that $K(x,y)$ is Dini continuous in $x$ uniformly in $y$ and merely measurable in $y$. Under the usual upper bound assumption, we prove the boundedness of $L_K$ from $H_p^σ(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for any $p\in(1,\infty)$. We also establish maximal $L_p$-regularity and unique solvability for all sufficiently large $λ$, provided that an additional nondegeneracy condition holds. We further extend these results to weighted spaces with arbitrary Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights and obtain estimates that are robust as $σ\to2$. We also construct a kernel that is jointly uniformly continuous in $(x,y)$, for which both operator boundedness and the maximal regularity estimate fail. This is in sharp contrast to the classical $W_p^2$ theory for second-order elliptic equations in nondivergence form, which allows VMO coefficients.
A simple solvable $Z_N$ Hamiltonian in any dimension

We construct local $Z_N$ clock Hamiltonians from Baxter-Fendley chains coupled according to an arbitrary finite oriented simple transverse graph. Bounded edge lengths and vertex degrees give finite-range multispin interactions, with $2d$-site bulk terms on a $d$-dimensional rectangular lattice. For open longitudinal boundaries, an explicit nonlocal unitary transformation decouples the chains and gives a free parafermion spectrum. On rectangular lattices this holds for any combination of open and periodic transverse boundaries. For periodic longitudinal boundaries, neighbouring chain charges fix the closing-bond twists. In each joint charge sector, the energies are sums of the corresponding twisted periodic-chain energies. As an example, we construct a three-dimensional array of chains perpendicular to a Penrose rhombus tiling.
On Hamilton-Jacobi equations and perceptron models

The solution to a finite-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi equation is classically known to admit a variational representation in two situations: when the nonlinearity is convex or concave, by the Hopf-Lax formula; and when the initial condition is convex or concave, by the Hopf formula. We identify a third situation: the space variable is split into two groups of coordinates, the nonlinearity is the scalar product of the two corresponding partial gradients, and the initial condition is the sum of a convex function of the first group of coordinates and of an arbitrary Lipschitz function of the second group. This structure is precisely that of the Hamilton-Jacobi equations describing the limit free energy of perceptron models. We illustrate this point by identifying the limit free energy of a class of perceptron models that can be rewritten as bipartite spin glasses, with Ising spins in one layer and bounded soft spins in the other. We also discuss how to extend the approach to several other classes of models, including general Ising and spherical perceptrons, possibly with labelled patterns.
Practical Semantic Communication for General-Purpose Networks: Compression of High-Dimensional Embeddings Under Quantization
Leonardo Roque; Louis-Adrien Dufrène; Quentin Lampin; Grégoire Lefebvre; Mohamad Assaad

This paper introduces a practical framework for semantic communication over wireless channels, focusing on the compression of high-dimensional embeddings under quantization and channel errors. Building upon a relaxed Gaussian Information Bottleneck (GIB) model, the approach provides analytical solutions for task-relevant information preservation, even with non-Gaussian targets. The framework relaxes traditional Gaussian assumptions, enabling effective compression for discrete and complex data such as text embeddings. It derives closed-form gradients for optimizing the compression matrix and establishes bounds linking continuous representations to discrete, noisy system performance. Comprehensive experiments on text classification tasks demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms task-agnostic quantization-based compression methods, maintaining high semantic fidelity at low bit budgets per embedding. The approach offers a scalable, interpretable, and resource-efficient solution for deploying semantic communication in general-purpose networks.
Unconditionally Positive Nonstandard Finite Difference Schemes for $p$-Laplacian Reaction--Diffusion Equations
Achraf Zinihi; Matthias Ehrhardt; Moulay Rchid Sidi Ammi

We propose a conservative, semi-implicit nonstandard finite difference scheme for the reaction--diffusion equation $u_t=λ(|u_x|^{p-2}u_x)_x+f(u)$, $p>1$, where, as is customary, the $p$-Laplacian is regularized by a parameter $\eps>0$. The scheme combines a denominator function, a lagged diffusion coefficient, and a nonlocal treatment of the loss part of the reaction. For every time step and mesh size we prove that the scheme is well posed and positive, that it preserves an invariant region $[0,K]$ whenever the reaction admits one, and that it reproduces every constant equilibrium exactly. Without reaction, it conserves mass, satisfies a discrete maximum principle, and, for $1<p\le 2$, decreases a discrete energy. An example shows that the energy may increase for $p>2$. The truncation error is $O(k+h^2)$ at interior nodes. Numerical tests confirm first order in time and second order in space, and show that the scheme remains positive and bounded for step sizes at which the explicit method breaks down.
Well posedness of the MHS equation with Grad Rubin boundary conditions near a dipolar field in an exterior domain
Daniel Sánchez-Simón del Pino; Juan J. L. Velázquez

In this article we study the well posedness of the MHS system in the exterior of a disk. We investigate the case of Grad and Rubin boundary conditions and obtain solutions by perturbing around the dipolar magnetic field. Unlike prior work in the case of bounded domains, we show that one needs to impose a "codimension four"-type condition on the boundary data in order to obtain solutions. Furthermore, due to the tangency points that appear in this situation, we need to develop a careful analysis of the solutions around these points.
The exact semisimplicity criterion for Brauer algebras of type $C$

We determine exactly when the Brauer algebra of type $C$, denoted by $\B_r(C,δ)$, is semisimple over $\C$, where $δ\neq0$. We first analyze the two admissible cases for homomorphisms from the top layer to the second layer. We construct an auxiliary operator on the space spanned by symmetric Brauer diagrams with a fixed bottom partial diagram and exactly two horizontal edges in each row. Using this operator, we prove that, in each admissible case, the corresponding quadratic condition is necessary and sufficient for the existence of a nonzero homomorphism. The constant terms of these quadratic expressions depend on sums of contents of horizontal $2$-strips in bipartitions. We then show that a failure of semisimplicity is detected by cell modules in the second layer. Finally, by relating the content sums for admissible bipartition pairs to the known sums for horizontal $2$-strips in ordinary partitions, we obtain an explicit finite set of exceptional nonzero parameters.
Variational Estimates for the Bilinear Hilbert Transform

We prove that for every $q>2$, the $q$-variation operator associated with the bilinear Hilbert transform is bounded from $L^r(\mathbb R)\times L^s(\mathbb R)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R)$ whenever $1<r,s<\infty$, $p>2/3$, and $1/p=1/r+1/s$.
Constructing high-dimensional representations of twin groups via several techniques

In this article, we consider the twin group $T_n$ for a positive integer $n$ and present two techniques for constructing high-dimensional and complicated representations of $T_n$. The first technique consists of composing a known representation of $T_n$ with the well-established Cohen map, while the second technique relies on the tensor product of two known representations of $T_n$. To implement these techniques, we consider the two representations $η_1$ and $η_2$ of $T_n$ introduced recently by Nasser. The first technique is applied to the representation $η_1: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{F}_n)$, which maps $T_n$ into the automorphism group of the free group $\mathbb{F}_n$ with $n$ generators. The second technique is applied to the representation $η_2: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}])$, which maps $T_n$ into the general linear group over the ring of Laurent polynomials in an indeterminate $t$. Using these techniques, we construct new high-degree representations of $T_n$ and examine, for some of them, structural properties such as faithfulness and reducibility. This work provides new avenues for developing representations of $T_n$ and related groups using these techniques.
The Göttsche conjecture and the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula

The aim of these notes is to give an account, intended for the non-specialist, of the two proofs of the Göttsche conjecture given, respectively, first by Tzeng, and shortly after by Kool, Shende and Thomas.
 Given a smooth, complex, projective surface $S$ and a positive integer $δ$, the Göttsche conjecture predicts that if $L$ is a sufficiently positive line bundle on $S$, then the number of $δ$-nodal curves in a general $δ$-dimensional linear subsystem $Λ\subset |L|$ is given by a universal polynomial of degree $δ$ in the four numbers $L^2$, $L K_S$, $K_S^2$, and $c_2(S)$.
 Besides, the Göttsche--Yau--Zaslow formula expresses the generating function of the aforementioned numbers of $δ$-nodal curves in terms of three explicit quasimodular forms and two unknown universal power series, whose coefficients can be determined by recursion.
Characterization of Cubic Graphs with Exactly Two Lonely Edges

Perfect matchings are fundamental to understanding structural connectivity in cubic graphs, with "lonely edges" (edges in exactly one perfect matching) forming a critical underexplored class. Goedgebeur et al. (J. Graph Theory, 112 (2026) 276-289) established an upper bound of 6 on the number of lonely edges in 3-connected non-double covered cubic graphs and completely characterized the classes $\mathcal{U}_k$ for $3 \le k \le 6$. Narayana et al. subsequently gave a recursive characterization of the subclass in which the two lonely edges lie in the same perfect matching. This paper completes the classification by presenting a full structural characterization of $\mathcal{U}_2$, the family of 3-connected cubic graphs with exactly two lonely edges. We identify the minimally non-contractible "primitive kernels" of $\mathcal{U}_2$ and develop constructive operations to generate any graph in $\mathcal{U}_2$ from these kernels.
Singular limits of the subelliptic Allen-Cahn equation and geometric flows

This paper investigates the singular limits of a bistable reaction-diffusion equation in a subelliptic setting, where the standard Euclidean diffusion is replaced by a subelliptic operator defined by a family of vector fields. We introduce a Riemannian approximation of these vector fields to regularize the problem, yielding a uniformly parabolic equation whose ellipticity degenerates as the singular parameter vanishes.
 We prove that the family of solutions converges globally in time to the stable equilibria away from a propagating interface. Our approach uses the definition of generalized geometric flow developed by Barles--Souganidis, uniquely defined through the level-set equation and viscosity solutions. The behavior of the interface depends on the traveling wave speed c: when c is not 0, the front propagates with constant normal velocity governed by a first-order subelliptic eikonal equation.
 When c = 0, the front evolves according to the horizontal mean curvature flow equation defined by the original vector fields. At present, this case comes with limitations: it requires a more restrictive condition on test functions at characteristic points to define generalized flows, where the horizontal gradient vanishes and standard arguments break down. This framework relies on our earlier work, where the equivalence between the generalized flow and the level-set approach was established when the vector fields generate a step-two Carnot group. We also assume that the comparison principle holds for the level-set equation in order for the level-set approach to be well-posed.
Stochastic Modelling of High-frequency (HF) Crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with General Compound Marked Hawkes Process
Mine Caglar; Serhat Guldogan; Anatoliy Swishchuk

The paper is devoted to the stochastic modelling of high-frequency crypto Limit Order Book (LOB) with general compound marked Hawkes process (GCMHP). We consider marked Hawkes process in a general form. LLN and FCLTs with stochastic and constant centralization are stated. Numerical example for high-frequency LOB dataset for BTC (bitcoin) based on sources from HF crypto LOB data is presented as well. The novelty of the paper lies in the new LLN and FCLTs for the GCMHP, and in the new application associated with high-frequency (HF) crypto LOB.
Maximum principle preserving approximation of scalar conservation equations with a fractional Laplacian
Andrea Bonito; Jean-Luc Guermond; Murtazo Nazarov

In this paper, we propose a maximum principle preserving continuous finite element method for scalar conservation laws augmented with a fractional diffusion operator of order $s\in (0,1)$. Conservation laws with fractional diffusion operators arise in a variety of physical models involving anomalous transport and nonlocal regularization, including geophysical flows, plasma physics, and nonlinear acoustics. The fractional Laplacian is approximated using a sinc-quadrature representation, yielding a resolvent-based formulation compatible with continuous finite elements and explicit strong stability preserving Runge--Kutta time integration. A first-order monotone scheme is constructed using graph viscosity and is shown to satisfy a discrete maximum principle under an explicit CFL condition. A high-order extension is obtained via entropy-consistent corrections and convex limiting, achieving second-order accuracy while preserving the maximum principle, and hence positivity, as well as mass conservation in the periodic setting. Numerical experiments, including applications to the Surface Quasi-Geostrophic equation, confirm the second-order accuracy and the robustness of the proposed method on unstructured meshes.
Creation Sequences for Numerical Semigroups and Exact Counts of Semigroup Partitions

A numerical semigroup is a subset of the non-negative integers that contains $0$, is closed under addition and has finite complement. A threshold graph is built by adding vertices one at a time, each new vertex being isolated or dominating, and the record of these choices is its \emph{creation sequence}. Reading the creation sequence as a lattice path gives an integer partition and, through the Keith--Nath correspondence, a numerical set in which the dominating vertices are the elements and the isolated vertices are the gaps. We show that threshold graphs with an isolated vertex correspond bijectively to numerical sets, and we study numerical semigroups through their creation sequences. We prove that in the creation sequence of a numerical semigroup of multiplicity $m$ every block of ones and every non-initial block of zeros has length less than $m$, we give criteria for partitions with a unique smallest part and with two distinct part sizes, and we classify all partitions with at most four parts. We show that every partition $λ$ with $g$ parts corresponding to a numerical semigroup satisfies $\ell(λ)\geλ_1$ and, more strongly, fits inside the staircase $(g,g-1,\dots,1)$; equivalently, its creation sequence begins with a Dyck path. Its size equals the genus plus the Weierstrass weight of the semigroup, and asymptotically at most half of all partitions correspond to numerical semigroups. Finally, we obtain exact formulas for the numbers of partitions of $n$ corresponding to numerical semigroups of genus $g$, multiplicity $m$ and Frobenius number $f$, valid in the sharp ranges $g\ge n/2$, $m>n/3$ and $f\ge n-\frac{n-1}{4}$. These formulas solve the open problems posed by Burson, Nam and Sisneros-Thiry \cite{BNS}, recover all of their counting theorems, and correct several of their statements.
Optimal Importance Sampling Densities for Estimating Several Expectations at Once

Simulation studies often estimate several quantities from a single sample, and the best importance sampling density depends on how the errors on these quantities are combined. We characterise the optimal auxiliary density for a general error criterion. We show that it is the nominal density reweighted by a weighted length of the vector of estimated functions, where the weights are set by the error criterion, or by the curvature of the loss when the criterion comes from a loss on the errors. We also provide a lower bound on the best achievable error. The optimal density is explicit for smooth losses, including the usual losses on covariance matrices. We also derive allocation laws for the cells of a histogram and characterise the minimax density for the probabilities of several events. When there is no closed form, we show how to compute the optimal density numerically.
On the volume of amoebas of complete intersections

We study the $2k$-dimensional volume of the amoeba of a smooth complete intersection $V$ of dimension $k$ in $(\C^*)^n$, $n\ge2k$, with Newton polytopes $Δ_1,\dots,Δ_{n-k}$. For $n=2k$ we prove $\Vol(\A(V))\ge\mathcal M(V)/\MV(Δ_1,\dots,Δ_k,-Δ_1,\dots,-Δ_k)$, where $\mathcal M(V)$ is the coamoeba volume counted with multiplicity, and we show $\mathcal M(V)\geπ^{2k}$ for plane curves ($k=1$, $n=2$) whose Newton polygon is not centrally symmetric, for nondegenerate varieties with odd $\MV(Δ_1,\dots,Δ_k,Δ_1,\dots,Δ_k)$, and for smooth towers of curve fibrations. We determine the equality case for curves and towers, and prove that $k$-planes in general position never attain the bound. For $n>2k$ we prove two-sided bounds for $\Hm^{2k}(\A(V))$ through coordinate projections, and show that for generic coefficients almost every fibre of the amoeba map is an orbit of a finite group. For lines we prove that in several random models the area of the amoeba of a line in $(\C^*)^n$ is asymptotic to $\frac\pi2n\log n$, and we compute its limit under degenerations of the configuration. Finally we characterise the varieties attaining the extremal volumes. For $n=2k$ every regular fibre of the amoeba map has an even number of points, divisible by $4$ for real varieties with $k\ge2$; the volume-maximal varieties are those with two-to-one amoeba maps and maximal rolled coamoebas, and they are never real when $k\ge2$; a volume-minimal plane curve is characterised by a group of symmetries of maximal order, and its amoeba has no holes. For $n>2k$ the extremal varieties lie in translates of $2k$-dimensional subtori.
A conic optimization framework for shape-constrained functional regression analysis
María Durbán; Vanesa Guerrero; Cristina Molero-Río

Standard regression methods do not always guarantee that the estimated model reflects prior knowledge about how predictors relate to the response, which motivates constrained regression. When the effects to be estimated are smooth nonlinear functions, a natural family of constraints is that of shape constraints, such as sign, monotonicity, or curvature, which encode qualitative properties that these functions are often expected to satisfy. While shape-constrained estimation of smooth functions is well established in classical regression with scalar covariates and response, its extension to functional regression, where the coefficients are themselves functions, remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose the functional shape-constrained conic P-spline estimator (FunSCOPE), a unified framework for shape-constrained functional linear regression that covers scalar-on-function, function-on-scalar, and function-on-function models, and in which any combination of the shapes above can be imposed on the functional regression coefficient. Building on a P-spline approach, the desired shapes are expressed as conditions on the scalar regression coefficients, which leads to an estimation problem formulated as a conic optimization problem. For univariate coefficients, as in scalar-on-function, function-on-scalar, and a particular case of the function-on-function regression, the concurrent case, these conditions are both necessary and sufficient, in contrast to existing approaches, which provide only sufficient conditions; for bivariate coefficients, as in general function-on-function models, they are neither necessary nor sufficient. Numerical experiments show that FunSCOPE outperforms competing methods in terms of estimation error and computational time.
Network-Native DNN Architecture Synthesis for Distributed Inference
Fan Yang; Xiaolong Wu; Qi Cao; Fen Hou; Yulin Shao

Distributed deep neural network (DNN) inference typically follows a model-first paradigm, in which a predefined DNN is partitioned and deployed over a physical network. On irregular communication-computation topologies, however, this approach can create transmission bottlenecks and leave distributed resources underutilized. This paper reverses this perspective and asks: given a physical network, what kind of DNN can it naturally support? To answer this question, we propose a network-native DNN architecture synthesis paradigm in which the physical network topology directly defines inter-node neural dependencies. Neural computation is allocated across nodes under communication, computation, storage, synchronization, and latency constraints. We establish structural properties of the synthesis problem and develop linear programming (LP)-based Architecture Synthesis (LPAS), an efficient topology-guided algorithm that produces a feasible architecture with a computable bound on suboptimality. Experiments on physical networks of different sizes show that LPAS achieves relative gaps below 0.6% to the LP-derived upper bound, with substantially lower runtime than direct mixed-integer LP optimization on larger networks. Under matched network deadlines, the network-native architectures activate more compute nodes and utilize a larger proportion of available model-storage capacity than the model-first baseline. After training, the network-native models achieve higher classification accuracy across all evaluated dataset-precision settings, with the average gain of up to 10.69%. This network-native design paradigm thus turns the physical network from a deployment constraint into an architecture design primitive.
Collapsibility of Vietoris--Rips complexes of hypercube graphs in codimension two

Shukla conjectured that the collapsibility number of the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph at scale $r$ equals $2^r$ for all $n\ge r+1$. We prove the conjecture for $n=r+2$ and every $r$, which gives the first known cases with $r\ge 4$ beyond the cross-polytope case $n=r+1$. Writing $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ as the independence complex of the graph $H_{n,r}$ that joins two points when their Hamming distance exceeds $r$, we construct a cover of $H_{r+2,r}$ by $2^r$ co-chordal subgraphs. The key general tool is the inequality that, for every graph $G$, the $θ$-number of Bıyıkoğlu and Civan of the independence complex of $G$, and hence the collapsibility number of that complex, is at most the co-chordal cover number of $G$; this strengthens Woodroofe's regularity bound. We also show, using a theorem of Alon, Jin, and Sudakov, that the induced matching number of $H_{n,r}$ equals $2^r$ for every $n>r$, and that $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $r=1$ or $n=r+1$. As consequences, we determine the top degree of nonvanishing homology and the coconnectivity of $\mathrm{VR}(I_{r+2};r)$, and we prove split injectivity in top-degree integral homology. Finally, assuming a recent skew Hamming set-pair theorem of Gao and Zhao, we prove that the collapsibility number of $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is at most $2^{r+1}-4$ for all $n>r\ge 2$.
Criterion for Glasner property and IC-Rigidity for actions on homogeneous space

Let $G$ be a semi-group acting continuously on a compact metric space $X$. The action $G\curvearrowright X$ is called Glasner if for every infinite set $A\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $g\in G$ such that $gA$ is $\varepsilon$-dense in $X$. Let $\mathcal{K}(X)$ denote the space of nonempty compact subsets of $X$. A $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{K}(X)$ is called an invariant random compact (IRC), and the action is IC-rigid if $δ_X$ is the only IRC supported on infinite compact subsets of $X$. In this paper we give a pair-correlation criterion implying both IC-rigidity and the Glasner property. As an application, we prove both these properties for finitely generated $\operatorname{Ad}$-Zariski-dense semi-groups acting on compact homogeneous spaces $G/Λ$, where $G$ is connected and noncompact with simple Lie algebra and $Λ<G$ is a cocompact lattice; in particular, this applies to finitely generated Zariski-dense semi-groups of $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. We also derive a Fourier-analytic criterion for semi-group actions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and use it to prove IC-rigidity for actions arising from suitable matrix-valued polynomials.
Non-stationary motion of an inextensible closed string

We consider a non-stationary motion of an inextensible closed string. The motion of the string is governed by nonlinear and nonlocal hyperbolic equations. The nonlocality of the equations is caused by the unknown tension of the string and reflects the inextensibility of the string. We show that the initial value problem to the equations of motion is well-posed locally in time. In the proof, it is crucial to show a strict positivity of the tension when the string is in motion. To this end, we derive a sharp lower bound of the Green's function for a periodic boundary value problem. We also derive a blow-up criterion of smooth solutions, which states that any singularities on the velocity or on the tension of the string do not take place before a curvature singularity appears.
A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ over the Unit Quaternions

We extend the recursive construction of perfect and odd perfect sequences over the simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ of Blake to arrays of any dimension. The three operations of that construction act on one direction of an array at a time, and are valid whenever the array is periodic in the remaining directions. Starting from a perfect array $P$ of shape $M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ they give perfect arrays of shape $2^a\times M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ for every $a\ge0$, with explicit index functions and with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$ in the lifted direction; from $a=5$ on these arrays are, in general, Kronecker products of a sequence with $P$ in neither order. Applied direction by direction, the construction gives perfect arrays over $\Qe$ in every shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$, and in every shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_{d-1}}\times N$ for which a perfect sequence of length $N$ over $\Qe$ exists. The contrast with the binary alphabet is sharp: a perfect binary array of shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ exists only when $\sum a_k$ is even and $\max a_k\le\frac12\sum a_k+1$, by a theorem of Jedwab and Kraemer on Menon difference sets in abelian $2$-groups, whereas over $\Qe$ there is no constraint on the shape. We also show that, unlike the one-dimensional case, single arrays carrying a non-central twist do exist in two dimensions, and determine where the one-dimensional non-existence argument breaks.
High-order Crank-Nicolson method via diagonal Padé factorization
Lou Freschi; Camille Lévêque; Jérémie Caillat; Richard Taïeb; Jonathan Dubois

We present a numerical method to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation at arbitrary order of accuracy in the time step, particularly well suited for tridiagonal Hamilton operators. The method is based on a factorization of the diagonal Padé approximants of the matrix exponential into products of linear factors, which preserves tridiagonal matrix structure at every time step and yields a propagator of order 2q in the time step at a cost of O(qN) operations. The propagator is exactly unitary by construction, and at lowest order q=1 it reduces to the standard Crank-Nicolson algorithm. We further extend the method to any Hamiltonian admitting a decomposition into a sum of tridiagonal or diagonal operators via high-order split-operator techniques (McLachlan, 2022), retaining O(qN) scaling at each time step. We also analytically show and numerically verify that the precision is dictated by the split-operator method. This covers a broad range of physically relevant cases, including higher-dimensional systems, higher-order spatial discretizations, and non-separable potentials.
Some notes on Erdős' last equation

We study the Diophantine equation $$n^h(x_1 + \ldots + x_n) = x_1 x_2 \cdots x_n,$$ where $h \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, and $x_1 \le \ldots \le x_n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. We define the solution set $ELE(h, n)$ consisting of all such integer tuples. We derive bounds on $x_n$ and $x_{n-1}$ in $ELE(h,n)$. We prove that $x_1 \cdot\ldots\cdot x_n \le n^h(n^h + 1)(n^h + n - 1)$. We also show that for $h = 1$, $x_{n-1} \le n + \max_{d \mid 2n^2 - 2n,\, d \le \sqrt{2n^2 - 2n}} d$, and for $h \ge 2$, the inequality $x_{n-1} \le 2n^h$ holds in $ELE(h, n)$. Moreover, we study the minimal value $g(h, n)$ of the largest coordinate $x_n$, and define $g(h) = \min_{n \ge 2} g(h,n)$. We prove that $$ \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{g(h,n)}{\frac{\log \log n \cdot \log \log \log \log n}{\log \log \log n}} \ge 1. $$ We also estimate the growth of the number of solutions. We show that for any $\varepsilon > 0,$ we have $\sum_{m \le n} |ELE(h,m)| < n^{h+1+\varepsilon} $
for sufficiently large $n$, and that $|ELE(h,n)| > n^{1 - \varepsilon}$ for infinitely many $n$.
Sign Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics for Supply-Demand Coordination under Binary Human Feedback
Yuya Miyaoka; Kengo Urata; Masaki Inoue

This paper addresses supply-demand coordination, in which a supplier sets prices to balance the demands of multiple buyers against limited resources. Existing studies typically solve the supply-demand coordination problem with a distributed algorithm called primal-dual gradient dynamics (PDGD), assuming that each buyer discloses the value of its own utility or marginal utility function. In contrast, we assume that each buyer discloses only binary information, namely whether it wants more or less of the current amount, and propose Sign PDGD. Sign PDGD is a PDGD algorithm in which the buyers' update depends only on the sign information. We analyze the convergence of Sign PDGD by interpreting it as a sliding mode control (SMC). For a quadratic cost and linear constraints, we show that under a gain condition, the primal and dual variables converge to the optimal solution. Numerical simulations on a toy resource-sharing problem confirm the two-phase behavior of SMC and show that the primal and dual variables approach the optimal solution.
Correspondence-Free Camera Pose Estimation by Matching Moments
Subhransu S. Bhattacharjee; Dylan Campbell; Rahul Shome

The blind perspective-$n$-point (PnP) problem is to estimate the pose of a calibrated camera from 2D and 3D point sets with unknown correspondences. We show that, for complete, noiseless observations, fourteen permutation-invariant image moments up to order four identify a fixed camera pose for almost every 3D point set containing at least twenty points. Our learning-free method, MomentPnP, matches these moments between the observed 2D points and the projected 3D points to initialize a camera pose without correspondences and refines the pose and correspondence weights using expectation--maximization. Across the test sets of three benchmarks, our method reduces median rotation error by $5$--$170\times$ relative to the best learned baseline, both with and without outliers. We recover accurate poses even with as many outliers as inliers. On dense ETH3D scans, pose accuracy improves as the point sets grow, even as individual correspondences become harder to resolve.
A scaling-based approach to mixed fractional $p$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$

We study equations driven by a sum of two fractional $p$-Laplacians with different orders and exponents. A central contribution of this paper is a Pohožaev identity for finite-energy weak solutions, established without additional regularity assumptions by means of a new approach based on scaling and convexity defects. This identity, which is of independent interest, yields nonexistence results for critical problems. Furthermore, we establish weighted Sobolev embeddings, construct an unbounded sequence of positive eigenvalues without relying on the Pohožaev identity, and prove multiplicity results for subcritical and doubly critical problems using scaling-based variational methods.
Relationship between generic Hecke algebra modules and $0$-Hecke algebra modules
Young-Hun Kim; So-Yeon Lee; Young-Tak Oh

Let $H_{R,a}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ be the Hecke algebra over a principal ideal domain $R$ with parameter $a\in R$. The representation theories of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ differ substantially and have largely been studied independently. In this paper, we relate the categories of finitely generated modules of these two algebras through specialization functors from the category of finitely generated $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules. We first investigate the fundamental properties of these functors concerning dimensions, essential surjectivity, and characters. We then construct $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules which, through these functors, provide connections between skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$, and between Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and dual plactic class modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$. Both families of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules are closely related to regular Schur labeled skew shape posets. We further explore how specialization functors relate the Frobenius characteristic to the quasisymmetric characteristic and connects the branching rules for skew Specht modules with those for $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules. Finally, we use the established connection with Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules to obtain a result on the classification of dual plactic class modules up to isomorphism.

Sullivan recently constructed continuum many countable homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for every $n\ge3$ by forbidding configurations he calls pair-cancelling. We show that, for every family $\mathcal F$ of pair-cancelling $n$-hypertournaments, the class of all linearly ordered finite $\mathcal F$-free $n$-hypertournaments is Ramsey and has the ordering property. In particular, freely ordered $\mathbf{H}_4$-free $3$-hypertournaments are Ramsey, answering a question of Cherlin, Hubička, Nešetřil, and the author from 2021. For every odd $n\ge3$, we give a simple Ramsey expansion with the expansion property for even $n$-hypertournaments by naming an $(n-1)$-hypertournament and a free linear order.
 We also show that, for $n\ge6$, no unbounded hereditary strong amalgamation class of finite $n$-hypertournaments has EPPA. Moreover, we prove the failure of EPPA for all Sullivan's classes with $n\ge4$, and for the even $5$-hypertournaments.
 We conjecture that even hypertournaments and classes omitting a family of pair-cancelling hypertournaments, together with the homogeneous cyclic order in arity three, are the only countably infinite homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for $n\ge3$. We give some supporting evidence.
Florian Luca; István Pink; Csaba Sándor

For a positive integer $n\ge 2$, we look at the number of solutions of the Diophantine equation $$ n(x_1+\cdots+x_n)=x_1\cdots x_n. $$ Denoting by $f(n)$ this number we show that $\liminf_{n\to\infty} \log f(n)/\log n=0$.
Treewidth and Separation Number: An Optimal Linear Bound

The \emph{separation number} $\sn(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $a$ such that every subgraph $H$ of $G$ admits a separation $(A,B)$ of {\em order} $|A\cap B|\le a$ whose two sides $A\setminus B$ and $B\setminus A$ each contain at most $2|V(H)|/3$ vertices. Dvořák and Norin proved that $\tw(G)\le 15\sn(G)$ for every nonempty graph $G$. We improve the constant to its optimal value: every nonempty graph satisfies $\tw(G)\le 4\sn(G)-2$. This is best possible: for every $k\ge 2$, there is a graph $G_k$ with $\tw(G_k)=4k+2$ and $\sn(G_k)=k+1$.
Extensions of $q$-supercongruences arising from a quadratic summation of Gasper and Rahman

In this paper, inspired by recent work of Guo and Zhao, and of Guo and Zudilin, we establish two parametric extensions of their $q$-supercongruences using Gasper and Rahman's quadratic summation, the Chinese remainder theorem, and the creative microscoping method. These extensions yield two one-parameter generalizations of the $q$-supercongruences considered by Guo and Zhao and by Guo and Zudilin.
Flat and very flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves on ind-schemes

This is a paper about homological algebra of flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves. We recall and collect various techniques such as accessibility and deconstructibility, and adopt them to ind-schemes under various assumptions. We also discuss the foundations of the notion of an ind-scheme.
Tunneling effect in some singular wells
Yannick Guedes Bonthonneau; Léo Morin; Nicolas Raymond

The Schrödinger operator in one dimension is considered. When the electric potential has a linear/V-shaped well, an approximation of the ground-state is established at fixed distance from the well. In this situation, the classical WKB analysis and the localization techniques à la Agmon near a non-degenerate minimum do not work. We propose an alternative to the WKB analysis better suited to the shape of the well and we prove that our Ansatz is an exponentially good approximation by means of revisited (and simplified) Agmon estimates.
Rigidity and classification of complete translating solitons and self-expanders with constant curvature in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$
