For complete immersed surfaces in Euclidean four-space whose mean curvature vector has constant length, translators are affine planes parallel to their fixed nonzero velocity, and self-expanders are planes through their centre. This rigidity requires no Lagrangian assumption, properness, volume growth control, or bound on the second fundamental form. Complete Lagrangian translators and self-expanders in $\mathbb{C}^{2}$ with constant Gaussian curvature are flat and, up to unitary equivalence, are properly embedded products of two complete planar curves. Translating factors are lines or grim reapers. Expanding factors are lines through the origin or nonstraight self-expanders. The proofs use moving frames, a transnormal function, a cubic tensor identity, and analytic continuation.
Large deviations and the asymptotic geometry of Lorentz balls

We study the uniform distribution on finite-dimensional Lorentz balls $B_{q,p}^n$ in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. We prove a Sanov-type large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the absolute coordinates of a random vector uniformly distributed on $n^{1/q}B_{q,p}^n$. The rate function is given by an entropy deficit under a weighted quantile constraint. We show that the entropy maximizer is unique and characterize its distribution function as the unique increasing solution of a nonlinear boundary-value problem. The limiting distribution has compact support, for which we obtain an explicit bound. These results establish the conjectured empirical limit of Kabluchko, Prochno and Sonnleitner [Journal of Functional Analysis, 288(1):110682, 2025] in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. As consequences, we determine the exponential volume asymptotics of Lorentz balls and obtain asymptotic independence of any fixed number of coordinates. We also prove a law of large numbers for Lorentz norms with finite parameters and use it, together with the volume asymptotics, to obtain a Schechtman--Schmuckenschläger type theorem for intersections of volume-normalized Lorentz balls. We further derive a variational formula for the logarithmic intersection asymptotics. The proof combines an exponential change of measure with quantile interpolation and a variational argument that does not assume regularity of the maximizing quantile in advance.
Conan Naichung Leung; YuTung Yau; Zhenyu Ye

Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,Ω)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[
 \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr)
 [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms.
 We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.
A Lifted Hessian-Riemannian Gradient Flow for LQR Synthesis under Passivity Constraints

The static state-feedback gain that renders a linear system passive at an external port and minimizes a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost cannot be computed by convex optimization, since the passivity certificate and the LQR cost are coupled bilinearly through the common gain. A previous indirect approach restricts the gain to a convex inner approximation of the passivity region, which is conservative and whose construction scales exponentially with the number of gain entries. This paper proposes a direct approach. The set of strictly passivating gains is the image of a convex lifted set of inverse storage matrices and transformed gains. We describe this set by a strict linear matrix inequality and an affine equality for every feedthrough matrix with positive semidefinite symmetric part, including feedthrough matrices with a singular symmetric part, and minimize the LQR cost over it by a gradient flow whose metric is the Hessian of a logarithmic barrier. For multi-input systems, this Hessian is singular along gain changes that preserve the storage function, and we complete the metric along these directions by the metric of the gain space. We prove that the flow exists for all times, that every gain along the flow is strictly passivating with an explicit storage function, and that the cost decreases monotonically while the gains remain in a compact set of stabilizing gains. Numerical examples show that the flow attains a lower cost than the indirect approach, that the completion is required for multi-input systems, and that the flow can converge to a local minimizer on nonconvex passivity regions.
Linear Dynamics of Composition Operators on Zygmund Spaces of Rooted Trees
Xiang Chen; Siwei Song; Liang Zhang; Zehua Zhou

We conjugate composition operators on the Zygmund and little Zygmund spaces of an infinite, locally finite rooted tree $T$ by the second-difference isometries. A path Green kernel gives row-finite matrices that characterize boundedness and yield exact operator norms. A rigidity result holds on the chain $\mathbb{N}_0$. Boundedness on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is equivalent to $\varphi(n)=qn+b$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}$. For these symbols, $\varphi(n)>n$ eventually characterizes Li-Yorke chaos of $C_\varphi$ on either Zygmund space, allowing noninjectivity and periodic vertices. If $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\mathcal{Z}_0(T)$ and $\varphi^k(T)$ eventually avoids every finite set, then for each $λ\ne0$, $λC_\varphi$ is Li-Yorke chaotic on either space exactly when the norms of its powers are unbounded. For $\varphi_q(n)=q(n+1)-1$ with integer $q\ge2$, the corresponding conditions are $|λ|q^2>1$ on both Zygmund spaces and $|λ|q>1$ on the little Lipschitz space. For bounded $C_\varphi$ on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$, topological mixing and Devaney chaos each hold exactly for injective symbols with no periodic vertices and eventual slope $q\ge2$. For such bounded operators with strictly increasing $\varphi$ and $\varphi(0)>0$, $q\ge2$ also characterizes hypercyclicity and frequent hypercyclicity.
An adaptive Gaussian splitting scheme for linear Fokker--Planck equations
Markus Bachmayr; Tianyu Jin; Damiano Lombardi; Olga Mula; Ahmad Zorkot

We develop an adaptive numerical method for linear Fokker--Planck equations on $\mathbb R^d$, based on approximating the evolving probability density by linear combinations of Gaussian functions (LCGs). The method applies to polynomial-type drift fields, without requiring a gradient-flow structure or a stationary distribution. It relies on an operator splitting that separates diffusion and affine drift, for which Gaussian functions can be propagated exactly, from higher-order transport, whose evolution is approximated adaptively by LCGs. Both the number of Gaussian components and their means and covariances are adjusted to meet the prescribed accuracy tolerances. The adaptivity is driven by computable error indicators involving polynomial moments of Gaussians that can be evaluated analytically. We provide a rigorous error analysis that relates the approximation error to the indicators driving adaptivity and illustrate the performance of the scheme in several test cases.
On Sobolev spaces and Koksma-Hlawka-type inequalities of fractional order

Spaces of fractional smoothness in the sense of Riemann-Liouville of order $0<α<1$ were introduced in [J. Dick, Ann. Math. Pura Appl., 187, 385-403, 2008]. Dick also proved Koksma-Hlawka type inequalities for these spaces, using a notion of fractional discrepancy. In [M. Gnewuch et al., Constr. Approx., 63, 647-711, 2026] upper error-bounds for QMC-integration on these spaces were obtained using $(t,m,s)$-nets and it was proved that the above mentioned Koksma-Hlawka inequalities by Dick are sharp. One step in the proof of the upper bounds was the embedding of the spaces of fractional smoothness into Bessel potential spaces, also called fractional Sobolev spaces. We prove that, up to norm equivalence, spaces of fractional smoothness and Bessel potential spaces are equal. From this we deduce that the upper error bounds for QMC-integration from Gnewuch et al. are indeed optimal for spaces of fractional smoothness. Furthermore, we obtain two types of Koksma-Hlawka inequalities for Bessel potential spaces. The first type uses the fractional discrepancy as introduced by Dick. The second type adopts an approach by Triebel from [H. Triebel, EMS Press, 2010] by using the norm of the (local) discrepancy function in an adjoint Bessel potential space.
A note on Padmanabhan's path-integral duality
P. Fernandez de Cordoba; J. M. Isidro

We develop a field-theoretic implementation of Padmanabhan's principle of invariance under the duality $\mathcal S \rightarrow {L_0^2}/{\mathcal S}$, where ${\mathcal S}$ is the proper length (the action integral along a particle's trajectory) and $L_0$ is a quantum of length. Starting from the particle propagator and its Schwinger proper-time representation, we derive the wave operator associated with the duality transformation in terms of a scalar field, rather than a point particle. The resulting theory is governed by a nonlocal operator involving modified Bessel functions. We analyse the infrared and ultraviolet regimes, demonstrate the recovery of standard Klein-Gordon theory at low energies, and show the appearance of exponential ultraviolet suppression. Our analysis provides a natural extension, to quantum field theory, of Padmanabhan's duality for point particles.
Beyond Finite Dimensions: Duflo-Serganova Cohomology, the Formal Superdimension, and a Kac-Wakimoto Theorem for Unitarizable Supermodules

The main results of this manuscript are fourfold. First, we introduce relative holomorphic discrete series supermodules over basic classical Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(n\vert n)$. These are unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents are Harish-Chandra modules of relative holomorphic discrete series representations. We show that these are exactly the unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose globalizations have supermatrix coefficients square-integrable modulo the center. Second, we define the formal superdimension of a relative holomorphic discrete series supermodule as the parity-weighted sum of the formal dimensions of its $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents. We show that it equals, up to sign, the value at zero of an $L$-packet supercharacter obtained by averaging over the Weyl group. Third, we prove a Kac-Wakimoto theorem for formal superdimension: it is nonzero if and only if the highest weight is maximally atypical. For integral highest weights, it equals the superdimension of a finite-dimensional simple supermodule with the same degree of atypicality. We realize these supermodules through derived Zuckerman functors. For nonintegral highest weights, it is computed by generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology. Finally, to establish the Kac-Wakimoto conjecture, we develop the theory of generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology for unitarizable supermodules. We prove that the cohomology of a unitarizable simple supermodule is unitarizable and either zero or simple.
Multi-bubble solutions for an exponential biharmonic Neumann problem in dimension four
Jiaoping Chen; Wenjing Chen; Shengbing Deng

We are concerned with the biharmonic Neumann problem \[ Δ^2u+u=0\quad\text{in }Ω,\qquad \partial_νu=0,\quad \partial_νΔu=-\varepsilon h e^{24π^2u} \quad\text{on }\partialΩ, \] where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^4$ is a smooth bounded domain, $ν$ is the outward unit normal, $h\in C^5(\partialΩ)$ is positive, and $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small. For each fixed integer $m\ge1$, we construct $m$-bubble solutions $u_\varepsilon$ by Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. As $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions concentrate at $m$ distinct boundary points, each carrying unit mass for the measure $\varepsilon h e^{24π^2u_\varepsilon}\,dσ$. For solutions corresponding to nondegenerate critical points $ξ^*$ of the interaction function $\mathcal F_m$, we establish local uniqueness and nondegeneracy, and prove $\ind(u_\varepsilon)=m+\ind(-D^2\mathcal F_m(ξ^*))$. In particular, for a generic positive weight $h$, all critical points of $\mathcal F_m$ are nondegenerate, and the $m$-bubble solutions associated with global minima of $\mathcal F_m$ have Morse index $4m$.
Scaled boundary finite elements for FFT-based computational micromechanics
Flavia Gehrig; Carolin Birk; Matti Schneider

We introduce a matrix-free FFT-based solver for three-dimensional linear elastic homogenization problems discretized by the scaled boundary finite element method (SBFEM) on a voxel grid. Owing to its analytical solution in the radial direction, the SBFEM discretization is inherently softer than fully integrated voxel finite elements, whereas its displacement-based formulation remains symmetric, conforming, and supports arbitrary stiffness anisotropy. These properties make SBFEM an attractive candidate for porous and highly heterogeneous microstructures, where existing voxel-based FFT discretizations offer no generally reliable choice: Reduced-integration hexahedral elements, equivalently the rotated staggered grid discretization, may suffer from hourglass instabilities in the presence of voids, whereas fully integrated hexahedral elements are often too stiff. The proposed discretization uses hexahedral SBFEM cells on the full voxel mesh of a regular periodic grid, retaining the simplicity of a fixed-resolution voxel representation without requiring adaptive mesh coarsening. The main contribution is a preconditioner based on the homogeneous SBFEM stiffness operator. We show that this preconditioner may be applied locally in Fourier space and that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by the material contrast, independently of the grid resolution. This result enables a fully matrix-free implementation of the SBFEM-discretized problem, without assembling or storing the global stiffness matrix. Numerical experiments on a short-fibre reinforced composite, a polyurethane foam and a sand-based binder jet microstructure demonstrate robust convergence and competitive accuracy compared with established voxel discretizations. In particular, SBFEM remains stable for porous microstructures, for which reduced-integration hexahedral elements become unstable.
Regularized Ray-Singer analytic torsion on odd dimensional convex-cocompact hyperbolic manifolds

We introduce the notion of regularized (or renormalized) Ray-Singer analytic torsion on odd dimensional convex-cocompact hyperbolic manifolds. We prove that the leading asymptotic along a certain sequence of representations is a constant multiple of a regularized volume extending the classical results which hold for finite volume hyperbolic manifolds possibly with singularities. Furthermore, we establish some of the functional equations, including Fried type identity, also extending the identities on finite volume hyperbolic manifolds.
Harish-Chandra Modules for the Lie algebra of Divergence-Free Vector Fields on a Two-Dimensional Torus
Xiangqian Guo; Ye Huang; Yufeng Yao

Let $\mathcal S_2$ be the Lie algebra of divergence-free Laurent polynomial vector fields on a two-dimensional torus. We determine its simple weight modules with uniformly bounded weight multiplicities. As a consequence, we obtain a classification of its simple Harish-Chandra modules, i.e., weight modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces, which are either simple generalized highest weight modules or simple quotients of tensor fields modules.
Minimax Growth and Morse Indices for the Critical Choquard Equation on the Sphere

We study the conformally critical Choquard equation on $\mathbb S^n$, \[ -Δ_{\mathbb S^n} v(ξ) + \frac{n(n-2)}{4} v(ξ) = \left(\int_{\mathbb S^n} \frac{|v(η)|^p}{|ξ-η|^μ} dV_η\right) |v(ξ)|^{p-2} v(ξ), \] where $n\ge 3$, $0<μ<n$, and $p=(2n-μ)/(n-2)$ denotes the conformally critical Choquard exponent. For the standard action of \(G=O(k)\times O(\ell)\) with \(k,\ell\ge 2\) and \(k+\ell=n+1\), we use the cohomological index and orbit interval partition to build attained minimax levels with sharp growth \(c_j\asymp j^{2p/(p-1)}\). All \(G\)-invariant solutions at \(c_j\) change sign for \(j\ge 2\). If \(p\ge 2\), positivity of the Riesz form on nodal truncations gives \(N_G(v)\le m_G(v)\), and \(N_G(v)\le j\) whenever \(E(v)=c_j\). Here \(N_G\) counts nodal domains, and \(m_G,ν_G\) are the invariant Morse index and nullity, respectively. In particular, \(c_2\) is the least energy of \(G\)-invariant sign-changing solutions, with such solutions having two nodal domains. Under the additional assumption that every critical point of the reduced functional \(Ψ\) at level \(c_j\) is isolated in the full critical set of \(Ψ\), the critical group theory gives \(m_G\leq j\leq m_G+ν_G\) for a selected critical solution. For \(p\ge 2\), only finitely many angular blocks contribute to the full index and nullity, and every nonconstant \(G\)-invariant solution has transverse negative directions. When \(k=\ell\) and \(μ>0\) is sufficiently small, we compute the radial index and nullity in the \((1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\) blocks of solutions from minimizing the reduced energy over \(G\)-invariant functions odd under factor interchange.
State-Dependent Saving and Heavy-Tailed Shocks in a Stochastic Solow Growth Model via a Logistic Lévy Framework

This work develops a stochastic Solow growth model in which the aggregate saving rate is state dependent and evolves on a faster time scale than capital. The saving target follows a mean-reverting process driven by symmetric $α$-stable Lévy noise, while the saving control adjusts toward this target and capital accumulates according to a Solow equation. After scaling, the model is a three-dimensional stochastic dynamical system with multiplicative heavy-tailed noise and a logistic saving function. We establish invariance of the economically meaningful state space for the discrete reflected model, derive the stationary distribution of the saving target in the Gaussian limiting case, and characterize how the tail index and logistic sensitivity affect the coupled dynamics. Monte Carlo simulations show bimodal capital and saving distributions, asymmetric first-passage behavior between low- and high-capital regimes, and a nonlinear relationship between output volatility, the logistic sensitivity, and the tail index. In particular, heavier tails increase the dispersion of the scaled saving target and low-to-high first-passage frequencies, but do not necessarily increase relative output volatility. The results highlight the importance of state-dependent saving and non-Gaussian shocks for growth dynamics.
Bing Yang; Chengjun Hou; Xiaochun Fang

We study $R^*$-subalgebras of von Neumann algebras. In finite homogeneous type $\mathrm I_n$, every $R^*$-subalgebra is locally finite-dimensional. We also give a trace criterion for local finite dimensionality in the semifinite setting under a finite-trace hypothesis, and prove an approximate halving property for projections in strongly dense $R^*$-subalgebras of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. For three projections in an $R^*$-subalgebra of a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, the reduced word-length filtration gives bounds on layer growth, criteria for stabilization, and uniform bounds on minimal-polynomial degrees at each fixed word length. Finally, we give a negative answer to Kadison's fifteenth problem by constructing an infinite-dimensional unital $*$-algebra generated algebraically by three projections in which every selfadjoint element has finite spectrum. The resulting $R^*$-algebra embeds unitally into every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.
Sharp Local Entropy Bounds in the Wasserstein Space
Chang Jun Im; Jeong Min Jeon

Fréchet regression extends regression analysis to metric space-valued responses such as probability distributions. Its asymptotic theory often relies on local entropy conditions, which control the complexity of small balls in the response space. A commonly used condition requires the associated local entropy integral to remain bounded as the balls shrink, but this requirement can fail when the response space is infinite-dimensional. We determine the exact rate at which this integral diverges in the Wasserstein space of probability distributions supported on a compact interval. Specifically, for a broad class of ball centers, we establish matching upper and lower bounds for the local covering entropy and show that the local entropy integral grows at the rate of the reciprocal square root of the ball radius. This rate persists when the response space is restricted to a large class of continuous distributions. The same rate holds for uniform local entropy integrals, with the supremum taken over ball centers. These results quantify the local complexity of the Wasserstein space and provide sharp benchmarks for entropy assumptions in statistical problems with distribution-valued responses.
Haar local mixing for transverse subgroups
Sam Edwards; Minju Lee; Hee Oh

Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. For torsion-free Zariski dense $θ$-transverse subgroups, we establish Haar local mixing for the partial Weyl chamber action under a Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) local mixing hypothesis. The proof is based on a transfer principle using the domains of discontinuity introduced by Delarue-Monclair-Sanders and extended to transverse subgroups by Guedes Bonthonneau-Lefeuvre-Weich. For $θ$-Anosov subgroups, we verify the BMS hypothesis by adapting existing arguments and hence obtain Haar local mixing. As a consequence, we obtain asymptotics for the volume and distribution of long returns and recover the growth indicator from return volumes. Under linear $θ$-regularity, the transfer also holds with polynomial error estimates. This condition is satisfied by subgroups of $θ$-Anosov or relatively $θ$-Anosov groups.
UNIDE: Cross-PDE Learning for Noise-Robust Discovery of Governing Equations

Governing partial differential equations (PDEs) provide compact and interpretable descriptions of physical systems. Classical methods, such as sparse and symbolic regression, fit a new equation to each observed field: what is learned on one system is not carried to the next, and observation noise corrupts the derivative features they rely on. This paper introduces UNIDE (Unified Identification of Differential Equations), a data-driven approach that learns across PDE families to identify governing equations from new noisy trajectories. It integrates three components: a self-supervised denoiser trained without clean targets, an encoder shared across PDE families that predicts which candidate terms are active, and weak-form least squares with residual-based pruning that estimates their coefficients. We demonstrate UNIDE on synthetic one-dimensional trajectories from six PDE families with known term structures, including the Burgers and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equations. We train one model per noise level and systematically compare UNIDE with SINDy, WSINDy, and PySR. The results show that UNIDE recovers the exact set of governing terms more often than all three at every noise level from $1\%$ to $80\%$. At $80\%$ noise, where the noise standard deviation is $0.8$ times that of the field, it recovers the exact terms for $92\%$ of held-out trajectories, whereas the best baseline recovers about $1\%$. UNIDE is also efficient: because its neural components are reused rather than refit, it identifies each new trajectory in $0.45$ seconds, $2.7$ times faster than WSINDy and $51$ times faster than PySR. These results demonstrate the potential of learning across PDE families for efficient equation identification under substantial observation noise.
Existence of global weak solutions for a simplified Ericksen-Leslie fluid interacting with a rigid body

In this paper, we consider a three-dimensional nematic liquid crystal governed by the simplified Ericksen-Leslie system interacting with a moving rigid body. We prove the existence of global weak solutions, where we especially treat the case of contact with the container wall. The director field $\boldsymbol{d}$ satisfies $|\boldsymbol{d}| = 1$ as well as $d_3 \ge 0$, and its non-homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition on the body interface, referred to as strong anchoring, is transported with the rigid motion. The moving-domain problem with the above director condition is obtained as a limit of a Ginzburg-Landau regularization. An extension of the director to the body domain yields global compactness, while a compactness argument as in the seminal work by Lin and Wang [39] yields strong convergence away from the interface. If the body is in contact with the wall, we impose a perfectly inelastic sticking law. Since the resulting domain after contact is not necessarily Lipschitz, we prove weak existence for the simplified Ericksen-Leslie model on arbitrary bounded open sets, which is of independent interest.
Local limit theorems and counting for transverse subgroups
Sam Edwards; Minju Lee; Hee Oh

Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. We study the joint distribution of partial Cartan projections and the two associated Cartan flags for Zariski dense $θ$-transverse subgroups. Assuming local mixing of the associated Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure, we prove two local limit theorems and deduce counting asymptotics in Euclidean balls and tubes, together with equidistribution of the Cartan flags. These qualitative conclusions hold for $θ$-Anosov subgroups, for which the local mixing hypothesis is satisfied. If the group is linearly $θ$-regular near the direction of maximal growth, a polynomial error in local mixing gives polynomial errors in these results. Applying the quantitative local mixing theorem of Kim-Oh-Pan, we obtain local limit and counting theorems with polynomial error estimates for several classes of relatively Anosov representations of Fuchsian groups.

Nonclassical multiphoton interference is an important resource for optical quantum information processing, and its output statistics depend on the distinguishability of the input photons. In this paper, using time delay as a tunable parameter, we theoretically analyze the interference behavior of independent pure-state single photons with identical Gaussian spectral envelopes under near-synchronous conditions. Using the immanant representation of the single-photon internal-state overlap matrix to express the weights of the exchange-symmetry components, we determine the leading asymptotic behavior and approximation error of each weight, and characterize the weight suppression laws when different groups of photons become synchronized on different scales. Given the local identity classes of the delay functions and the vanishing orders of pairwise delay differences, the vanishing orders of the weights of the exchange-symmetry components can be computed in polynomial time by integer minimum-cost flow. On this basis, we provide a network-independent total-variation error bound for the complete output photon-number distribution, establish a quantitative relationship among the photon spectral width, synchronization precision, and interference statistics deviation, and provide a quantitative basis for the analysis and approximation of near-synchronous multiphoton interference.
Explicit topology control in isogeometric topology optimization using persistent homology
Wenliang Yin; Gengchen Li; Hongwei Lin

Explicitly controlling structural topology remains a major challenge in topology optimization. While many implicit methods regulate topology only indirectly, available explicit strategies often focus on two-dimensional hole control or extend to 3D without a unified treatment of tunnels and cavities. This study proposes a differentiable, persistent homology-based framework for explicit topology control in 2D and 3D isogeometric topology optimization. A NURBS-represented density field induces a single sublevel filtration whose persistence diagrams quantify the connected components, holes in 2D, and tunnels and cavities in 3D directly. To enforce prescribed bounds on topological feature counts, weighted topological objectives are applied in a staged manner that coordinates the different homology dimensions. Each redundant feature is removed either by cutting or by filling according to the region of its corresponding persistence pair, avoiding the excessive structural changes associated with filling alone. The topological inverse mapping yields analytical sensitivities with respect to the density control coefficients, so that the resulting objective is readily incorporated into gradient-based optimization and solved by the method of moving asymptotes. Numerical experiments on 2D and 3D benchmarks demonstrate explicit and reliable topology control while maintaining competitive mechanical performance and stable convergence.
Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras

We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.
Universality of Brown measure convergence for non-Gaussian matrix polynomials with adjoints

Let $P$ be a noncommutative polynomial of arbitrary degree. We prove that the empirical spectral distribution of $P$ evaluated at independent Wigner matrices converges weakly in probability to its Brown measure limit. The same conclusion holds for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent iid matrices and their adjoints. The entry laws have bounded real or joint planar densities and a finite $(2+\varepsilon)$ moment; only second moments are required on the Wigner diagonal. The real and imaginary parts of an entry may be dependent, and its pseudovariance need not vanish. The proof develops the coefficient-algebra approach of the author's earlier work on matrix polynomials with Gaussian and non-Gaussian iid inputs \cite{Han}. The main step is a polynomial lower-tail estimate, under only second moments, for the least singular value of a tensor pencil with arbitrary fixed matrix coefficients. We use a logarithmic determinant method: a real-block small-ball argument shows that logarithmic derivatives of the determinant control the inverse pencil. Relative polynomial anti-concentration then gives the lower-tail bound. We establish convergence of logarithmic potentials by Hermitian resolvent comparison and rank truncation. This extends the recent Brown measure convergence theorem of Collins, Kitagawa, Miyagawa, Yuan and Zhong \cite{Collins} for GUE polynomials to non-Gaussian Wigner inputs.
On the behavior of the number of $k$-full integers between successive $k$-th powers

Let $k\ge2$ be an integer. Inspired by an observation of Erdős (1976), we investigate the behavior of $h_k(n)$, the number of $k$-full integers in the interval $(n^k, (n+1)^k)$ for positive integers $n$. Let $δ_k$ denote the supremum of the exponents $δ$ for which the inequality $h_k(n) > (\log n)^δ$ holds for infinitely many positive integers $n$. We improve the previously known lower bound $δ_k \ge 1/2$, implied by Munsch, Shparlinski, and Yau (2020), to $δ_k \ge 1$. Furthermore, for any given integer $m \ge 1$, we derive an effective upper bound for the smallest positive integer $n$ satisfying $h_k(n)\ge m$.
On Primitive Divisor Multiplicities of Lucas Sequences

Let $(U_{n})$ be a nondegenerate Lucas sequence with coprime integer parameters. Assuming the rational $abc$ conjecture, we prove that almost every index $n$ has a primitive prime divisor of $U_{n}$ of multiplicity one. More quantitatively, the logarithmic contribution of repeated primitive prime factors tends to zero relative to the primitive part along any family with $φ(n) / n$ bounded below, and also in Cesàro mean over all indices. We derive explicit logarithmic lower bounds for Lucas non-Wieferich primes with ranks in prescribed residue classes. Both signs of the discriminant are allowed. Independently, we describe initial multiplicities at good odd primes by a unique Hensel root in the recurrence-parameter disk and by the exact contraction rate of a normalized Dickson-polynomial iteration. Applications include rank and period lifting for Fibonacci numbers and the Wall-Sun-Sun condition.
Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions I

We study isolated boundary singularities of positive solutions of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We prove the critical upper bound for general smooth metrics in dimensions $3\le n\le17$ and for Euclidean domains with smooth boundary in dimensions $3\le n\le22$. For general metrics, this range extends to $n=18$ when the conformal metric is complete near the singularity. In every dimension, the critical upper bound implies removability or a matching lower bound and convergence to a unique flat Fowler solution with a positive power rate. Sharpness of these dimension ranges will be established in a subsequent paper.
Uniform-in-time error estimates for the Klein-Gordon-Schrödinger system in the nonrelativistic limit regime

In this paper, we study the Klein--Gordon--Schrödinger system in the nonrelativistic regime $\e\to 0$ on $\R^d$ with $d\ge4$, where $\e$ is a small parameter proportional to the inverse of the speed of light. For sufficiently regular initial data, we show that its solution is well approximated by oscillatory profiles governed by a decoupled linear Schrödinger-wave semi-limiting model with error $O(\e^2)$ uniformly for all $t \ge 0 $. This rigorously justifies the numerical study of Bao and Zhao \cite{BZ17}.
A study guide for Bourgain's 2003 sum-product theorem and 2010 discretized projection theorem

These notes present Bourgain's proofs of the discretized sum-product theorem and its applications. The discussion emphasizes the construction of trees with multiscale porosity from small additive doubling, using either quantitative Freiman theorrem or the Plünnecke-Ruzsa inequality, and the amplification of these structures by multiplication. Additive combinatorial tools connect the resulting growth estimates to discretized sum-product problem. The notes also discuss the passage to the exceptional set estimates for orthogonal projections, the exclusion of Borel subrings of intermediate Hausdorff dimension, and Fourier decay for multiplicative convolutions of measures.
Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for convex Hamilton--Jacobi equations with super critical viscosity
Gengyu Liu; Zibo Wang; Jianlu Zhang

This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.
Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus

We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $κ$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{π_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to give an alternative proof to a theorem of Larson in (arXiv:2404.12607), and verify a conjecture of the second author in (arXiv:2604.11958) in the rank $2$ case.
Hyperbolic string vertices as geometric chains

For 0<L<=2arcsinh(1), the hyperbolic string vertices of Costello and Zwiebach consist of the bordered hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary of length L whose interior simple closed geodesics have length at least L. We show that the corresponding regions in moduli space are compact oriented orbifolds with corners whose boundaries are, including orientations and automorphism groups, the spaces of twisted sewings. Hence their generating chain satisfies the master equation without the bracket term exactly in a complex of geometric chains. The usual connected form cannot hold exactly for geometric chains; we determine its exact form, show that it holds modulo gluing and covering relations in a complex computing the homology of the moduli spaces, and that the vertex currents are the unique top-dimensional solution. Finally we compare with Costello's homotopical framework. In a strict model given by hyperbolic surfaces with marked boundary points, every solution of his master equation with his initial condition integrates exactly to the vertex currents, up to the sign (-1)^(3g-3+n); such solutions exist, are unique up to homotopy, and correspond to the hyperbolic vertices. Under a continuity assumption on the comparison map and granting the inputs of Costello's homology computation, the hyperbolic vertices represent his homotopy class of solutions, for a completed notion of homotopy.
Folding of d-invariants via F-invariants with applications to quiver Hecke KR-modules

The \(\de\)-invariant measures the interaction between two simple modules and controls the behavior of their convolution product. Using categorical interpretations of Cao's tropical and \(F\)-invariants, we establish folding formulas for the \(Λ\)-invariants between determinantial modules in arbitrary symmetrizable type and derive the corresponding \(\de\)-formula by symmetrization. We apply the \(\de\)-formula to quiver Hecke Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules and show that, in every finite type, their \(\de\)-invariants are completely determined by the coefficients of the symmetrized inverse \(t\)-quantized Cartan matrix. We obtain explicit formulas in all finite types, including closed formulas in the classical types \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(D\).
A new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras

This paper introduces a new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras and investigates the corresponding bialgebra structures. To this end, we first study an invariant-c$2$c form on a compatible Lie algebra, namely a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form that is invariant with respect to one Lie bracket and is a commutative $2$-cocycle with respect to the other, which naturally arises from a quadratic differential Novikov algebra. Then we introduce the notion of compatible Lie-anti-pre-Lie algebras (compatible LAPL algebras in short), which serve as the underlying algebra structures of compatible Lie algebras endowed with invariant-c$2$c forms. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a compatible LAPL bialgebra, which is shown to be equivalent to a Manin triple of compatible Lie algebras with respect to the invariant-c$2$c form. We investigate triangular compatible LAPL bialgebras, which are obtained from antisymmetric solutions of the compatible LAPL Yang-Baxter equation. We also use $\mathcal{O}$-operators of compatible LAPL algebras to construct such solutions. Finally, we show that every differential Novikov bialgebra gives rise to a compatible LAPL bialgebra and that this construction preserves triangularity.
Liouville theorems for nonlinear polyharmonic equations with indefinite nonlinearities
Juncheng Wei; Meiqing Xu; Hui Yang

We establish a Liouville theorem for nonnegative bounded solutions of the indefinite polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=x_1u^p$ in $\mathbb R^n$, for all integers $m\ge2$, $n\ge1$, and all $p>1$. The main difficulty lies in extending the moving-plane method to a higher-order equation with a sign-changing coefficient. We first combine sublinear growth estimates with reflection arguments to establish the super-polyharmonic property in the right half-space, without prescribing boundary conditions on the separating hyperplane. We then use a doubling and rescaling argument to obtain relative first- and second-derivative estimates on strips, replacing the scalar Harnack estimates used in the second-order case. These estimates allow us to establish monotonicity in the $x_1$-direction within the right half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, and a cutoff argument then yields the desired nonexistence result.
Full $t$-Linkage, Cancellation, and Almost Krull Domains

Motivated by open questions of Kabbaj and Mimouni, we determine the position of full $t$-linkage among the standard classes of integral domains and its relationship with almost Krullness. Full linkage for a star operation is equivalent to cancellation in the monoid of all nonzero fractional star ideals. For the $t$-operation, this full cancellation law, denoted by $\mathrm{TCL}$, lies strictly between the $t$-almost Dedekind and completely integrally closed classes; on the $\mathrm{PvMD}$ locus, we recover the known $t$-almost Dedekind characterization. We prove that $\mathrm{TCL}$ and almost Krullness are incomparable. A monoid algebra arising from Reinhart's example satisfies $\mathrm{TCL}$ but is neither almost Krull nor a $\mathrm{PvMD}$. In the opposite direction, we construct a locally factorial almost Krull domain with a maximal ideal $0\ne M=M_t=(M^2)_t\subsetneq D$. For this domain the canonical locally divisorial operation $κ$ is cancellative and $κ_f=t$, but cancellation does not descend to $t$. In contrast, finite valuation patching proves that the Heinzer--Ohm and Arnold--Matsuda almost Krull non-$\mathrm{PvMD}$s satisfy $\mathrm{TCL}$ with $t<κ$; in the latter example $κ=v$. Class-monoid, residual, and support criteria identify the obstruction to descent. Thus the missing $t$-linkage node is governed by cancellation in the entire fractional $t$-ideal monoid, rather than by local Krullness alone.
Neural Operator Approximation for Yau--Yau Nonlinear Filtering: Stability, Approximation, and Fast Computation
Xiaopei Jiao; Xiuqiong Chen; Stephen S. -T. Yau

Since the introduction of the Kalman filter, nonlinear state estimation has become an important topic in areas such as aerospace engineering, sensor design, and target tracking. Within the optimal filtering framework described by the Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, Yau-Yau filtering (YYF) employs an offline-online decomposition: the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov (FKE) equations, initialized by a prescribed set of basis functions, are solved offline, and the prior density is projected onto these basis functions during the online stage. However, this approach still faces two computational challenges: solving multiple FKEs offline can be computationally expensive, and the online projection becomes costly when filtering is performed repeatedly or in high-dimensional settings. To address these limitations, we develop a neural operator filter (NOF) that directly learns the mapping from the prior density to the posterior density, thereby eliminating both the expensive offline FKE solves and the online projection. The underlying operator is approximated using a Fourier neural operator (FNO). Numerical experiments on several challenging filtering systems verify both the effectiveness and accuracy of our method, and we further provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of its stability and approximation error.
Solutions concentrating on spheres for Hamiltonian elliptic systems with supercritical growth
Hui Zhang; Jianjun Zhang; Xuexiu Zhong

We study positive solutions of the singularly perturbed Hamiltonian elliptic system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -\varepsilon^2Δu+u=|v|^{q-2}v &\text{in }A,\\ -\varepsilon^2Δv+v=|u|^{p-2}u &\text{in }A,\\ u,v>0\text{ in }A,\qquad u=v=0 &\text{on }\partial A, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $A=\{x\in\mathbb R^{2m}:a<|x|<b\}$, $0<a<b$, $m\geq2$, and $2<p,q<2(m+1)/(m-1)$. We prove the existence of a family of solutions whose two components concentrate around the same $(m-1)$-dimensional sphere on the inner boundary as $\varepsilon\to0$. The two spheres of maxima are at distance $o(\varepsilon)$ from each other, and both components decay exponentially away from these spheres. The admissible range of $(p,q)$ includes critical and supercritical exponent pairs in dimension $2m$. The proof uses a reduction to a weighted system in dimension $m+1$. We establish foliated Schwarz symmetry of its ground states with a common axis via reduction by inversion and polarization. A uniform estimate on generalized Nehari fibers gives the upper energy bound. A half-space nonexistence result and the corresponding lower bound then determine the concentration location and the limiting profiles.
Finite-time blowup in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics model

We prove finite-time blowup of both the velocity and magnetic field in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) model starting from smooth odd initial data. The construction combines the dynamical rescaling approach with weighted stability estimates. Both the velocity and magnetic field remain in $L^2$ before the blowup time.
Distribution of Primes in Galois Extensions of Global Fields with Explicit Constant Terms

We study the distribution of primes among Frobenius conjugacy classes in finite Galois extensions of global fields. In earlier work, the author and Koyama proved that the existence and nonvanishing of the limit of partial Euler products on the critical line for Artin $L$-functions (the Deep Riemann Hypothesis (A), or DRH(A)) are equivalent to an asymptotic formula for weighted prime counting functions with an unspecified constant term. In this article, we prove that a refined asymptotic formula is equivalent to the full version of DRH, namely the convergence of the Euler products on the critical line (DRH(A)) and the determination of their limiting values (DRH(B)). Here, the constant term is given explicitly in terms of the residue of the zeta function, central derivatives of Artin $L$-functions, ramified primes, and higher prime-power contributions.
$G$-Hilbert schemes of canonical abelian quotient threefolds

Ishida and Iwashita showed that the canonical abelian quotient singularities of dimension three that are not Gorenstein fall into four families. For the two families that have not been treated before, we extend a method of Kędzierski and compute the toric charts of the $G$-Hilbert scheme explicitly. As a result, we show that the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities. Combined with known results, this shows that for every three-dimensional canonical abelian quotient singularity, the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities, every essential divisor over the singularity appears on it as a prime divisor, and its limit F-blowup is a resolution of the singularity. These results also hold for every three-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial canonical toric singularity in any characteristic, if we replace the $G$-Hilbert scheme by the limit F-blowup of the singularity.
Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for the Two-Dimensional Compressible Flow with General Bulk Viscosity
Xinyu Fan; Song Jiang; Jing Li; Boqiang Lv

The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with general density-dependent bulk viscosity is established for large initial data allowing vacuum. Both the periodic problem and the Cauchy problem with far-field vacuum are considered under a common logarithmic derivative bound and growth condition on the viscosity primitive. A time-independent density upper bound and uniform low-order estimates are obtained in both domains. The admissible coefficients include every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with logarithmic gains. Exponential relaxation to the positive equilibrium is proved in the periodic setting. In the whole space, uniform relaxation toward vacuum and algebraic decay of the pressure, velocity gradient, material acceleration, and relative kinetic energy are established.
Nonsense rank correlations between independent random walks

Yule's nonsense correlation persists for Spearman's rho and Kendall's tau between independent random walks. Neither coefficient concentrates at zero as the sample size grows. For centred random walks with finite increment variances, we derive a universal joint limit expressed through Brownian occupation functionals. Integral formulas give limiting variances of approximately 0.222 and 0.108, respectively, below the Pearson value of 0.241. Rank correlations thus reduce the limiting dispersion on their respective coefficient scales. We prove that both marginal limits have symmetric densities and represent them exactly as limits of polynomial densities determined by Gaussian moment integrals. Spearman's conventional t test and Kendall's normal approximation are asymptotically invalid, with rejection probabilities tending to one under process independence.
Stability threshold of Couette flow for two-dimensional MHD equations on the infinite channel
Jiahong Wu; Tianyuan Yu; Ning Zhu

In this paper, we study the stability threshold of the two-dimensional incompressible MHD equations near Couette flow and a constant horizontal magnetic field \((β,0)\) on \(\mathbb T\times\mathbb R\). For \(N>10\), \(0<ν,μ\le1\) and \(|β|\ge(ν+μ)/(3\sqrt{νμ})\), we prove global stability for initial perturbations of size \(δ_N\min\{ν,μ\}^{1/3}\) in \(H^N\), where \(δ_N>0\) is independent of \(ν,μ,β\). We also obtain enhanced dissipation of the nonzero horizontal modes on the time scale \(\min\{ν,μ\}^{-1/3}\), together with inviscid damping of the vertical components. The proof combines time-dependent Fourier multipliers with an energy correction constructed using the Alfvén oscillations. By combining the nonlinear terms arising from this correction, we obtain the cancellation needed to close the energy estimates at the $1/3$ scale.
Structure-Preserving Neural Time-Stepping for Gradient-Flow PDEs via Onsager's Variational Principle
Zhonghua Qiao; Xianmin Xu; Rukang You; Tao Zhou

We propose a unified Onsager-based neural time-stepping (ONTS) framework for solving gradient-flow partial differential equations with conserved and nonconserved dynamics. Unlike conventional neural time-stepping methods that directly parameterize the evolving state, the proposed framework employs spatial neural networks to approximate the Onsager process variables, namely, the rates in nonconserved systems and the fluxes in conserved systems. Within this Eulerian framework, we develop three complementary schemes: an explicit least-squares scheme (E-ONTS), an implicit variational scheme (I-ONTS), and a predictor--corrector scheme (PC-ONTS) that combines explicit prediction with safeguarded implicit correction. For conserved systems, the flux-based formulation guarantees discrete mass conservation under periodic or no-flux boundary conditions. Furthermore, we rigorously establish unconditional discrete energy stability for the implicit schemes, provided that a suitable descent criterion is satisfied, without requiring global minimization of the neural variational objective. Numerical experiments for the heat, Allen--Cahn, Cahn--Hilliard, Fokker--Planck, and coupled Poisson--Nernst--Planck equations demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and structure-preserving properties of the proposed framework.
Schauder bases and local unconditional structure in Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series
Tengfei Ma; Yufeng Lu; Chao Zu

We prove that among the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series with $1\le p<\infty$, only $\mathcal{H}^2$ has local unconditional structure. Consequently, $\mathcal{H}^p$ admits an unconditional basis exactly when $p=2$. At the endpoint $p=1$, we also construct a Schauder basis of Dirichlet polynomials and give an explicit formula for each basis vector. Together, these results answer the basis questions posed by Aleman, Olsen and Saksman, as well as the question of Saksman and Seip concerning an unconditional basis for $\mathcal{H}^1$.
A Staggered Discontinuous Galerkin Neural Network Method with a Computable Error Decomposition
Gung-Min Gie; Chang-Yeol Jung; Bongsuk Kwon; Kiwoong Kwon

We develop a staggered discontinuous Galerkin neural network (SDGNN) method for scalar elliptic problems with a computable error decomposition. The staggered discontinuous Galerkin (SDG) method requires only local continuity of its trial functions and gives a square, inf-sup stable system without stabilization parameters; we carry this structure over to neural networks. Networks defined on the patches of a staggered mesh satisfy the SDG continuity conditions for all values of the network parameters, and the loss is the squared dual norm of the SDG weak residual. We show that the loss is equivalent, with computable constants, to the square of the training error, the distance between the SDG projection of the network and the SDG finite element approximation, so that the full error is bounded by the discretization error, a multiple of the square root of the loss, and the network projection error. The weak residual requires no derivatives of the networks, the boundary and convection terms carry no penalty or stabilization weights, and the scalar trial functions may jump across the midlines of the primal cells. Numerical experiments show that the square root of the loss tracks the error during the training, that prescribed jumps across a square and a circular interface are captured consistently over the initializations, and that the method is more accurate than physics-informed neural networks at the same parameter counts.

Let $L=\{0,1,2,3,4,8\}$, associated with the large Witt design $S(5,8,24)$, and let $m(n,24,L)$ be the maximum size of a family of $24$-element subsets of an $n$-element set whose distinct members have intersection sizes in $L$. We prove that there are positive constants $c,C,n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, \[ cn^{316/63}\leq m(n,24,L)\leq Cn^{169/29}. \] We also obtain similar results for the systems associated with $S(4,7,23)$, $S(3,6,22)$, and $S(3,4,14)$. The upper bounds follow from a non-Shannon information inequality and disprove conjectures of Kupavskii and Terekhov. The lower bounds follow from an algebraic construction for arbitrary Steiner systems.
A compact non-Kähler shrinking Ricci soliton

We construct a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton on the simply-connected eight-manifold $\mathsf{SU}(3)\times_{\mathsf T^2}\mathbb{CP}^1$. This Riemannian manifold is not Einstein, is nowhere locally Kähler, is locally irreducible, and is invariant under the effective cohomogeneity one action of $\mathsf{PSU}(3)\times S^1$. This new gradient Ricci soliton is found by first constructing an approximate solution, certifying the residual, and applying a fixed-point theorem.
ECPack.wl: A Mathematica Package for Elliptic Curves over the Rationals and Finite Fields
B. Ananthanarayan; Darsh R. Bhatt; Parastoo Taghizadeh Asl

We present a Mathematica package entitled ECPack.wl, where we implement many important properties and commands relevant to the study of elliptic curves over the rationals and finite fields, namely $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $q=p^r$ and $p$ is prime. By streamlining the analysis of general elliptic curves and their transformations, ECPack.wl offers foundational computational tools for applications in high-energy physics, including elliptic Feynman integrals. This package significantly extends the functionalities of a package due to McGee in so far as we are able to study all versions of elliptic curves, such as the long Weierstrass, quartic and Legendre forms. We implement suitable transformations that are required for the general case, as well as those associated with fields of characteristic 2 and 3. Furthermore, the package computes many curve properties, such as point arithmetic, minimality checks, rank bounds and analytic rank, group structure, invariants, and the Weil and Tate pairings, over both $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_p$, as well as the Kodaira classification of the singular fibres of one-parameter families of elliptic curves, with the associated F-theory data. The package and its accompanying notebooks are available at https://github.com/DhamakedarDarsh/Mathematica-Code-and-worked-out-notebooks-for-Elliptic-Curves
Klein four slices of the representation suspensions of $H\underline{\mathbb{F}_2}$

We study the regular slice filtration of representation spheres $S^V\wedge H\underline{M}$. For every finite group $G$, we locate all slices in an explicit interval $[n(V),k(V)]$ and show that both endpoints occur. We introduce a \emph{defect vector} to measure a slice's failure. For the Klein four-group with $\underline{\mathbb F}_2$-coefficients, a balanced defect allows us to move $S^V\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ by certain $RO(G)$-graded cohomology classes to its $\dim V$-slice, which is again a representation sphere, while an odd defect obstructs any spherical slice. As an application, we obtain closed formulas for the bottom slice of $Σ^nH\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$ for every $n$, recovering the computation of Guillou and Yarnall by a different method. Along the way, we determine the complete slice tower of $S^{\inftyα_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ and consequently, the partial tower for $S^{nα_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$.
Fernando González del Cueto; Fernando Guevara Vasquez; Apratim Majumder; Rajesh Menon

We consider an optical system with a periodic point spread function, such as a camera with a periodic diffractive filter array placed near the sensor. Such systems produce a monochrome image that we call ``diffractogram'', and that multiplexes the spatial and spectral information about the scene. We present a method to efficiently invert this forward model and recover the hyperspectral scene. The inverse problem is formulated as a large scale $\ell_1$-penalized least squares problem that is solved iteratively with the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). A Krylov subspace solver, such as LSQR, may require tens to hundreds of iterations to approximatively solve the augmented least-squares problem required in each ADMM iteration. Here we present an exact direct solver for the augmented least-squares problems that exploits the periodicity of the point spread function. Each direct solve costs roughly as much as three LSQR iterations, eliminating inner iterations entirely. We validate the method on both synthetic and experimental datasets.
Limit theorems and bias correction for the initial-noise-adjusted SIML estimator

We propose a sine-based modification of the separating information maximum likelihood (SIML) estimator for integrated volatility and covariance under equidistant sampling with microstructure noise. The estimator allows for nonzero initial observation noise. We establish consistency under moment assumptions and asymptotic normality under first-order Malliavin regularity of the diffusion coefficients. We also construct a feasible noise-bias correction using an estimator of the unknown noise covariance. This correction permits wider spectral bandwidths for consistency and stable asymptotic normality.

Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on $n$ vertices with $e(G)=p\binom{n}{2}$ and $e(H)=q\binom{n}{2}$, where $p,q\in(0,1)$ are fixed. Bollobás and Scott studied intersections of two graphs under random relabelling and asked for the minimum $L^2$ norm of the deviation of their intersection size from its expected value. We answer this question by proving that, for graphs of order $n$ with fixed edge densities $p,q\in(0,1)$, the minimum is \begin{equation*} \left(\sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)q(1-q)}{2}\cdot\frac{1-\sqrt R}{1+\sqrt R}}\right)n+o(n), \end{equation*} where $R=\max\{p,1-p,q,1-q\}$. The coefficient of the linear term is best possible.
 Bollobás and Scott defined the positive and negative discrepancies of two hypergraphs as the largest deviations of their intersection size above and below its expected value under relabelling, respectively. They asked for the minimum product of the positive and negative discrepancies of two $(n/2)$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices with $\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ edges. We answer this question by proving that the minimum product of these discrepancies is $0$ if $4\mid\binom{n}{n/2}$ and $1/4$ otherwise.
Uniqueness for an inverse problem of determining orders and coefficients for multi-term time-fractional diffusion equation

This paper investigates a uniqueness problem for determining all fractional orders and their corresponding coefficients in multi-term time-fractional diffusion equations with Caputo derivatives in an abstract Hilbert space. The main result establishes that these parameters can be uniquely identified from a single scalar observation of the solution, of the form (u(t), phi), by comparing the solutions of two evolution equations governed by possibly different positive self-adjoint operators A and B. In contrast to existing results that rely on local space-time measurements and, in particular, may require the initial data to satisfy sign conditions and strong spatial regularity assumptions, our approach uses only the minimal assumption that a belongs to H, without imposing any sign or additional smoothness conditions on the initial value. The proof combines spectral representations of the solutions with a recursive asymptotic comparison method based on fundamental identities for the multinomial Mittag-Leffler function. This approach enables the successive identification of all fractional orders and their associated coefficients, even when the two equations involve different operators. Furthermore, the uniqueness argument extends to multi-term time-fractional wave equations with orders in the interval (1,2).
Global existence of an initial boundary value problem for the Einstein equation via a Hamiltonian approach

The global existence of the initial boundary value problem for the Einstein equation in \((2+1)\)-dimension with totally geodesic timelike boundary is proved by a Hamiltonian approach. The initial boundary value problem is formulated within the framework of the ADM formalism, and the ADM reduction is carried out under the constant mean curvature spatial harmonic gauge. Deriving energy estimates for the flows in the reduced phase space shows the global existence.
Freidlin-Wentzell exit-laws for a stochastic Cucker-Smale model
Hetranso Ahni; Jean-François Jabir; Julian Tugaut

This paper investigates the exit-time asymptotics, at a vanishing noise limit, related to a stochastic particles system in mean-field interaction subjected to frictions, confining potential and flocking forces. The dynamics are governed by a kinetic Langevin-type SDE with an idiosyncratic noise acting solely on the velocity coordinates. Using the seminal large deviations principles of Freidlin and Wentzell [20], and their extension by Azencott [4] to the framework of non-elliptic diffusions, we establish the Arrhenius' law and Kramers' type law related to the first exit-time of the system from an energy level set $\mathcal O^γ_N(R)$ of interest.
Effects of elasticity on the stability of viscoelastic boundary layers
Shengxin Li; Dehua Wang; Feng Xie; Zhu Zhang

The elastic effect on the stability of boundary layers is studied for incompressible elastic fluids in the half-plane. It is known from [33] that if the deformation tensor matrix is nonsingular near the boundary, elasticity can prevent the formation of a boundary layer. In this paper, we prove stability properties when the deformation tensor degenerates. Our results are twofold: (1) when the first row of the deformation tensor has a non-degenerate projection onto a fixed direction, the initial-boundary value problem for the two-dimensional viscoelastic Prandtl boundary layer equations in the half-plane admits local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces, without any monotonicity condition on the velocity profile; (2) when the first row of the deformation tensor vanishes simultaneously at one point, the linearized Prandtl boundary layer system is ill-posed. The first result reveals the stabilizing effect of elasticity against the classical Prandtl instability. The second result shows that elastic effects cannot suppress the Prandtl-type instability associated with a non-degenerate critical point of the velocity profile.
Degenerate Preconditioned Proximal Point Algorithms as Forward Methods for Nonmonotone Inclusions

We study degenerate preconditioned proximal point algorithms (PPPA) for finding zeros of nonmonotone set-valued operators in Hilbert spaces under solution-relative $(U,V)$-semimonotonicity, with possibly indefinite $U$ and $V$. With a closed-range preconditioner $P$, the reduced PPPA dynamics admit a forward representation through the complementary resolvent of a parallel composition, without requiring monotonicity or admissibility. Relative semimonotonicity of the range-restricted operator transfers to the reduced forward map, allowing our forward theory for possibly set-valued mappings to yield Fejér estimates and residual rates. Under suitable conditions, including demiclosedness of the reduced map at zero, the projected PPPA iterates and shadows converge weakly to a common projected zero. Without demiclosedness, a counterexample shows that the projected sequences may converge to a point outside the projected zero set, even when the original operator is continuous. Bounded recovery condition yields weak convergence of the full (non-projected) shadows. The monotonicity modulus $U$ yields additional results: under suitable conditions, $U\succeqτP$ with $τ>0$ gives strong and linear convergence of the projected PPPA sequences, while $U\succeq-σP$ with $0\leσ<1/2$ still permits local linear rates under metric subregularity. These strong convergence and linear rate guarantees extend to the full shadows when a Lipschitz recovery estimate holds, such as when $U$ is strongly monotone on $\ker P$. For Chambolle--Pock and Douglas--Rachford splitting, we establish Lipschitz recovery even when $U=0$ by exploiting the primal--dual structure. Under suitable parameter conditions, full-shadow convergence guarantees, including $R$-linear rates, extend to the original PPPA iterates.
Postselection on Halting and Reductions to the Halting Problem

A probabilistic Turing machine is an ordinary Turing machine that may also toss fair coins, with no limit on its running time or memory. If it always halts, it decides only computable problems. Aaronson et al. studied machines that may run forever on some coin tosses, with the answer read only from the runs that halt. Suppose the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one. They showed that these machines decide exactly the problems solvable with a fixed list of questions about the halting problem. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be the more likely one. We show that the machines then decide exactly the problems solvable by asking such questions one after another, each chosen after the earlier answers. We also show that the factor two can be replaced by any fixed factor greater than one. A machine may promise two numbers: a lower bound on its probability of halting, and a lower bound on its probability of being right when it halts. From these two numbers we compute exactly how many questions fixed in advance the machine can replace. The main idea is that probability acts as a budget for how often a computable guess may change its mind. The results extend to oracle machines and to machines nested inside each other. Quantum machines decide the same problems.
Lieb-Robinson Bounds for Electric Quantum Walks
Houssam Abdul-Rahman; Christopher Cedzich; Günter Stolz

We derive Lieb-Robinson type bounds with optimal propagation velocity for shift-coin and split-step quantum walks in rational electric fields. The velocity decays exponentially fast in the period of the field, showing long intervals of suppressed spreading. The proof rests on bounds for the imaginary part of the analytically continued dispersion relation of the electric walk. We show that the infimal Lieb-Robinson velocity coincides with the asymptotic velocity for these walks, while a nonhomogeneous example demonstrates that the two types of velocity need not agree in general. We also obtain an exponential tail estimate on the probability of a walk to lie outside the effective light cone.
Optimal Dynamic Quantizers for Periodically Time-Varying Systems via Cyclic Reformulation

This paper addresses the design of optimal dynamic quantizers for discrete-time linear periodically time-varying (LPTV) plants with discrete-valued inputs. Optimal dynamic quantizers, which minimize the worst-case output error caused by quantization, are well established for linear time-invariant (LTI) plants, whereas the corresponding design for plants with periodically time-varying dynamics has not been addressed. For square LPTV plants having relative degree one at every time phase, this paper derives an optimal periodic dynamic quantizer in closed form. The quantizer is constructed by applying the LTI theory to the cycled plant obtained by cyclic reformulation and reading off its periodic coefficient matrices block by block; its optimality is then verified directly, showing that it attains a performance lower bound determined by the largest instantaneous input-to-output gain over the time phases. The worst-case output error of general periodic dynamic quantizers is also characterized. The optimal quantizer is shown to be stable if and only if all invariant zeros of the cycled plant lie in the open unit disk, which is the condition that governs stable causal inversion of LPTV plants. A numerical example with comparisons to conventional quantizers illustrates the results.
Decomposition Bounds for MCMC with Mixture Targets: Multimodality and Heavy-Tailedness

We establish quantitative mixing-time bounds for Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms targeting multimodal and heavy-tailed mixtures. The dynamics of a Markov chain are decomposed into local and global levels, and possibly weak Poincaré inequalities at both levels are combined to form convergence bounds. We apply this framework to location and scale mixtures of strongly log-concave distributions, obtaining explicit convergence bounds for random-walk Metropolis, proximal, and random-scan Gibbs samplers. For location mixtures connected along a finite path, the bounds depend polynomially on the number of components and exponentially on neighboring separation, remaining informative as the overall diameter grows. For scale mixtures, we relate the global dynamics of the chain to the isoperimetry of the log-scale mixing distribution, and illustrate the effect of heavy-tailed targets by examining inverse-gamma mixing distributions.
A bound-preserving hybrid lattice Boltzmann method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws

Solutions to scalar hyperbolic conservation laws may develop discontinuities within finite time even from smooth initial data, while higher-order lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods tend to generate non-physical oscillations and out-of-bounds behavior near steep gradients. To address this issue, we first construct a first-order LB method with the upwind-type equilibrium distribution functions under the \(DdQ(2d+1)\) lattice structure, and establish its bound-preserving (BP) conditions. We then develop a second-order multiple-relaxation-time LB (MRT-LB) method by introducing the auxiliary source distribution functions, and analyze its \(L^2\) stability. Building on these, we propose a hybrid LB method that preserves the collision-streaming structure, by conservatively mixing first- and second-order updates through a convex constraint mechanism. We further establish the global BP (GBP), local BP (LBP), and relaxed LBP (RLBP) limiters in the hybrid LB method, together with the associated macroscopic BP constraints. Numerical experiments examine the convergence order, interface capturing performance, and discontinuity resolution capability of the proposed BP hybrid LB method. The results indicate that it effectively suppresses out-of-bounds behavior in the second-order LB method and reduces numerical dissipation in the first-order LB method, while maintaining the prescribed bounds and discrete mass conservation.
A proof of a conjecture on bipartite correspondence packing

A correspondence cover assigns a set of possible colors to each vertex of a graph. For each edge, a matching between the two endpoint color sets specifies the forbidden color pairs. A correspondence coloring selects one color at each vertex so that no forbidden pair is selected. A full correspondence packing is a collection of such colorings that uses every color at each vertex exactly once.
 We prove a conjecture of Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, and Kang [Random Structures & Algorithms 64 (2024), 62--93]. For every sufficiently large $D$, there is a positive integer $k(D)=(1+o(1))D/\log D$ such that every correspondence cover of any finite bipartite graph has a full correspondence packing if each color has at most $D$ forbidden partners and each vertex has $k(D)$ colors. More precisely, we prove this conclusion with \[
 k(D)=\left\lceil\frac{D}{\log D-2\log\log D-6}\right\rceil \] for every integer $D\ge\lceil e^{20}\rceil$.
Quantitative homogenization of $k$-Hessian equations in periodic media
Tianling Jin; YanYan Li; Hung V. Tran; Xushan Tu

Let $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the $k$-admissible solutions of $σ_k(D^2u^\varepsilon)=f(x,x/\varepsilon)$ and $σ_k(D^2u)=\overline f(x)$ on a bounded convex domain $Ω$, with the same Dirichlet data. Here, $f$ is uniformly positive and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline f(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}f(x,y)dy$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<α\leq1$, we prove $\|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+α}$ for all $0<\varepsilon\leq1$, provided that $u\in C^{m+2,α}(\overlineΩ)$ and $f\in C_x^{m,α}(\overlineΩ;C_y^{2,γ}(\mathbb T^n))$ for some $0<γ<1$. Periodic cell estimates give smooth dependence of the correctors on the background Hessian and the normalized density. The divergence-free property of the Newton tensor cancels the first macroscopic correction and yields the higher rate. Both exponents are optimal in general, already for $n=k=1$.
Scale profile, nesting, and the $A_2$ growth of dyadic paraproducts

For the dyadic paraproduct $π_b$ and $Q\ge1$, let $Φ_b(Q)$ be the supremum of $\|π_b\|_{L^2(w)}$ over dyadic weights with $[w]_{A_2^d}\le Q$. Beznosova's linear bound $Φ_b(Q)\lesssim Q\,\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_d}$ is sharp over $\mathrm{BMO}_d$, while every nonzero symbol safisfies $Φ_b(Q)\gtrsim Q^{1/2}$. We ask which properties of a fixed symbol place its growth between these extremes, and identify two: the distribution of the Haar coefficients of $b$ over scales and the nesting of their supports. Symbols supported on $L$ consecutive scales obey a two-weight bound of order $\sqrt L$; as a consequence, polynomial decay of the scale tails determines the sharp trowth exponent, except at a critical rate where the growth is determined up to a factor $(\log Q)^{1/2}$. For symbols supported on a chain, $\sup_Q Q^{-1/2}Φ_b(Q)$ is comarable to $\|S_d b\|_{\infty}$, and for every symbol the boundedness of the dyadic square function $S_d b$ is necessary for minimal growth $Q^{1/2}$. Conversely, $Φ_b(Q)\lesssim Q^{3/4}\|S_d b\|_{\infty}$ for every symbol, and the bound $\|π_b\|_{L^2(w)}\lesssim [w]_{A_2^d}^{1/2}\|S_d b\|_{i\infty}$ holds for every symbol at weights whose local $A_2$ imbalance has bounded evergy off a family of dyadic chains with disjoint tops; this class contains all weights used in our lower bounds.
Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures

In Eliashberg theory of phonon-mediated superconductivity with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential, the critical temperature $T_c$ marks the linear instability of the normal state. Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan (KAY) characterized it through the top eigenvalue of a compact operator on Matsubara-frequency sequences. They proved that $T_c$ is unique at strong coupling and conjectured $T_c<C(λ\langleω^2\rangle)^{1/2}$ for every coupling $λ$, with $\langleω^2\rangle$ the second moment of the normalized phonon spectrum and $C\approx0.1827$ sharp, a bound Leavens stated in 1977 on partly numerical grounds. A preprint by Kondratev, not yet peer reviewed, gives a proof of this bound and of all-coupling uniqueness. We give an independent proof, for every spectrum with finite second moment, based on a comparison principle that is also Kondratev's central step and was proved to first order by Bergmann and Rainer: strengthening the pairing interaction at every Matsubara transfer, strictly at the smallest one, strictly raises the top eigenvalue. At fixed $λ$ and $\langleω^2\rangle$ a single Einstein mode maximizes $T_c$. Convexity of the top eigenvalue in the spectrum gives sharp bounds on $T_c$ by the moments $\intω^nα^2F dω$, $0\le n\le1$, including Leavens's zeroth-moment bound $T_c\le c_0\intα^2F dω$, $c_0\approx0.231$ numerically, optimal at moderate coupling. All bounds persist under a Coulomb pseudopotential with symmetric cutoff. A prefix decomposition of non-increasing vectors proves a third KAY conjecture, not treated in the preprint.
