Thus we introduce and investigate the \emph{contingent HOD dichotomy}, according to which either (1) the set-theoretic universe V is close to HOD by forcing---HOD is a ground, V = HOD is forceable, the universe is ordinal-definable from a set parameter $V=\text{HOD}_b$, the blurry HOD hierarchy collapses to kappa-HOD for some cardinal kappa, and furthermore these features are invariant by forcing and hold throughout the generic multiverse; or (2) the universe V is far from HOD by forcing in all those respects, so $V\neq\text{HOD}$, but also HOD is not a ground, V = HOD is not forceable, the set-theoretic universe is not ordinal-definable from a set, the universe is not kappa-HOD for any kappa, and these features hold invariantly throughout the generic multiverse. We investigate the nature of the dichotomy in connection with large cardinals, with set-theoretic geology, with the iterated $\text{HOD}^α$ classes, and with the maximality principles MP and MP(R), showing generally that both prongs of the dichotomy occur with diverse set-theoretic phenomena.
Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth

We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group.
 As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities.
 Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.
Bellman Residual Bracketing: Resolving the Sample Complexity of Discounted and Average-Reward RL

We study the sample complexity of the empirical planning or plug-in approach for reinforcement learning (RL) with a generative model. We show the discounted plug-in approach finds an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy with $O(SA (1-γ)^{-3} \varepsilon^{-2} \log(SA/δ))$ samples, where $S, A, γ, δ$ are the state and action sizes, discount factor, and failure probability, respectively. In the average-reward setting, we show that discounted plug-in and direct (undiscounted) plug-in achieve $O(SAH\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ and $O(SAD\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ complexities, respectively, where $H$ upper-bounds the optimal bias span and $D$ is the diameter. Combining with our lower bounds for nonadaptive generative models, these results resolve the minimax sample complexity of discounted RL and average-reward RL --- in both the span- and diameter-based classes --- up to constant factors. Our main technical contribution is a novel Bellman residual bracketing technique which improves the efficiency of prior absorbing-MDP-based concentration analyses.
Conditional Stochastic User Equilibrium as a Gibbs Distribution: Tractable Flow Laws and Exact Path-Free Sampling

Treating traffic counts as data calls for the joint distribution of link flows. Stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) gives a single flow vector, and independent route choice at fixed probabilities ignores congestion feedback between travelers. Conditional stochastic user equilibrium (CSUE), in which each traveler of a finite population chooses a route by logit conditional on the routes of all others, contains this feedback but has been hard to compute with at scale. Under separable link costs and a common route-choice precision, the CSUE conditionals are those of a unique Gibbs distribution whose energy is a left-endpoint discrete congestion potential, and for continuous nondecreasing costs the law concentrates on deterministic logit SUE in the large-population limit. When the routes of each origin are the paths of an acyclic bush, retaining origin- or OD-level labels gives an unnormalized layered link-flow law with an explicit product-form multiplicity. On this representation we build a block Metropolis-Hastings sampler whose proposal is an integer version of Dial's loading under frozen costs. It leaves the CSUE law on the bush route sets invariant without enumerating paths or storing individual routes, and at stationarity the mean rejection rate of a block lies between one and two times the total variation distance between its proposal and exact conditional. In experiments, the sampler reproduces reference laws from exact enumeration and traveler-level Gibbs sampling, whereas independent route choice at frozen costs reproduces mean flows but overstates link-flow standard deviations by up to 48% and distorts correlations. On Sioux Falls, the block sampler attains 76.1 times the minimum effective sample size per CPU second of traveler-level Gibbs sampling, and on Chicago Sketch, with over one million travelers, its sampled covariance is used to assess traffic-count locations.
We prove Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the 2D Toda model and solutions of the Ernst equation, using the Pfaffian solutions obtained in our previous work arXiv:2610.27420.
An Explicit Version of Serre's Open Image Theorem for Galois Number Fields
Clifford J Rodrigues; Debargha Banerjee; Krishna Kishore; Sunil Kumar Mallick

In 1971, Serre showed that the mod $p$ Galois representation associated to a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field is surjective for all but finitely many primes $p$. That is, there exists a constant $c(E,K)$, for $E$ a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field $K$, such that $ρ_{E,p}:\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \mathrm{Aut}(E[p])$ is surjective for all primes $p>c(E,K)$. We give a bound for this constant using an effective version of the Faltings isogeny theorem for specific number fields. We show that, for $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ with $|D|<50$ and $K$ a formally real number field, given a non-CM elliptic curve $E$ over $K$ we have $c(E,K)\le 2C_1(K)\log N_{K/\mathbb Q}\operatorname{rad}\left( 2\mathcal O_K\mathfrak N_{E}\right )+2 C_2(K)$, where $\mathfrak N_E$ denotes the conductor ideal of $E$, and the constants $C_1(K)$ and $C_2(K)$ can be described explicitly. We also show that for primes greater than this bound, the image cannot be contained in the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup. This works for any Galois number field. Our proof assumes the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).
Counterexamples to Strichartz estimates for general irrotational compressible Euler backgrounds and positive estimates for a spherical isotropic background solution

We consider the free boundary problem for the irrotational compressible Euler equation in a physical vacuum setting. By using the irrotationality condition in the Eulerian formulation of Ifrim and Tataru, we previously showed that the problem can be rephrased in terms of the velocity potential function as an acoustic wave equation that turns out to be widely used in solar seismology. This paper is another step towards understanding what Strichartz estimates are achievable for the aforementioned equation. Our object of study is the corresponding linearized problem. In a previous work, we constructed a class of gallery modes in a model stationary case, which turned out to be counterexamples to Strichartz estimates, forcing a loss of derivatives. By a careful regularization of the domain defining function, we transplant these counterexamples to general Euler backgrounds, and obtain general counterexamples in the same range. On the other hand, we also prove that for the background corresponding to a concrete affine isotropic spherical solution for the irrotational compressible Euler equations, one has Strichartz estimates up to the aforementioned threshold, which shows that they are optimal for at least some explicit Euler backgrounds. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first results of this kind for explicit solutions of the irrotational compressible Euler equations in a physical vacuum.
Determinateness in a classical theory of nonclassical truth

Recent theories that take determinateness as primitive are either nonclassical theories of nonclassical truth, like Field's INT, or classical theories of classical truth, like Fujimoto and Halbach's CD and CD^+. This paper develops a third option: a classical theory of nonclassical truth. The theory, KFDcs, extends the Kripke-Feferman theory KFcs with a primitive determinateness predicate. Unlike CD^+, KFDcs keeps the iteration of truth unrestricted and gives up its completeness. With or without a consistency axiom, KFD is proof-theoretically equivalent to the theory \widehat{ID}_2 of twice iterated fixed points, with ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}({\varepsilon}_0, 0)0), thus stronger than CD^+. It is also shown that replacing full induction with internal induction yields ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}(ω, 0)0), and restricting internal induction to total formulae yields {\varphi}({\varepsilon_0},0), the ordinal of KF.
Sharp condition for the existence of wave operators

We study the wave operators for a Jacobi matrix whose spectral measure satisfies the Szegő condition. We formulate a sufficient condition in terms of the associated Verblunsky parameters and show that it is sharp.

We construct sets of $1104$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $5744$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$, each containing no three distinct collinear points. A reflection lift sends the Calderbank--Fishburn $236$-cap to a cap with three parallel layers of sizes $512,80,512$; both outer layers are linearly equivalent to the FunSearch $512$-cap. A coordinate substitution in Hill's $112$-cap uses replacement sets of sizes $80,32,32$ for the three values of one scalar coordinate. Assigning the $80$-point set to a noncentral $45$-point section gives $5744$, gaining $240$ points over the $5504$ construction obtained from a central $40$-point section.
Func-JEPA: Learning a Sobolev Space of Functions as Latent Vectors

Pretraining an encoder once and reusing it across tasks is a widespread approach in vision and language. However, neural symbolic mathematics still trains a dedicated sequence-to-sequence model for each task, so that no representation of a function is shared. In this work, we propose the Function Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Func-JEPA, abbreviated f-JEPA): an encoder of mathematical functions, pretrained on their symbolic form, whose latent space imitates the Sobolev space H^1 and in which differentiation is a learned latent operator. The norm of a latent is computed exactly from the function, whereas its direction is learned to match Sobolev angles. The frozen encoder is then reused by lightweight modules for decoding, composition, integration, and regression from samples. The representation and four downstream tasks are evaluated within and outside the pretraining distribution. f-JEPA recovers exact formulas from noisy samples more often than the compared symbolic-regression methods, whereas computer algebra and task-specific models remain stronger on standard integration and differential-equation benchmarks.
Second-Order Threshold and Value Asymptotics in Multiple-Stopping Secretary Problems
José María Grau Ribas; Raúl Sánchez Galán

We study the classical secretary problem with a fixed number of selection opportunities. We derive explicit corrections to the limiting thresholds and to the optimal success probability. A cancellation identity removes the influence of later threshold rounding from the first correction, while a Poisson representation explains its probabilistic meaning. Every bounded rounding of the limiting thresholds shares the first value correction. We obtain integer rounding laws, eventual threshold identities along continued-fraction convergents, and joint rounding frequencies. Rigorous rational bounds show that the first eleven corrections are positive and the twelfth is negative, producing the first shifted convergent identity.
Chang's Omitting Types Theorem in Lukasiewicz Logic

We prove Chang-style omitting types theorems for standard first-order Lukasiewicz logic. Starting from a prescribed model $M$, we obtain an extension that omits higher-complexity types while preserving lower-level types already realized in $M$. If $T$ is a $Π_{n+2}$-theory, every model of $T$ has an exact extension that preserves its realized $Σ_{n+1}$-types and omits every $Σ_{n+2}$-type not generated by a $Σ_{n+1}$-type. An iterated construction also omits infinity-universal types, whose unbounded quantifier complexity cannot eventually be generated by the corresponding lower-complexity fragments of a single type. The main tool is a refinement of Robinson's infinite forcing sensitive to the quantifier complexity of formulas.
Rodrigo Bañuelos; Mähdi Hormozi; Alexander Volberg

For $1\le p\le2$, we obtain the sharp weak-type $(p,p)$ inequality for each classical Riesz transform on real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^n$, with the same optimal constant as for the Hilbert transform. The proof combines the Bellman function method of \cite{BHV} with Janakiraman's sharp strip potential \cite{Janakiraman}.
On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
Duc An Phan; Tuan Anh Dao

In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $σ$-evolution equation $$u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-Δ)^σu+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(τ)/b(τ) dτ$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(τ)/b(τ)dτ\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.
Geometrically formal Hermitian metrics on compact complex surfaces

We classify compact complex surfaces admitting either a geometrically Dolbeault formal or an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric. Furthermore, we prove that on a compact Kähler surface, every ABC-geometrically formal metric is Kähler, whereas, for geometrically Dolbeault formal Hermitian metrics, Gauduchon, LCK, and Kähler conditions are equivalent. On non-Kähler surfaces, an ABC-geometrically formal Hermitian metric is LCK and, except on Inoue surfaces, Vaisman.
Edgeworth expansion on sums of Wiener chaos

In this paper, we study Edgeworth expansions for random variables belonging to a fixed finite sum of Wiener chaoses. Building on the work of Mansanarez, Poly and Swan (arXiv:2510.14002) for a single Wiener chaos, we investigate the extension of their approach to functionals $F$ living in a finite sum of Wiener chaoses $\mathcal{W}_{\leq d}$. Within the Malliavin--Stein framework, we bound the total variation distance between the law of $F$ and its Edgeworth approximation of order $2dm$ by $(\sum_{p,q}^d \operatorname{Var}Γ(F_p,F_q))^{m/2}(\operatorname{Var}Γ(F,\operatorname{L}^{-1}F))^{1/2}$, where $F_p$ denotes the projection of $F$ onto the $p$-th Wiener chaos. The presence of several chaotic components introduces additional interactions, since these components are orthogonal but generally dependent. Since our proof relies on the integration-by-parts formalism and the spectral properties of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator, this result extends naturally to the broader framework of Markov chaoses.
A note on distributive lattices with a commutative generalized implication

We study distributive lattices with an ideal-valued generalized implication satisfying a commutativity identity. This class extends commutative weak Heyting algebras by allowing implication values to be non-principal ideals. We characterize its intersection with several known classes of gi-lattices, study gi-deductive systems and their relationship with gi-filters and gi-congruences, and extend the relational characterization of commutativity to this setting. The resulting correspondence yields a Priestley-style duality by restricting the established duality for gi-lattices.
Equilibrium measures for anisotropic exponential interaction energies with applications to transformers
Oleksii Kachaiev; Martin Burger; Samira Kabri; Yury Korolev; Tim Roith

We study the minimization of anisotropic exponential interaction energies over probability measures on the sphere, motivated by mean-field models of self-attention in transformer architectures. For every symmetric positive definite interaction matrix, we relate the minimizer to a corresponding anisotropic Brownian motion and use the Feynman--Kac formula and elliptic regularity theory to show that it admits a smooth, strictly positive density on the sphere. We further show that it is the only stationary measure with full support for the dynamics considered. We use the stochastic viewpoint to derive an algorithm for sampling from the minimizer. In dimension two, we also propose a numerical scheme for approximating its density based on a Mathieu series expansion.
Renormalization Group Flow from 4d Chern-Simons Theory

The four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory coupled with surface defects is known to realize two-dimensional integrable quantum field theories (QFTs). We discuss the renormalization group (RG) flow of such two-dimensional integrable QFTs from first-principles Feynman diagram computations intrinsically in the four-dimensional framework. We first derive the one-loop RG flow of two-dimensional QFTs realized by the four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory on $Σ\times C$ coupled with the order surface defects supported on $Σ$. Here, the affine Kac-Moody symmetry of the defects underlies the one-loop RG flow. We then derive the one-loop RG flow of the principal chiral model (PCM) without Wess-Zumino term, which is realized using disorder surface defects, within the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. We obtain the nontrivial one-loop RG flow of the PCM, reproducing its known asymptotically-free beta function, using two complementary methods: by explicitly evaluating one-loop Feynman amplitudes, and by computing an analogue of analytic torsion for four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory.

Recovering dynamical equations from data is a central problem in nonlinear science. In practice, measurements are corrupted by noise and often contain fast oscillations that are not part of the slow dynamics of interest. For this reason, data are typically pre-processed before model recovery or classsification. Here, we reveal the effects of filtering, a specific denoising technique, on recovery. Our analysis show that equation discovery performed on filtered data recovers, up to a fixed precision, the normal-form (effective) equations rather than the original system.
Homomorphisms between Weyl modules for $\mathrm{GL}_3$ in characteristic $2$

We classify the homomorphism spaces between Weyl modules for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. We prove that these spaces have dimension at most one and give an explicit recursive procedure that determines when they are nonzero and constructs generators in terms of semistandard tableaux. As a consequence, we determine the dimensions of certain homomorphism spaces between Specht modules in characteristic $2$.
An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant

The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$.
Yang He; Artan Sheshmani; Shing-Tung Yau

We study regularized quantum periods under birational contractions involving threefold flips. Let $g:X \dashrightarrow X'$ be a birational map between Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities which contracts exactly one prime divisor $E$ and extracts no divisor. We prove that
 $$
 \lim_{r \rightarrow +\infty}\widehat{G}_{X,rE}(t) =\widehat{G}_{X'}(t).
 $$
 The proof uses logarithmically smooth degenerations and positive discrepancies on good resolutions. Compatibility with orbifold invariants is proved using successive quotient-point extractions and the two-component orbifold degeneration formula.
 We also define stationary descendant invariants of projective terminal Fano threefolds by good resolutions and prove compatibility with a given projective $\mathbb{Q}$-smoothing. The period comparison extends to projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano endpoints under the same hypothesis on the birational map. Its proof compares the endpoints on a common resolution.
Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials

We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fréchet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

We investigate vacuum black-hole solutions in metric-affine Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity (MG-I), where $R$ is the affine Ricci scalar and $T$ is a quadratic torsion invariant, not the trace of the matter energy-momentum tensor. For the polynomial model $F(R,T)=αR+βT+γT^3$, with $α\neq0$, we first vary the metric and all components of the independent affine connection, and only then specialize to metric-compatible geometry with totally antisymmetric torsion. Nonzero axial torsion admits an exceptional branch $α+β+3γT_*^2=0$, on which the metric satisfies the Einstein equations with effective cosmological parameter $Λ_*=γT_*^3/α$. We establish a local existence result and construct torsionful Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter representatives that are smooth through a selected future Killing horizon. Within the spherically symmetric axial ansatz, we characterize Ricci-symmetric affine connections by the condition $(fV-U)'=0$ and compare a constant-$W=fV-U$ family with a constant-$U$ family. Although these connections share the same metric and torsion scalar, their affine curvature invariants generally differ. Independent coordinate-level curvature contractions and component tests of the unrestricted metric and connection variations corroborate the identities used in the construction; these checks complement the analytic variational derivation. Finally, we identify null directions of the restricted axial quadratic form and distinguish this degeneracy from a complete metric-affine stability analysis. Our conclusions are local and do not establish global extendibility, physical inequivalence of all torsion profiles, or dynamical stability.
Asymptotic Divergence-Based Monitoring for Data Drift in Production AI Systems: A Discrete Case Approach

We develop a complete asymptotic theory for monitoring data drift in production artificial intelligence (AI) systems whose inputs take values in a finite set of categories. The framework combines two complementary inferential tools. Under the no-drift hypothesis $H_0$, the two-sample likelihood-ratio statistic $G$ of Wilks follows a universal Chi_{r-1}^2 law, independently of the divergence chosen and of the sample sizes; the calibrated Population Stability Index (PSI) of Yurdakul and Naranjo (2021) shares the same Chi_{r-1}^2 limit and is asymptotically equivalent to the $G$-test under $H_0$. Under the drift hypothesis $H_1$, the plug-in phi-divergence is asymptotically normal with a variance computed in closed form for the one-sample, two-sample and symmetrized configurations, yielding standardized $Z$-statistics, detection boundaries, power functions and sample-size planning rules. We supply a per-category decomposition that localizes the drift on specific categories, a Benjamini--Hochberg procedure for monitoring many features simultaneously, and an explicit comparison with the heuristic PSI cut-offs of industrial practice. Two fully worked simulation examples - one one-sample with the Rényi divergence and multiple testing, one two-sample with the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and sample-size planning - illustrate every notion of the paper on realistic production data.
Maximality of the Došen--Petrić Boolean Category

We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two morphisms differ. Composition with morphisms selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables is a preorder. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.
Quaternion Matrix Tuples with Common Invariant Subspaces: Dimension and Nonuniqueness
Cailing Yao; Bingzhe Hou; Yang Zhang

Let $M_n(\mathbb{H})$ denote the algebra of $n\times n$ quaternion matrices. We study common invariant right subspaces of tuples in $M_n(\mathbb{H})^r$ and determine exact real semialgebraic dimensions for two associated sets. If $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ are positive integers, $n=n_1+\cdots+n_s$, and $q=\sum_{1\leq a<b\leq s}n_an_b$, the set of tuples preserving at least one nested chain with successive increments $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)q$. For $r\geq2$ and $1\leq k<n$, the set of tuples with at least two distinct common $k$-dimensional right invariant subspaces has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)(k(n-k)+n-1)$. The proofs use finite right-module coordinates and a common local-rank argument.
Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
Daniele Garrisi; Alessandro Portaluri; Li Wu

We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining scalar spectral flow on fixed spaces with overgroup nullities, we bound the number of bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and singular ambient endpoints, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. Finite Morse index reduces the inputs to indices and nullities; extensions cover varying form domains and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems.
 For a Newtonian nine-body family containing a reported counterexample to Moeckel's stability conjecture, we prove analytically that two nonconjugate exact reflection types bifurcate at a common central mass, displacing the central body. Positivity excludes larger stabilizers, while a scalar Schur complement synchronizes the bifurcations, independently of the reported stability assertion.
Ship-as-a-buoy for Phase-resolved Reconstruction of Surface Waves
Yifan Du; Guangyao Wang; Yulin Pan

We develop a data assimilation framework to address the ``ship-as-a-buoy'' problem, i.e., estimation of the wave field from time series of ship motion. Unlike previous algorithms which only provide information of wave spectrum, our approach reconstructs the instantaneous phase-resolved wave field. The full framework includes two steps: the first step to generate an initial (rough) estimation of the wave field using the response-amplitude-operators (RAOs), and the second step to refine the reconstruction using an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) to incorporate the measured motion time series. Together with EnKF in the second step, we model the coupled wave-ship dynamics by a high-order spectral (HOS) method for waves and a Cummins equation for ship motion (although higher-fidelity ship model can be applied). We conduct extensive tests of our method for the case with one ship, and the naturally extended cases with multiple ships or with uncertain parameters in the ship motion model. For all test cases we demonstrate favorable reconstruction of the wave field, which in general further improves with the number of ships available and with uncertain parameters properly estimated. We also provide insights on the successful reconstruction in terms of ensemble correlations between the motion time series and features of the wave field.
Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
Andreas A. Buchheit; Torsten Keßler; Sergej Rjasanow

We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $ν>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of $1.5\times10^{-13}$ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.
Computing rare events in Lévy-driven systems via optimal control

We extend the optimal control formulation of sample path large deviation theory, which has proven effective for numerical computation of instantons and sharp probability estimates in stochastic differential equations with Gaussian noise, to systems with light-tailed Lévy noise. In the scaling limit of small jumps and high intensity, such systems satisfy a large deviation principle of Freidlin-Wentzell type, with a running cost given by the Legendre transform of the noise cumulant generating function. We propose to numerically minimize this cost over noise realizations subject to the system dynamics, which yields the instanton without having to solve Hamilton's equations, and naturally handles degenerate and multiplicative noise. When the cumulant generating function has a bounded domain, the cost grows only linearly for large noise, and instantons can contain jumps. We analyze when jumps are not only admissible but optimal, depending on the subleading behavior of the cost and on the drift, and show how jumps can be resolved numerically through a time reparameterization that freezes physical time. For continuous instantons, we derive Riccati and Fredholm determinant expressions for the leading-order prefactor, and we discuss the modifications needed when the instanton jumps. We illustrate and validate our methods against Monte Carlo simulations in several examples: a two-dimensional nonlinear model, an active run-and-tumble particle with non-Gaussian tumbling noise, and the Ghil-Sellers energy balance climate model with Lévy-perturbed solar forcing.
Local asymptotic normality for Cox-Ingersoll-Ross drift parameters under high-frequency sampling and the strict Feller condition

For the ergodic Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) diffusion with known diffusion scale and a fixed initial value, we prove local asymptotic normality (LAN) of the exactly sampled experiment for the drift parameters whenever the Feller index exceeds $1$, assuming only a vanishing mesh and a diverging observation horizon. This improves the previously known condition that the index exceed $(11+\sqrt{89})/2$. The proof cuts off the continuous score near $0$, recovers the remainder by exact conditional centering on each sampling interval, and transfers LAN by a conditional-likelihood argument.
Generic finiteness of rotating relative equilibria in the planar $N$-vortex problem

For every $N\ge2$, we prove that Zariski-generic nonzero real circulations, with any prescribed signs, admit at most $N^{2N}$ labeled, collision-free rotating relative equilibria modulo translations, rotations in $SO(2)$, and positive scaling. The excluded parameters lie in an explicit finite union of quadratic hypersurfaces. The proof combines a logarithmic-residue obstruction to positive-dimensional complex solution sets with Bézout degree bounds.
A Proof of The Twin-Star Hypothesis in Dimension Five

It was recently shown that the question of whether the determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to multiplication by a scalar is equivalent to a combinatorial conjecture regarding cycle-free \(d\)-partitions of the complete graph \(K_{2d}\), known as the twin-star hypothesis. This hypothesis asserts that every cycle-free \(d\)-partition of \(K_{2d}\) is weakly equivalent to one that contains a component isomorphic to the twin-star graph \(TS_d\). This hypothesis was previously established for \(d\le4\). In the present paper, we prove it for \(d=5\). Consequently, the associated determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to a scalar in dimension \(5\).
A Universal Algebraic Construction of Hilbert-Space Fragmentation

We present a mechanism for obtaining Hilbert-space fragmentation from arbitrary quantum lattice Hamiltonians acting on finite-dimensional local spaces. We first express the Hamiltonian in an algebraic form using supersymmetry (SUSY) and parasupersymmetry (paraSUSY) generators. Enlarging their representations defines a lifting procedure, which we study in two forms, site-wise and bond-wise lifting. Site-wise lifting introduces immobile zero modes that generate exponentially many invariant sectors while retaining the original dynamics in the fully active sector. We determine the sector structure and establish strong fragmentation for uniform lifts at fixed intermediate zero-mode density. For nearest-neighbor chains, correlation functions reveal restricted propagation and, in the mixed-field example, persistent local memory. Bond-wise lifting produces mobile conserved strings, pair-flip dynamics and fluctuating dimers, and extends to fragmented unitary circuits. Different representations and embeddings realize different fragmentation mechanisms. Some of the fragmented models obtained by this method include lifted permutation and Ising spin chains, a lifted toric code, the \(XXC\) families of spin chains, and fragmented extensions derived from the integrable \(H_{1,11}\) and \(H_{1,3}\) seed densities. The last two models are derived from Hietarinta's classification of constant $4\times 4$ Yang-Baxter solutions.
Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe

We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable.
 The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra.
 In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link outside the Lorenz spectrum. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.
Qing-Ming Cheng; Fengjiang Li; Guoxin Wei

Let $X:M^n\to\R^{n+1}$ be an $n$-dimensional complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm $S$ of the second fundamental form. For $n=4$, we prove that if $f_3=\sum_iλ_i^3$ is constant, where $λ_i$ denotes principal curvatures, then $S=0$, or $S=1$ and the image $X(M^n)$ in the rigid cases is one of the hyperplane, the sphere or the standard generalized cylinders. In every dimension, under assumption of sub-exponential growth we prove the same conclusion. Without assumption of sub-exponential growth, we prove if $S\leq 3+1/\sqrt n$, then the same conclusion holds.
An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms

To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue.
 In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject. We further equip this category with a symmetric monoidal structure, compute its homotopy 1-category, and extend the construction to manifolds endowed with tangential structures, obtaining the interval Segal space of $d$-dimensional bordisms with tangential structure.
 To model the stratifications supporting topological defects, we work with conically smooth stratified spaces, a suitably smooth framework for conical stratifications.
 We define stratified topological manifolds as stratified $\mathcal{B}$-manifolds for a suitable $(\infty,1)$-category of basics $\mathcal{B}$. Using these, we construct an interval Segal space whose objects are compact closed stratified topological $(d-1)$-manifolds and whose 1-morphisms are stratified $d$-dimensional bordisms, and we endow it with a symmetric monoidal structure. We also use tangential structures on conically smooth stratified spaces to formulate a notion of defect labels, aiming toward bordisms with labeled defects in the style of Carqueville et al.
 Finally, we sketch a higher-dimensional generalization of the interval category to a category of $d$-cubes for $d>1$, conjecturally presenting $(\infty,d)$-categories, and outline how stratified factorization homology may be used to produce derived stratified defect TQFTs.
A Quantum Metric Approach to Stabilizer Codes

We associate a spectral triple with each stabilizer code in a projective error model arising from a nice error basis and equipped with a length function. The spectral triple records the dimension of the code as well as the minimum code distance. For Pauli stabilizer codes of dimension greater than one with Hamming weight, Latrémolière's dual propinquity provides a pseudometric which allows us to compare codes of different physical and logical dimensions. We show that in the resulting topology, minimum distance of a code is locally constant for qubits and for qudits of dimensions three and five. Thus correction of all errors up to a prescribed weight is a local property in these cases. Moreover, for each prime $p$, we classify the underlying $C^*$-algebras in the metric closure as a subclass of AF algebras, namely those arising as tensor products of $C((\mathbb{Z}_p)^r)$, for $r \in \{0,1,2, \ldots , \infty\}$, with matrix algebras of $p$-power order or the UHF algebra of type $p^\infty$. Every such $C^*$-algebra not isomorphic to $M_{p^k}(\mathbb{C})$ for any $k\geq 1$ occurs as the underlying algebra of a point in the metric boundary. In particular, we obtain the CAR algebra as a metric limit of qubit stabilizer codes.

The counting problem for meromorphic differentials on $\mathbb{CP}^1$ with fixed orders of zeros and poles and vanishing residues at some specific poles, up to the action of $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ and the multiplication by a nonzero constant, was completely solved before by several authors. In all the cases when there are finitely many such meromorphic differentials, an explicit formula for their number was found and also, in the case of residueless meromorphic differentials with two zeros, a link to the WDVV equations and the KP hierarchy was established. We consider a real analog of these counting problems by requiring that a meromorphic differential is preserved by a real structure on $\mathbb{CP}^1$. Our real counting problems admit refinements, obtained for example by specifying the orders of poles and zeros that are fixed by the antiholomorphic involution. We obtain explicit formulas for all our real counting problems and also, in the case of real meromorphic differentials with two complex conjugate zeros and residueless poles, establish a link to the open WDVV equations and the system of equations for the wave function of the KP hierarchy. An application to real Hurwitz numbers is also presented.
Cotorsion pairs in $η$-extensions with applications to $θ$-extension rings and tensor rings
Pan Chen; Yongyun Qin; Jinrui Yang

Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category with enough projective and injective objects, and let $\mathcal B\ltimes_ηF$ be an $η$-extension of $\mathcal B$ with $η$ associative. Given a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ in $\mathcal B$, we show that the cotorsion pair $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ exists for arbitrary associative $η$, removing the square-zero assumption $F^2=0$ from Hu's construction. When $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ is hereditary, the heredity of $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ is characterized by the first left derived functor of a canonical defect functor $δ$. We also remark that Hu's construction and hereditary result for the cotorsion pair $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ remain valid without the nilpotence assumption on $η$. Under nilpotence hypotheses, we establish a completeness criterion for $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ using the Beligiannis radical functor $\mathfrak r$. And we also provide a completeness criterion for $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ if $\mathcal B\ltimes_ηF$ has enough injective objects. We give sufficient conditions for their coincidence. Dual results are obtained for $ζ$-coextensions. Finally, we specialize the theory to $θ$-extension rings and tensor rings, where the abstract conditions admit explicit module-theoretic descriptions.

In this paper, we study Smirnov's conjecture: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p>0$ and dimension $d$. Let $I$ be an $\mathfrak{m}$-primary ideal. If $R$ is weakly $F$-regular, analytically unramified and Cohen-Macaulay, then $\displaystyle L_1(I)=e(I)-e_{\mathrm{HK}}(I)$ if and only if $I$ is stable. Here, $e(I)$ and $e_{\mathrm{HK}}(I)$ denote the Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity and the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity of $R$ with respect to $I$, respectively. Moreover, $\displaystyle L_1(I)=\lim_{q\to\infty}\frac{e_1(I^{[q]})}{q^d},$ where $q=p^e$ and $e_1(I^{[q]})$ denotes the first Hilbert coefficient of $R$ with respect to the $q$th Frobenius power of $I$.
 We prove the conjecture when $R$ is either excellent and strongly $F$-regular, or excellent of dimension $3$.
Powers of projective lines inside full flag varieties

Up to now, symplectic foliations of Poisson varieties have been primarily studied from a set theoretic perspective by describing their symplectic leaves individually as orbit closures. In the direction of obtaining algebro-geometric characterizations, for the standard Poisson structure $π$ on the full flag variety $G/B_+$ of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$, we prove that the irreducible components of the reduced part of the 0-degeneracy locus of $(G/B_+, π)$ are precisely the inclusion-maximal $T$-stable complete Poisson submanifolds of $(G/B_+, π)$ that are isomorphic to powers of $\mathbb{P}^1$. This characterization is based on a theorem that explicitly classifies the closed Richardson varieties of $G/B_+$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{P}^1)^d$. In turn, this theorem is based on a general theorem for arbitrary $T$-stable subvarieties of full flag varieties $G/B_+$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{P}^1)^d$.
On $z_{2M}(21,4)$: the Hole Extensions of the Chen--Chen Configuration Are Reducible, and the Extremal Configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ Are Not Unique
Carles Marín; Liqun Qi; Gaohang Yu

The second order extended Zarankiewicz number $z_{2M}(m,n)$ of Qi and Yu allows a secondary half of a $2$-edge to be shared, while the $1$-edge graph stays $C_4$-free and extremal and $1$-edges and main halves stay exclusive. Whether $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ is open. Since deleting a $2$-edge removes exactly one displayed square, $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ if and only if there is no irreducible admissible configuration with exactly $56$ displayed squares, and by the cell count of Qi and Yu and the heredity of irreducibility such a configuration without empty cells is an extremal $55$-square configuration of $z_2(21,4)$ plus one $2$-edge at its hole. For the extremal configuration of Chen and Chen we show, by certificates verified in exact rational arithmetic, that all $56$ such extensions have SOS rank at most $55$: $32$ by product relations and $24$ by contraction certificates of Xu--Yan type. We also show, with computer-assisted certificates and an exhaustive isomorphism search, that the extremal configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ fall into at least six isomorphism classes; Chen and Chen leave the structural classification of extremal augmented graphs open. Finally we prove a six-to-four reduction. For irreducible configurations whose $1$-edge graph is $C_4$-free with $m+\binom n2$ edges it bounds the multiplicity of a shared half by $n(n-1)$ ($12$ at $21\times4$), and it applies directly to an explicit number of the extensions of any extremal configuration of $z_2(21,4)$, eight for that of Chen and Chen, bringing each to at most $54$ squares, in agreement with the certificates. The cell count, the heredity lemma, the rows lemma, the six-to-four identity and a $2\times2$ example are checked in Isabelle/HOL; the remaining arguments are written proofs.
$Q$-operators, cluster mutations, and flavored Toda chain
Saebyeok Jeong; Taro Kimura; Norton Lee

We construct Baxter $Q$-operators for a family of quantum cluster integrable systems, that we call the flavored Toda chains, associated with quivers $\mathcal{Q}_N[F]$, where $F\subseteq\{2,\dots,N\}$ specifies data of $\vert F \vert$ additional nodes compared to $\mathcal{Q}_N[\varnothing]$ for the ordinary $N$-particle open $q$-deformed Toda chain. A distinguished sequence of quantum cluster mutations yields an ordered product of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithms. We prove that these operators form a commuting family and that their shifted quotients are transfer matrices whose coefficients are commuting Hamiltonians. We identify these transfer matrices with matrix elements of products of explicit local Lax matrices of rank two. Local cluster transformations move flavor insertions along the chain while preserving their ordered flavor parameters and the transfer matrix together with the canonical transformation. We also derive integral kernels for the $Q$-operators and evaluate an associated Fourier transform as a factorized scalar $Q$-function. Finally, we relate the quivers to the BPS quivers of five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories in the decoupling limit and identify the normalized scalar $Q$-function with the perturbative contribution of a canonical codimension-two defect wrapping a squashed three-sphere.
Ramsey goodness of large generalized fans

Given graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $N$ such that any red-blue edge coloring of $K_N$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. If $H$ is connected, Burr's lower bound gives $r(G,H)\geq (χ(G)-1)(|V(H)|-1)+s(G)$, where $s(G)$ is the minimum size of a color class over all proper $χ(G)$-colorings of $G$. The graph $H$ is called $G$-good if equality holds in this bound. Liu and Li [J. Graph Theory, 2025] characterized the graphs $G$ with $s(G)=1$ for which $K_p+nH$ is $G$-good for $p\geq 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, and posed the corresponding problem for $p=1$. We solve this problem by showing that for a graph $G$ with $χ(G)=k+1\geq 2$ and $s(G)=1$, a graph $H$ of order $h$ and sufficiently large $n$, $K_1+nH$ is $G$-good if and only if $G\subseteq mK_2+K_{k-1}(m)$ when $nh$ is odd, or $G\subseteq (mK_2\cup K_{1,2})+K_{k-1}(m)$ when $nh$ is even, for some positive integer $m$.
Existence of alternating Hamiltonian paths on specific bicolored point sets

Consider a bicolored point set $P$ in general position in the plane consisting of $n$ blue and $n$ red points. We show that if $P$ can be partitioned into bicolored pairs $(a_i,b_i)$ such that, for every $i$, $a_i$ and $b_i$ have different colors and the sets $P\setminus \{a_i\}$ and $P \setminus \{b_i\}$ have the same order type, then there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. We also investigate the case when $P$ lies on the circle, and every interval along the circle contains at most $c$ more points of one color than of the other. For $c=2$, we show that there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. For $c=3$, we show that there exist configurations of points for which the longest noncrossing alternating path on $P$ has size at most $(2-1/25)n + O(1)$.
From Objective Compromise to Structure-Enabled Intelligence: Reshaping the Scientific Paradigm of AI

Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), are fundamentally constructed upon the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm. This paradigm can be characterized as an ill-posed optimization problem within a high-dimensional parameter space. When confronted with real-world scenarios characterized by noise and conflicting constraints, the logic of global error minimization inherently induces a strong smoothing effect. Consequently, this yields statistical compromise solutions that flatten local features, making it arduous to overcome the inherent bottleneck of Out-of-Distribution (OOD) generalization. Existing AI models generate outputs purely based on statistical probabilities. They lack the capacity to autonomously discern truth from falsehood or establish causal logic, thereby lacking genuine cognitive intelligence. To address the ontological limitations of the OD paradigm, this paper proposes a novel paradigm termed \textit{Structure-Enabled Intelligence}. This approach abandons the conventional path of relying solely on computing power scaling and data fitting to achieve emergent intelligence. Instead, it embeds mathematical structures and physical mechanisms as underlying priors into the algorithmic architecture, constraining the model's solving process with structured scientific rules. Through this paradigm shift from ``data-driven objective fitting'' to ``mechanism-structure dominance,'' the proposed approach fundamentally mitigates the issue of statistical compromise, enhances the model's extrapolation and generalization capabilities, and simultaneously reshapes human-AI synergy by upholding human subjectivity in scientific cognition.
On the Waldschmidt constant of monomial ideals

We investigate a conjecture proposed by Cooper et al. in 2017 regarding a lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant of monomial ideals. We first show that this conjecture does not hold in general by explicitly computing the Waldschmidt constant for a family of monomial ideals. Also, we identify a class of monomial ideals for which this conjecture holds by proving a containment between symbolic and ordinary powers. For a monomial ideal, we provide a new lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant, which modifies the conjectured lower bound under a certain condition.
Smoothing of the Coupled KdV System on \mathbb{T}

We study the nonlinear smoothing properties of the Coupled KdV system posed on the torus. This system arises as a particular case of the four-parameter family of Boussinesq systems studied by Bona, Chen and Saut, corresponding to the choice $η^{2}=\frac{2}{3}$, $b=d=0$ and $a=c=\frac{1}{6}$. Although the similarities with the periodic KdV equation and the favorable resonance structure of the Majda-Biello system for the coupling parameter $α=-1$ might suggest that smoothing can be established by a relatively straightforward adaptation of existing techniques, the nonlinear interactions in the Coupled KdV system introduce additional difficulties. In particular, certain mixed interactions lead to degeneracies in the associated resonance functions, resulting in a loss of frequency decay that restricts the attainable smoothing gain. By combining normal-form reductions, duality arguments and Bourgain-space estimates, we establish a smoothing gain of any order $
a< \min \{1,\frac{2}{3}(2s+1)\} $
for $s>-\frac{1}{2}$. Our result demonstrates that the interplay between nonlinear interactions and resonance structures plays a decisive role in determining the smoothing properties of coupled dispersive systems.
First-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise

We prove first-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the Freidlin--Wentzell minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise, which answers the question of the sharp rate left open in [Hong, Jin, Sheng, \emph{IMA J. Numer. Anal.} 45 (2025), 1501--1536]. As shown in that work, a bound on the action controls only the $L^2$ norm of the velocity, which leads to a half-order estimate for the difference between the discrete and continuous actions. To improve it, we use the discrete Euler--Lagrange equation to derive mesh-independent $L^\infty$ bounds on the velocity of piecewise affine interpolants of stationary discrete paths with bounded action. For the case of a unique continuous minimizer, we identify the leading coefficient of the error between the discrete and continuous minimum actions on uniform grids, and a scalar example shows that the first-order error bound is sharp. We also prove strong $H^1(0,T;\mathbb R^d)$ subsequential convergence of interpolated discrete minimizers. Numerical experiments for a two-protein genetic toggle switch confirm first-order convergence of the discrete action for transitions in both directions.

We study faithful Galois extensions in a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathscr{C}$ by a dualizable $\mathbb{E}_1$-group $G$. We prove that these extensions correspond to colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathrm{An}^{\mathrm{B}G}$ to $\mathscr{C}$. Under suitable assumptions, we use this correspondence to construct a Galois pro-anima that classifies Galois extensions in $\mathscr{C}$. This generalizes the étale fundamental groupoid of commutative rings and Mathew's weak Galois groupoid.
An implicit high-order flux reconstruction method with logarithmic variables for hypersonic flows in thermochemical nonequilibrium
Rayan Dhib; Vatsalya Sharma; Vincent F. Giangaspero; Firas Ben Ameur; José Miguel Luzia Murteira; Stefaan Poedts; Andrea Lani

Simulating hypersonic flows in thermochemical nonequilibrium requires solving the Navier-Stokes equations for reacting, possibly ionised mixtures. Compact high-order computations of viscous two-temperature air flows on unstructured grids have not gone beyond P = 2. We present an implicit Flux Reconstruction (FR) method for such flows, built on three ingredients. First, the solver stores and updates the logarithms of the partial densities and temperatures, making every state admissible without a positivity limiter and, for ionised mixtures, imposing charge neutrality consistently with the implicit update. Second, shocks are captured by subcell order blending, extended to steady implicit computations on curved Gauss-Legendre meshes, with second-order subcell blending in subsonic regions and an automatic freeze of the blending near convergence. Third, a pseudo-transient Newton method with a physicality-limited update and automatic CFL control reaches steady state from the free stream with the same settings at every order. The design order is verified up to sixth order on a manufactured solution for five-species air with finite-rate chemistry and vibrational relaxation. Steady viscous solutions up to sixth order are obtained for five- and eleven-species air on the High Enthalpy shock tunnel Göttingen (HEG) cylinder and for eleven-species air on the RAM-C II vehicle. To our knowledge, this work gives the first design-order verification of a high-order method with finite-rate air chemistry and vibrational relaxation, and the first high-order finite-element-type computations of viscous eleven-species, two-temperature air. On the HEG cylinder, the stagnation-point heat flux is within 2% of finite-volume references and within 6% of the measurements, with a comparable number of degrees of freedom to second-order finite-volume computations but on meshes with 20 to 40 times fewer elements.
Klaus Altmann; Andreas Hochenegger; Frederik Witt

Previous work of the authors introduced the class of Horrocks-Mumford sheaves over normal algebraic k-varieties, the most prominent example being the classical Horrocks-Mumford bundle on projective four-space. For a smooth semiprojective toric variety, we derive an explicit description of these sheaves in terms of finitely generated graded modules over the Cox ring which we use for an algorithmic treatment. In particular, we discuss some explicit examples, their indecomposability and local freeness.
Switching Structure and Finite-Event Optima for One-Orbit Minimum-Fuel In-Plane HCW Maneuvers

Under in-plane Hill$\unicode{x2013}$Clohessy$\unicode{x2013}$Wiltshire dynamics with independently bounded radial and along-track thrust, we prove that every target reachable within one orbit has a fixed-time minimum-fuel control with at most ten switches. We first show that regular optima have at most four radial and six along-track switches, coupled through a shared costate. Of the 35 candidate count pairs, 11 require minimum durations, one cannot be optimal, and 23 are attainable at arbitrarily short durations. We then convert singular-arc optima into bang/off optima with at most five switches by preserving terminal moments. We demonstrate terminal accuracy and whole-arc Pontryagin consistency through 55,296 numerical transfers.
The governing equation for probability density of transition path time

Transition path time is the time it takes a system to move from the initial state (State A) to a final state (State B) without recrossing back to State A in between. The transition path time is probabilistic in nature, and considerable research has been devoted to studying its distribution. In this paper, we derive a governing integral equation that expresses the density of the transition path time in terms of the probability density of the first passage time, which is well understood. An efficient numerical method is provided to solve this governing equation. Several numerical examples are presented to validate the governing equation and to compare the densities of the transition path time and the first passage time.
$L^p(\mathbb{R}^3)$-estimates for maximal averages along mixed homogeneous hypersurfaces with vanishing Hessian

We study maximal averages over the surfaces parametrized by $c+Φ$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, where $c$ is a constant and $Φ$ is mixed homogeneous and real analytic away from the origin. Under the assumption that the Hessian determinant of $Φ$ vanishes identically, we classify the possible graphing functions for all positive weights. For surfaces in each resulting class, we establish sharp $L^{p}$-estimates for the corresponding maximal averages.

We settle a long-standing problem by proving that every block-primitive combinatorial design is point-primitive. Since block-primitivity and point-primitivity coincide for symmetric designs by duality, it remains to treat the non-symmetric $2$-designs. For these we apply the O'Nan--Scott theorems for primitive and for quasiprimitive permutation groups and prove that the automorphism group of every such design is almost simple on points and on blocks. Together with the classification of finite simple groups, this classifies all non-symmetric block-primitive $2$-designs except for two families of block stabilizers in even characteristic.
 The exceptions are as follows. One family is of subfield type, $PSL_2(q_0)$ with $q=q_0^{d}$, $d\geq2$, of order below the dihedral point stabilizer $D_{2(q\pm1)}$, and includes $S_3\cong PSL_2(2)$ and $A_5\cong PSL_2(4)$. The other is the dihedral block stabilizer $D_{2(q-1)}$, where the block is a union of $a$ of the $q/2$ orbits, so that $v=q(q-1)/2$, $k=a(q-1)$ and $λ=2a(aq-a-1)/(q-2)$, the last an integer exactly when $(q-2)/2$ divides $a(a-1)$; this family is exhausted by finite enumeration except at the degrees beyond its range.
 We then determine which of these designs have strength $t\geq 3$. Apart from the inversive planes and the five Witt designs, exactly two Steiner families arise, attached to the exceptional maximal subgroups of $PGL_2(q)$. There is no non-complete design of strength $t\geq 6$.
Strictly pseudoconvex $CR$ structures on $\sfS^5$ that can be turned inside out
The existence of a complex structure on $\sfS^{6}$ implies that of strictlty pseudoconvex structures on $\sfS^{5}$ which can be turned inside out by a homotopy.
A Liouville theorem for Lévy operators on nilpotent and compact Lie groups

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a left-invariant Lévy operator, with characteristics $(a,b,μ)$, on a connected
 and simply connected Lie group $G$ that is either compact or nilpotent with $[G,[G,G]]$ relatively
 compact (equivalently, of step at most two). We prove that every bounded distributional solution of $\mathcal{L}u=0$ is right-invariant under
 the closed subgroup $P=\overline{\langle\exp\mathfrak h_0\cup\text{supp}μ\rangle}$, where
 $\mathfrak h_0=\text{Lie}\langle b,\operatorname{ran}(a)\rangle$, and is constant if and only if $P=G$. In the
 compact case we give three proofs, one through the Itô--Kawada equidistribution theorem, one by
 propagation of the maximum and one by an application of the Peter-Weyl theorem, while the nilpotent case rests on the Choquet--Deny theorem of Bénard and Frisch.
Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Stationary Convective Brinkman--Forchheimer Extended Darcy Equations with a Nonlinear Slip Boundary Condition of Friction Type
Wasim Akram; Weimin Han; Manil T. Mohan

This work develops and analyzes several discontinuous Galerkin methods for a variational inequality associated with the stationary convective Brinkman--Forchheimer extended Darcy (CBFeD) system. The CBFeD model generalizes the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations by incorporating additional damping and pumping terms. The resulting variational inequality characterizes the motion of a viscous, incompressible fluid in a saturated porous medium under a friction-type slip boundary condition. For the CBFeD variational inequality, we first explore the existence of a unique weak solution. Then, we establish the existence, uniqueness, and stability of the numerical solutions obtained using discontinuous Galerkin methods. Optimal error estimates are derived, measured in the broken $H^1$-norm for the velocity and in the $L^2$-norm for the pressure, when linear velocity elements and piecewise constant pressure approximations are employed. Numerical simulations are carried out to confirm the theoretically predicted convergence orders and to highlight key strengths of the method, including its ability to capture discontinuities, effectively resolve shear layers, handle advection-dominated regimes, and operate robustly on general polygonal meshes.
Two-Sided large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta function and its iterates

Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we establish lower bounds for large oscillations of the iterated argument functions \(S_n(t)\) of the Riemann zeta function. As a corollary, we prove that, for every fixed integer \(n \geq 0\),
 \[S_n(t)=Ω_{\pm}\Big(\frac{(\log t)^{1/2}(\log_3 t)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 t)^{n+1/2}} \Big).\] For even \(n\), this recovers two results of Chirre and Mahatab in 2021. For odd \(n\), our result strengthens theirs by establishing the missing direction of oscillation with the same order of magnitude.
Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems

We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.
Two-scale system: compactified ambient metrics and Scri/Spi/Ti
Xavier Bekaert; Maxim Grigoriev; Mikhail Markov

We show that certain geometric constructions, including the Fefferman-Graham ambient metric, Brinkmann spaces, and ultrastatic vacuum spacetimes, admit natural conformal compactifications and can be unified within a single framework arising naturally from conformal geometry. The framework is based on a two-scale system comprising two weight-one conformal scalars satisfying almost-Einstein equations and certain regularity conditions. As a particular instance of this unifying framework, we obtain a new ambient construction for Spi and Ti, the extended spatial and temporal infinities of Ricci-flat spacetimes. A remarkable feature of this construction is that Spi/Ti and the null infinity of the corresponding spacetimes are naturally realised as a boundary face and the corner of the two-scale ambient space, respectively. We also demonstrate how the two-scale system can serve as a background ambient geometry for studying the asymptotic behaviour of (gauge) fields at spatial, temporal, and null infinity.
On VMO-Type Characterizations of Ball Banach Sobolev Spaces and Independence of Integrable Index of Special John--Nirenberg--Campanato Spaces
Zhexu Bai; Hao Peng; Dachun Yang; Wen Yuan; Yangyang Zhang

Let $k\in\mathbb N$, $X$ be a ball Banach function space, and $W^{k,X}$ denote the corresponding ball Banach Sobolev space. In this article, we solve six questions in [Math. Z. 311 (2025)]. Specifically, we first prove that the constants in its VMO-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ are sharp uniformly over all ball Banach function spaces satisfying suitable assumptions. Next, we show that the BBM-type formula and the BSVY-type formula involving minimizing polynomials or ball averages fail in general. In contrast, we establish higher-order BBM-type formulas involving Taylor polynomials and further obtain a Taylor-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ under suitable assumptions. Moreover, we construct counterexamples to show that the characterization of $W^{k,X}$ via higher-order minimizing polynomials fails in general. Finally, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for special John--Nirenberg--Campanato spaces defined via congruent cubes to be independent of their integrability exponent $q$.
Markov potential priors for prediction in Gamma models

We consider Bayesian prediction in independent Gamma scale models with arbitrary known positive shape parameters. When the dimension is at least three, we construct a shrinkage prior toward any prespecified positive scale vector. The resulting predictive density strictly dominates the Jeffreys predictive density under Kullback--Leibler loss and is minimax. The prior is obtained by weighting the Jeffreys prior with a Markov potential. The transition is determined by the beta--gamma decomposition. The domination result is nonasymptotic.
A counterexample to the Jordan tuple conjecture of Ball and Helton

This article constructs a pair of bounded commuting 3-symmetric operators with no Jordan-family extension. The operators are coordinate multipliers on a Sobolev space of functions with values in three dimensional complex Euclidean space with an equivalent Hilbert norm. Their quadratic symbol has no operator polynomial factorization, even with an auxiliary target Hilbert space. The construction transfers the nonfactorability of the matrix quadratic used by Russo to the symbol of a commuting 3-symmetric tuple. The factorization approach of McCullough--Russo and Russo then supplies the obstruction to a Jordan-family extension.
A generic $p$-Wasserstein space is isometrically rigid
Zoltán M. Balogh; Eric Ströher; Tamás Titkos; Dániel Virosztek

We prove for any parameter $p \geq 1$ that the $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ of a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X)$ is isometrically rigid, that is, its isometries are precisely the push-forwards of the isometries of $(X,d_X).$ We also study the question whether the isometry class of a $p$-Wasserstein space completely determines the isometry class of the underlying space. We prove for any $p\geq 1$ that for a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X),$ its $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ is isometric to another $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(Y,d_Y)$ if and only if $(Y,d_Y)$ is isometric to $(X,d_X).$ En route we prove that a stronger property, which we call the Dirac preservation property, is also generic.
Bumpless pipe dreams for involutions and shifted plane partitions
Eric Marberg; Alejandro H. Morales; Tianyi Yu

This article studies a triangular variant of bumpless pipe dreams for involutions in the symmetric group. We prove that a natural weight generating function for these objects recovers all involution Schubert polynomials. For vexillary involutions, we derive a $K$-theoretic extension of this result that gives a new formula for orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials. In the course of showing this formula, we compute a diagonal term order Gröbner basis for the defining ideals of symmetric matrix Schubert varieties associated to vexillary involutions. As applications, we prove a conjectured product formula for principal specializations of involution Schubert polynomials. We go on to derive a shifted analogue of the Fomin--Kirillov formula counting bounded plane partitions. This analogue proves the straight-shape case of a conjecture of Ferroni, Morales, and Panova on the Ehrhart positivity for the order polytopes of shifted partitions. We also conjecture a bumpless pipe dream formula for involution Grothendieck polynomials and discuss connections with diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrices and asymptotics of principal specializations.
Absence of binding for the helium anion

We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.
Yangming Li; P. Pérez-Altarriba; L. A. Kudrachenko; A. Ballester-Bolinches

We investigate complemented skew left braces, that is, skew braces in which every skew subbrace admits a complement. We establish that if every minimal subbrace of a finite skew brace is complemented, then the brace is supersoluble and all its skew subbraces of prime power order are elementary abelian. We also show that the converse does not hold in general, providing a finite counterexample. Furthermore, we prove that every subbrace of a finite direct product of square-free skew braces is complemented. Finally, we extend our investigation to the infinite setting, proving that every multipermutational complemented skew brace is hypercyclic and that all its skew subbraces whose additive groups are $p$-groups are elementary abelian.

We describe a method for generating infinitely many rational parametric solutions of the problem and another method for generating parametric solutions of the problem in terms of univariate polynomials with integer coefficients. Here, we derive the most general continuous-time, CP-divisible evolution of such an object, the \textit{quantum comb master equation} (QCME), which governs the quantum ``dynamics of dynamics''.
