Our two main results are an eight-element list theorem for fullerenes and the universal bound $λ(G)\le708587$ for all 3-connected plane graphs. We establish structural nine- and eight-color bounds, classify triangulations whose vertices of degree at least five form an independent set, and determine their exact diagonal chromatic numbers. We also prove closure under triangular sums for $q\ge7$ diagonal colors, with an optimal uniform threshold. For cubic 3-connected plane graphs we obtain $λ\le14$, improving to $λ\le9$ in the bipartite case.

We study self-interpretations of theories and their connection to Kraj\'ıček-theories. Our two main results are the following. Firstly, if the self-interpretations of a theory form a group in the category ${\sf INT}_3$ of theories and interpretations, then the theory is a Kraj\'ıček-theory. Secondly, a sequential theory is a Kraj\'ıček-theory iff all its self-interpretations are initial. Here initiality of the interpretation $K$ means roughly that its internal interpretations of the weak theory ${\sf S}^1_2$ are initial in all interpretations of ${\sf S}^1_2$.
Fourier Harmonics and Pentagonal Rigidity in the Planar Ulam Floating Body Problem

We give a new proof that the disk is the only strictly convex planar body floating in equilibrium in every orientation at perimetral densities $σ=1/5$ and $σ=2/5$. The proof uses the Fourier harmonics of the chord-angle function and the closure relations of the associated pentagonal carousel. Their combination gives inequalities that force the body to be a disk.
Convergence rate of observables in the Marcus-Lushnikov process toward Smoluchowski with singular homogeneous kernels

We study the approximation of the Smoluchowski coagulation equation by the Marcus--Lushnikov process with $N$ initial particles for the singular family of kernels $K\_α(x,y)=x^{-α}+y^{-α}, α> 0$. For regular mean-field particle systems, pathwise fluctuations are naturally expected on the scale $N^{-1/2}$, whereas sufficiently smooth observables may exhibit a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ after averaging. The singularity of $K\_α$ at the origin makes it unclear whether this second-order mechanism survives. We prove that it does: for a class of sufficiently regular nonlinear functionals of the empirical measure, we establish a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ on finite time intervals. The main mechanism is a regularization produced by the singular dynamics itself. Small clusters coagulate at increasingly large rates, which generates exponential moments in the singular variable $x^{-α}$ and yields a rapid escape from the singularity at zero. We exploit this phenomenon through a Wasserstein-type distance adapted to $x^{-α}$, together with weighted total variation estimates used to construct and control the derivative of the Smoluchowski flow.
The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs

Inspired by the theory of pro-graded adic rings developed recently by Ishizuka and Yoshikawa, we introduce and study the notions of a pro-graded Huber ring and a pro-graded Huber pair \begin{equation*}((\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}), \mathcal{A}^{+}),\end{equation*}which capture the intuition of a complete Huber ring (or Huber pair) equipped with a dense graded subring. Using these notions, we define and study an analog \begin{equation*}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}, \mathcal{A}^{+})\end{equation*}of the $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction from algebraic geometry in the realm of adic spaces, without restricting our attention to adic spaces satisfying any Noetherian or finite-type assumptions. We consider gradings both by $\mathbb{Z}$ and by $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ for a fixed prime number $p$, so our $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction recovers both classical examples such as usual adic projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{ad}}$ and infinite-type, perfectoid examples such as perfectoid projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{perfd}}$. Using GAGA, we prove that the adic analytification of any projective variety $X$ over a nonarchimedean field $K$ can be described as the adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ of a suitable pro-graded affinoid algebra $\mathcal{A}$. Moreover, we prove that in this case $\dim X=\dim \mathcal{A}-1$. We also relate our adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction to formal models.
Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
Elena Agliari; Adriano Barra; Andrea Ladiana; Andrea Lepre; Diego Pallara

Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $Λ_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.
The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells

It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.
Normalized ground state solutions to the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem

We study normalized solutions to the Born--Infeld problem \begin{equation*} -{\rm div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right)+μu=f(u)\ \hbox{ in }\mathbb{R}^N,\qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\,dx=2m^2, \end{equation*} $N\ge3$, where $m>0$ is prescribed and $μ>0$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. The nonlinearity $f$ is assumed to be superlinear at infinity, with no upper restriction on its growth, and to behave like $|s|^{p-2}s$ near zero, with $2<p<2^*$. Following a Lagrangian approach, we relate the action ground state level $a(μ)$ of the prescribed frequency problem to the masses of its ground states by means of one-sided derivative formulas, which lead to the existence of normalized solutions. A distinctive feature of the Born--Infeld operator is that the gradient constraint makes the energy bounded from below on every mass sphere, even in the $L^2$-supercritical case. For $2+4/N\le p<2^*$ we obtain a threshold $c_*>0$ such that normalized action ground states exist for $m^2>c_*$, and none exist for $m^2<c_*$. In the $L^2$-subcritical case they exist for every $m^2>0$. We prove that every action ground state has constant sign and is radial up to a translation.
The roads taken in the directed landscape
Pranay Agarwal; Sourav Sarkar; Bálint Virág

Every finite-length path in the directed landscape spends almost all of its time on geodesics. More precisely, let G be the union of the interiors of all geodesics. We prove that, almost surely, every path of finite landscape length lies in G outside a set of times of Hausdorff dimension at most 57/61. We also construct finite-length paths whose exceptional set has dimension at least 1/3. The proof combines quantitative bounds on nearly optimal detours, stochastic domination of the environment outside a geodesic, and a three-geodesic disjointness estimate.
Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order

Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence. In dimension ten, the 25 literature classes considered here all have one. We study all quadratic APN functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with such a self-equivalence, which usually confines them to a much smaller linear space. Up to conjugacy and power similarity, self-equivalences of prime order have 299 types. We settle 298 of them. Elementary lemmas exclude 280 types, and exhaustive searches confirm this for 242 of them. The other 18 types are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates. Up to extended affine equivalence, the 298 types contain 29 classes of quadratic APN functions, four of them new. This also classifies the quadratic APN functions with coefficients in a subfield. Exactly 24 classes contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_4$, and all 3 that contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ are among them. The open type consists of the quadratic canonical triplicate functions. They correspond to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes. Three different searches find only the invariants of 16 classes, all among the 29. We conjecture there are no others. No quadratic APN function in the 298 settled types is Carlet-Charpin-Zinoviev equivalent to a permutation.
The Moduli of Canonical Threefolds of Minimum Volume
Pinxian Bie; Peien Du; Zhengjie Yu

We determine the moduli space of complex projective canonical threefolds of volume $1/420$. It consists of an irreducible rational component of dimension $33$ and two isolated points, represented by the explicitly constructed rigid threefolds Vega and Altair.
Squared Bessel particle systems with weak repulsion
Julia Lenczewska; Jacek Małecki; Szymon Sołtysiak

We study squared Bessel particle systems with repulsion parameter $κ>0$ and dimension parameter $δ\in\mathbb R$. We prove that the singular equation has a unique global strong solution for every initial state in the closed Weyl chamber, including states with coinciding particles. The solutions have locally integrable interaction terms and spend zero Lebesgue time at pairwise collisions. We also consider the equation in which the interaction terms are set to zero at collisions. At certain integer values of $δ$, this equation admits infinitely many solution laws from suitable initial configurations. In these solutions, a block of particles can remain at zero for any prescribed time before being released. For positive initial states, we determine when zero is reached and when particles enter the negative half-line. From distinct initial positions, collisions occur almost surely for $0<κ<1$ and do not occur for $κ\ge1$. Collisions of three or more particles are excluded away from zero. We give an example of a triple collision at zero. We obtain two-sided bounds for the tails of the first-zero and first-collision times. The bounds give matching powers for the first-zero time when it is finite, and for the first-collision time in nonnegative systems when $0<κ<1$.
Quantitative high-contrast homogenisation of composite media with highly anisotropic fibres

This work concerns a non-uniformly elliptic second-order differential operator with periodic coefficients that describes a composite medium formed by a periodic array of highly anisotropic cylindrical fibres set in an isotropic matrix. The ratio of transverse to axial conductivity in the fibres is linked to the period of the coefficients through a `critical' high-contrast scaling, and the axial conductivity is allowed to vary along the fibres. As the period $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, ellipticity degenerates in the directions transverse to the fibres. We are concerned with the resolvent of this operator in the small-$\varepsilon$ limit. For fibres with constant axial conductivity, the two-scale limit of such problems was identified by Cherednichenko, Smyshlyaev and Zhikov (Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: Section A Mathematics 136(1), 87--114 (2006)), and a full two-scale asymptotic expansion, with remainder estimates for smooth right-hand sides, was constructed by Cherednichenko (Asymptotic Analysis 49(1--2), 39--59 (2006)). In the non-constant axial conductivity setting, considered here, we approximate the resolvent in terms of the two-scale limit operator and prove that the error is order $\varepsilon$ in the operator norm, uniformly over right-hand sides in the unit ball of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$; we also obtain order-$\varepsilon$ estimates for the reciprocals of the spectral band functions. This work builds on results announced, without proof, for fibres with circular cross-section in Cooper and Kamotski (Direct and Inverse Problems with Applications: Extended Abstracts of the 2024 GAP Center Summer School, pp.~69--75, Birkhäuser (2026)).
Cover times of random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees
Omer Angel; Christina Goldschmidt; Peleg Michaeli

We study the cover times of uniform random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees, including the negative-parameter models corresponding to random $d$-ary increasing trees. We prove explicit limits in probability and expectation when the cover times are rescaled by $n (\log n)^2$. In particular, for the uniform random recursive tree the cover time is close to $e n (\log n)^2$ with high probability.
Online Switching Control as Learning with Experts
Masataka Nakamura; Kaito Ito; Hideaki Ishii

This paper addresses the problem of online switching control for discrete-time nonlinear systems where a controller is sequentially selected from a finite set of candidates. The goal is to generate an adaptive sequence of controllers to minimize the cumulative cost under unknown disturbances and cost functions. Specifically, we consider a full-information feedback setting where realized disturbance effects and cost functions are available after each selection. Using counterfactual costs computed from historical data, we reduce the online switching control problem to the experts problem with switching costs. Then, we propose an adaptive switching algorithm based on the Hedge algorithm with a switching suppression mechanism. Notably, the proposed algorithm achieves an expected regret of $O(\sqrt{T\log N})$, where $T$ is the time horizon and $N$ is the number of candidate controllers, while ensuring uniform boundedness of the state. This matches the optimal regret order for the standard experts problem.
A Parametric Active-Set Algorithm for Solving Monotone Generalized Nash Equilibrium Problems

We present a fast active-set algorithm for the solution of monotone linear-quadratic generalized Nash equilibrium problems (GNEPs) with shared affine inequality and equality constraints. The algorithm, which we call gPAQ, is an adaptation of the parametric active-set method proposed by Best (1996) and extended in qpOASES by Ferreau et al. (2014) to solve convex quadratic programs. Under strong monotonicity, we show that the same active-set strategy applies. We handle the case of merely monotone problems by using gPAQ as the inner solver within proximal-point iterations. To solve strongly monotone convex nonlinear GNEPs, we propose a Newton-type iterative scheme, which we call gPAN, which iteratively linearizes the nonlinear problem and solves the resulting LQ-GNEP subproblems using gPAQ. We show in numerical examples that the proposed algorithms are significantly faster than existing methods.
Quantifying Dependence Effects on $k$-out-of-$n$ Reliability Relative to the Independent Benchmark

Understanding how dependence among component lifetimes affects the reliability of redundant systems is a central problem in reliability engineering. In this paper, we develop a framework for quantifying the impact of multivariate dependence on $k$-out-of-$n$ system reliability relative to the independent benchmark. Using an orthogonal Legendre expansion of the copula density, we derive an exact decomposition that separates the dependence structure from the system architecture. This representation identifies how individual dependence contributions are transmitted to system reliability through explicit structural weights. An application to multivariate Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copulas demonstrates that higher-order dependence can produce distinct reliability effects even when all bivariate copulas remain unchanged. Our findings provide a systematic approach to quantifying and interpreting the effects of multivariate dependence on the reliability of redundant systems.
Enumeration of Cospectral Graphs with Respect to the Average Flow Matrix

A graph is said to be determined by the spectrum of a graph-associated matrix if no nonisomorphic graph shares the same spectrum with it. In this paper, we introduce the average flow matrix of a connected graph and study its spectral properties. We investigate its effectiveness in distinguishing graphs by carrying out a computational enumeration of connected graphs having a cospectral mate with respect to this matrix up to order 10. Our computations show that every connected graph on at most 10 vertices is determined by the spectrum of the average flow matrix. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first graph-associated matrix for which the spectrum distinguishes all connected graphs of order at most 10.
Potential Flow, Stress, and Straightness in Flow Matching: Euler Error on Gaussian-Mixture Targets
Zijian Liu; Julian Olszewski; Jie Xu

In linear flow matching, coupling straightness measures conditional displacement variance. The conditional covariance gives a kinetic stress in the Jeans balance. The virial identity relates the mean trace of the covariance to a radial moment of acceleration. Euler error also depends on how the flow propagates acceleration. On constructed Gaussian-mixture targets, closed-form couplings with matched straightness yield different median Euler errors. Learned fields from fresh minibatch assignments also yield different Euler errors from their partners at matched estimated straightness. The leading Euler coefficient accounts for more of the error variation than straightness in these experiments. We relate the additive-noise characterization of isotropic Gaussian sources to potential flow. A gradient constraint reduces velocity error on the independent isotropic Gaussian example and increases it on two examples with rotational exact fields.
Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation
Peter A. Clarkson; Clare Dunning; Ben Mitchell

In this paper Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation are discussed. The Bäcklund transformations are applied to rational solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation, which are expressed in terms of the generalised Laguerre polynomials and generalised Umemura polynomials. Using appropriate Bäcklund transformations, we derive non-unique solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation in terms of modified Bessel functions. Further it is shown that there are also rational solutions in terms of generalised Umemura polynomials for the same values of the parameters, which are not special cases of the modified Bessel function solutions. The relationship between solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation and solutions of the third Painlevé equation is also discussed.
Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group

We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.
On Borwein polynomials with multiple roots outside the unit disk
Souad El Otmani; Musbahu Idris; Jean-Marc Sac-Epee

A Borwein polynomial has coefficients in ${-1,0,1}$ and nonzero constant and leading coefficients. We seek Borwein polynomials having a multiple root outside the unit disk. To this end, we consider the powers $L^2$ and $L^3$ of Lehmer's polynomial $L$, which has a real root $τ>1$. Since $L$ has exceptionally small Mahler measure, the theorem of Bombieri and Vaaler guarantees the existence of Borwein multiples of these powers. Such multiples have $τ$ as a root of multiplicity at least 2 and 3, respectively. Mossinghoff (2003, Algorithm 3, p. 323) constructed examples that, under the substitution $x\mapsto -x$, yield such multiples. The main contribution of this paper is to determine the least possible degrees of Borwein multiples of $L^2$ and $L^3$, with and without symmetry restrictions on their coefficients, and to describe their degree spectra. For $L^2$, the minimum degree is 34 without symmetry restrictions, 38 among self-reciprocal multiples, and 41 among antireciprocal multiples. For $L^3$, the corresponding minimum degrees are 115, 115, and 117. We determine the complete degree spectra for $L^2$ and, for $L^3$, classify the degrees from 115 to 150 for which self-reciprocal or antireciprocal Borwein multiples exist, giving an explicit example for each admissible degree in each symmetry class. Further constructions yield Borwein multiples of $L^3$ in every degree $D\geq 215$, with both symmetry types for every $D\geq 231$.
All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model

In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=λΔ+\tanπ(θ+n^2α)δ_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $λ>0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(α, θ)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tanπ(θ+n^2α)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $α\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.
Non-abelian Hodge correspondence for semistable parabolic connections on curves in positive characteristic

Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. We establish a non-abelian Hodge correspondence between semistable parabolic connections on $C$ and semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on its Frobenius twist $C'$, allowing arbitrary prescribed residue eigenvalues, parabolic weights and filtration types. The relationship between the parabolic weights and residue eigenvalues on the two sides is encoded in a table analogous to Simpson's table. We obtain this result by extending the notion of "very good regular connections" to incorporate a residue-dependent degree condition, and by developing a Cartier descent formalism for parabolic connections. Working with filtered sheaves, we obtain a particularly clean description of this Cartier descent formalism that potentially extends to higher dimensional varieties.
Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
Frank Göhmann; Karol K. Kozlowski; Mikhail D. Minin

We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.
Hierarchical Interactions in Mobility Networks: A Model-Free Feedback Approach
Mingjia He; Zhiyu He; Jan Ghadamian; Florian Dörfler; Emilio Frazzoli; Gioele Zardini

Urban mobility systems are large-scale networked systems whose performance emerges from hierarchically coupled decisions of public authorities, competing mobility operators, and travelers. Existing approaches to policy design either collapse one of these levels or assume that the authority can model and differentiate through the equilibrium responses of operators and travelers. In this paper, we model policy design as a tri-level game on a multimodal network, in which a municipality sets taxes, licenses, and integration subsidies, a public transport and a taxi operator compete on prices and service supply, and heterogeneous travelers reach a stochastic user equilibrium. We prove that the traveler equilibrium is unique and continuously differentiable in the operator strategies, that the variational inequality characterizing operator equilibria admits a solution for every policy, and that the resulting tri-level game admits a Stackelberg equilibrium. Building on this structure, we design a model-free hierarchical controller in which the municipality and the operators update their decisions from zeroth-order evaluations of observed equilibrium outcomes. On the Zurich multimodal network, operator equilibria computed from different initializations differ by a median of 0.3% in the municipal objective. On a grid of 3,125 policies, only those that subsidize transfers between public transport and taxis benefit both operators, and 24 of them also lower travel costs without degrading the municipal objective. Finally, the controller matches the best policies of three black-box optimizers and terminates at the most consistent policies across runs.
Nuclear dimension of uniform Roe algebras
Liang Guo; Kang Li; Jiawen Zhang; Jingming Zhu

We prove that for every discrete metric space $X$ of bounded geometry with Yu's Property A, the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ has nuclear dimension at most one. This answers in the negative a long-standing question of Winter and Zacharias on whether the nuclear dimension of $C^*_u(X)$ always equals the asymptotic dimension of $X$. Consequently, $dim_{nuc} C^*_u(X)\in\{0,1,\infty\}$ for every discrete metric space $X$, with or without bounded geometry.
Kronecker Approximations of Covariance Matrices for Solving Inverse Problems

Inverse problems arise in many applications where the task is to recover unknown parameters from indirect or noisy observations. In contrast to forward problems, where outputs are directly computed from known inputs, inverse problems are designed to infer the underlying variables from the observed effect. Inverse problems are often ill-posed, so regularization is needed to compute reasonable solutions. One form of regularization incorporates prior knowledge about the unknown parameters in the form of prior distributions. However, in many settings, large prior covariance matrices pose computational bottlenecks for solving inverse problems. To address this, we study approximations of large covariance matrices via structured Kronecker-Toeplitz products and demonstrate how these approximations can be used to solve inverse problems. We exploit the Block-Toeplitz-Toeplitz-Block structure induced by the covariance kernel to construct compact approximations that are orders of magnitude cheaper to store and invert. These approximations are deployed as prior covariance surrogates in Bayesian inverse problems solved via generalized hybrid iterative methods. We demonstrate that the Kronecker-Toeplitz approximation attains lower relative approximation error than existing matrix approximations, exhibits rapid error decay with rank, and enables efficient matrix-vector products. Applications to 2D seismic tomography reconstruction problems illustrate the practical utility of these methods.
Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras

Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.
Composition of Near-Planar Infrastructure Network Instances with Certified Skewness Bounds

Computational studies of optimization problems on infrastructure networks may require more suitable instances than are available. We propose a method to obtain additional instances by extracting and joining connected parts of existing networks, reusing their topology and parameters. Many infrastructure networks are near-planar, so added connections should preserve this property. We measure near-planarity by skewness, the minimum number of edges whose removal makes a graph planar. We derive bounds on the additional skewness caused by joining and give sufficient conditions under which none is added, and propose the corresponding strategy. We evaluate our approach on 100 sets of network parts extracted from each of PGLib-OPF and SNDlib. Within time limits, we show that no skewness is added for about half of the resulting power transmission networks and all considered telecommunication networks. Our method gives smaller mean upper bounds on added skewness than baselines that select vertices randomly, in order of decreasing degree, or using a Kamada--Kawai layout. Extraction and composition may also make the resulting optimization instances infeasible. To reduce this risk, we solve a simpler, tractable variant of the intended optimization problem during generation and restart if it is infeasible. On the generated instances, we solve security-constrained optimal transmission switching and survivable network design problems in full, demonstrating that the instances vary in computational difficulty with runtimes ranging from seconds to hours. The method thus extends the available benchmark sets with instances that inherit source data, have known skewness bounds, and cover a range of computational difficulty.
Integrated Topology and Redispatch Optimization of Real-World Power Transmission Systems using Branch-and-Benders-Cut
Tim Donkiewicz; Oliver Gaul; Marco Lübbecke

Transmission system operators can reduce congestion management costs by jointly optimizing network topology, generator redispatch, and transformer settings. The large number of switching decisions, detailed operational constraints, and security requirements under outages make this problem computationally demanding. We present a full mixed-integer linear programming formulation that combines line switching, substation reconfiguration, generator commitment and redispatch, and transformer settings with operational requirements. We solve the problem using an exact branch-and-Benders-cut algorithm. We integrate specialized subproblem solution methods, subproblem selection, cut filtering, partial decomposition, and techniques for enforcing network connectivity. A sequential switching heuristic provides initial solutions for the exact solve. An extensive computational study on 130 synthetic instances demonstrates substantial reductions in solution time compared with standard Benders decomposition and shows how heuristic warmstarting improves solution quality, especially when more switching actions are allowed. Results on real transmission networks illustrate how joint topology and redispatch decisions identify effective switching actions that sequential approaches can miss. Selected solutions generated by our approach were presented to system operators and subsequently checked using alternating current power flow calculations. All seven discussed solutions passed a first operator assessment, indicating the practical potential of the integrated approach.
Arithmetical and set-theoretic semantics of the logic of problems and propositions

Kolmogorov interpreted intuitionistic logic as a calculus of problems and later remarked that a complete treatment should deal with problems and propositions together. Melikhov's logic HC is such a joint two-sorted system: it combines classical propositions with intuitionistic problems by means of two modalities, the problem !A (``find a proof of the proposition A'') and the proposition phi (``the problem phi has a solution''). We give the language of HC a formal semantics in which the modalities are read literally: solutions of !A are proofs of A in a fixed formal theory, ?phi states that phi has a solution, and the connectives on problems are interpreted as in Kleene realizability. Three variants are studied: the arithmetical semantics I (provability in PA), its external version E (truth in the standard model), and the set-theoretic semantics B over ZF, where problem variables are ``black boxes'' and a quantifier Pi over them is available. Validity is defined as the existence of a computable uniform solution. We determine which schemes are valid, build calculi HCI, HCE, HCB sound with respect to the three semantics, and derive Lob's scheme from the fixed-point lemma inside the common core of our calculi and HC. The propositional fragments of HCI and HCE are exactly the provability logics GL and GLS; the positive modality-free fragment of valid problems is intuitionistic logic, while the full modality-free fragment lies strictly above it (Rose's formula is valid, Scott's principle is not). We compare the calculi with HC, which turns out to be incompatible with fixed points, prove independence results and list open questions.

We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,φ(\ell/h)\,\barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)=f, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_φ(t):=\frac{tφ'(t)}{φ(t)}\ge k+1+δ, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.
From Butson Hadamard switching to graph switching and back
Aida Abiad; Ronan Egan; Stef Mohnen

Switching is a local operation that preserves specified properties of a combinatorial object. It has been used to derive constructions of inequivalent Hadamard matrices and nonisomorphic cospectral graphs. In this paper we investigate the relation between these constructions for real and Butson Hadamard matrices. We show that, while equivalent matrices have isomorphic associated graphs, the converse can fail for Butson matrices. We prove that a character decomposition determines the graph spectrum from the singular values of entrywise powers. For prime phase, we also observe that the spectrum depends only on the order and phase; for composite phase, a switching preserving the Butson property can change it. We show that Orrick's closed-quadruple and Hall-set switchings correspond to Wang-Qiu-Hu switching, up to graph isomorphism. Going in the other direction, we characterise when the Godsil-McKay and Wang-Qiu-Hu reflections preserve the Butson property and give phase-multiplicity conditions for the corresponding graph switchings. Finally we also relate block switching to cyclic graph switching under a phase-balance condition, automatic at prime phase. These results provide a basis for transferring tools and techniques between matrix switching and graph switching.
On the dynamics of N classical particles interacting with a complex environment
Thierry Goudon; Bruno Marcos; Thomas Oudeville; Simona Rota Nodari

The interactions of a particle with its environment eventually lead to the damping of its motion. This phenomenom is well understood when considering a single particle exchanging energy with the environment. The situation is definitely more complex when many particles are considered: the energy dissipation mechanisms are not clear whenever particles create a common well in which they keep interacting. In this framework, we identify the equilibrium solutions, that consist in clusters of particles at rest, and we establish their spectral stability. We show that the mean position/velocity pair is damped exponentially fast at the linearized level. Coming back to the non linear problem, we can show, at least in some simplified cases, that the dissipation mechanisms also involve far slower rates, that explain the difficulty in observing the relaxation behavior on the individual trajectories.
Transforming local positivity: from minimal valuations to irrational Seshadri constants

We explain how a valuative Nagata type statement proposed by Dumnicki, Harbourne, Küronya, Roé and Szemberg on a polarised surface $(S, H)$ implies maximality (and hence often irrationality) of Seshadri constants on simple cyclic covers. As sample applications we show that very general degree two K3 surfaces and very general hypersurfaces in $\mathbb P^3$ of degree $6$, $8$ or $d\geq 10$ have irrational Seshadri constant at a very general point, unless $d$ is a square.
Dongjing Ma; Qiqi Zhang; Hua Zhu

We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<θ<π/2$, we consider \[ σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) = f(ξ)h^{p-1} rac{ρ^{k+1}}{φ(ρ)}, \qquad ρ=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_μh=\cotθ\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=φ(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_φ(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.
On non-vanishing of the first Hochschild cohomology of blocks

Let $B$ be a block of a finite group algebra $kG$, where $k$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Inspired by the result of Fleischmann, Janiszczak and Lempken that $\mathrm{HH}^1(kG) \not=0$ when $p$ divides the order of $G$, Linckelmann conjectured that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)\not= 0$ when $B$ has non-trivial defect. By developing the methods of Briggs, Rubio y Degrassi and the author, we give a fusion theoretic criterion for non-vanishing, proving the conjecture holds for all blocks of abelian defect. Further, we show the criterion holds for all blocks at $p > 5$, proving the conjecture for all such primes
Kobayashi-Hitchin Correspondence on Equivariant and Basic Bundles
Lucas H. S. Gomes; Hisashi Kasuya; Takashi Ono

Let $(X,J,ω)$ be a compact complex manifold with Gauduchon metric and $G$ a Lie group acting on $X$ by holomorphic isometries. We give an explicit proof of the existence of a $G$-invariant Hermitian-Einstein metric on a $G$-polystable $G$-equivariant holomorphic vector bundle adapting the proof of Lübke-Teleman. We see that if $G$ is a connected complex Lie group with the bijective exponential map and the action of $G$ on $X$ is locally free, then our existence theorem is equivalent to the existence of a basic Hermitian-Einstein metric on a basic polystable basic holomorphic vector bundle on $X$ foliated by the foliation generated by the $G$-action. As an application, we can say that the foliated Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on a Sasakian manifold $S$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-equivariant Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on the Vaisman manifold $S\times S^1$.
Nondegeneracy of the bubble for a fourth-order Liouville boundary problem
Jiaoping Chen; Wenjing Chen; Shengbing Deng

We establish the nondegeneracy of the bubble for \[ Δ^2u=0\quad \text{in }\mathbb R^4_+,\qquad \partial_tu=0,\quad \partial_tΔu=e^{24π^2u} \quad \text{on }\partial\mathbb R^4_+. \] Using Fourier analysis, stereographic projection and a removable-singularity argument, we classify the weighted $L^2$ boundary kernel without assuming boundedness of the boundary solution. This determines the bounded half-space kernel. Both kernels are generated by dilation and tangential translations. We further obtain sharp estimates for the projected spherical inverse.
Real-Space-RG for the drawups and drawdowns of run-and-tumble trajectories: universality classes for models with space-dependent velocities and switching rates

For one-dimensional run-and-tumble processes with the two velocities $v_{\pm}(x)$ and the two switching rates $γ_{\pm}(x)$, a given stochastic trajectory is an alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima corresponding to the switching events between the ballistic motions with velocities $v_{\pm}(x) $ in the two directions. The renormalized trajectory at scale $Γ$ is obtained by keeping only the alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima that are separated by drawups and drawdowns of amplitude bigger than $Γ$. Its statistical properties can be analyzed via the generalization of the previous work arxiv:2611.04853 concerning diffusion processes involving arbitrary diffusion coefficients $D(x)$ and Ito forces $F_I(x)$. The main result is that the scale function $s(x)$ of diffusion processes that depends only on the ratio $\frac{F_I(x)}{D(x) } $ is replaced by a pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ that depend only on the two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$. This pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ govern the exit probabilities from an interval and determine the universality classes of the renormalized trajectories: all run-and-tumble processes with the same two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$ share the same statistics of renormalized trajectories. This general framework is illustrated with examples that are compared to their diffusive counterparts : uniform symmetric and asymmetric processes on the whole line $x \in]-\infty,+\infty[$, geometric process on the half-line $x \in]0,+\infty[$, and an exponential functional of the telegraph process with a normalizable steady state.
Inverse energy transfer for 2D Navier--Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse

We prove inverse energy transfer for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse, confirming the 1979 prediction of Novikov and Sedov. Nonlinear interactions transfer kinetic energy from high to low frequencies over a common time interval that shrinks to the collapse time as the viscosity tends to zero. We prove that the net nonlinear transfer over this interval converges to the same positive constant across an expanding range of frequency cutoffs, with quantitative error bounds uniform in the cutoff.
Atlas-DeePC: Learning Behavioral Atlases for Predictive Control
Dian Jin; Zhiyuan Jin; Jeremy Coulson

Data-enabled Predictive Control (DeePC) uses linear combinations of recorded input-output trajectories to compute control actions without a parametric model. For nonlinear systems, these linear combinations may not satisfy the system dynamics, and the computational cost grows with dataset size. We propose Atlas-DeePC, which approximates the behavior of a dynamical system using a collection of low-dimensional subspaces, termed a behavioral atlas, to enable computationally efficient prediction and control. The atlas is constructed offline by clustering the data and fitting a subspace to each cluster. Online, the controller selects the subspace that best matches recent measurements and solves a predictive control problem parameterized by its orthonormal basis. A graph-based reference planner complements the controller by providing intermediate references across operating regions. We illustrate Atlas-DeePC on a planar robotic manipulator, where it achieves higher success rates and substantially lower online computation times than the compared controllers based on online data selection. An additional benchmark of an autonomous racing task is also included. The project website provides code and demonstrations https://dianjin-frederick.github.io/Atlas-DeePC/
Dongjing Ma; Peihe Wang; Hua Zhu

We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2φ(\ell/h)}{f}\, \barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)-h, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_φ(s)=\frac{sφ'(s)}{φ(s)} \ge k+1+δ, \qquad s a_φ'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_μ}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cotθ, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<θ\leπ/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_μ\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<θ<π$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.
Einstein contact metrics with integrable CR structure

We prove that every compact Einstein contact metric manifold of dimension at least $5$ with integrable associated CR structure is Sasakian. We show that without the assumption of compactness this result does not hold: namely, for every odd dimension at least $5$, we construct an explicit noncompact Einstein contact metric manifold, with integrable CR-structure, which is not Sasakian.
Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs

Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $τ=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $α$ satisfying $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|α-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(α;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.
Equivariant resolution of singularities for $T$-varieties in positive characteristic

Let the ground field be algebraically closed of positive characteristic. We prove that every variety endowed with an algebraic torus action whose general orbits have codimension at most three admits an equivariant resolution of singularities. The proof combines the description of such varieties in terms of proper polyhedral divisors and divisorial fans, the existence of log resolutions in dimension at most three, and the resolution of toroidal embeddings established by Kempf, Knudsen, Mumford and Saint-Donat.
ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization

Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set. In this work, we study preference-guided multi-objective optimization, where a predefined preference function is minimized over the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives. Leveraging a merit function that vanishes on the weak Pareto set, we propose a penalty-based min-max-min formulation, termed the M$^3$ problem, which unifies preference optimization and the enforcement of weak Pareto optimality in a single objective. We further develop ParetoM$^3$, a single-loop first-order algorithm for computing stationary solutions of the resulting M$^3$ problem. Under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption, we prove that ParetoM$^3$ finds an $ε$-stationary point of the M$^3$ problem that is also approximately weakly Pareto optimal for the original multi-objective problem when the penalty parameter is sufficiently large, with explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates. We also show that this stationarity notion recovers existing optimality criteria, including approximate preference stationarity and approximate Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, under the same assumptions used in prior works. Experiments on a synthetic benchmark, image classification, regression, and math reasoning demonstrate that ParetoM$^3$ reliably attains preferred weak Pareto optimal solutions while achieving strong practical performance. Code is available at https://github.com/tpgoodboy/ParetoM3.
What is... An Exceptional Set Estimate?

Exceptional set estimates are a fundamental topic of interest in projection theory. We introduce the topic through discrete geometry, and use this perspective to motivate some key results in the realm of geometric measure theory. To appear in the "What is?" series in the Notices of the AMS.
Fer expansion converges almost twice as far as Magnus for qubits

The Fer expansion writes the propagator of a time-dependent Hamiltonian as a product of unitary exponentials whose error decreases doubly exponentially with the number of factors, while the Magnus expansion improves by one order at a time. Its convergence, however, was guaranteed only below a radius of about $2.6058$, smaller than the Magnus radius $π$. We establish a guaranteed convergence threshold of about $6.2106$, or $1.98\,π$, for a qubit. This is almost twice the optimal universal Magnus threshold $π$; the bound on a single Fer step is sharp, while the exact convergence radius remains open.
Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations

Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.
Simultaneous recovery of elastic and viscous coefficients in a Kelvin-Voigt equation
Dong Qiu; Song-Ren Fu; Yeqiong Ye; Ting Zhou

In this paper, we study the simultaneous recovery of a spatially dependent elastic coefficient and a time- and space-dependent viscosity coefficient in a scalar Kelvin-Voigt equation. We prove that the displacement-to-traction map over any fixed time interval uniquely determines both coefficients, provided that the Riemannian metric induced by the viscosity is simple at each time. In the velocity formulation, the elastic term gives rise to a Volterra memory term involving second-order spatial derivatives, with a corresponding memory contribution to the boundary traction. We first determine all normal derivatives of both coefficients at the boundary using highly oscillatory boundary data. We then construct exact parabolic exponential solutions in the presence of memory and determine the viscosity by boundary rigidity. With the viscosity determined, an approximate identity argument reduces recovery of the elastic coefficient to injectivity of the scalar geodesic ray transform. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate a regularized finite-dimensional reconstruction of both coefficients from finitely many moments of the displacement-to-traction map.
Sergey Salishev; Anton Makarov; Oleg Granichin; Renata Avros; Zeev Volkovich

A unified framework is proposed that characterizes supervised deep classification as the decoding of error-correcting codes in the Shannon sense. Cross-entropy optimization is shown to align softmax classifiers with maximum-likelihood decoding, where logits map to Hamming distances to class-specific codewords. This correspondence explains the emergence of standard divergence objectives (e.g., Kullback-Leibler, Jeffreys) and provides a geometric basis for the stability of decision boundaries. Furthermore, the geometries of Neural Collapse and LeJEPA are identified as optimal constellations for decoding under isotropic noise. Unlike classical Error-Correcting Output Codes, deep networks are shown to learn effective codebooks in the feature space implicitly. This insight is leveraged to derive novel criteria for lossless quantization, improved knowledge distillation, and architectural regularization based on code redundancy. Finally, this perspective is extended to self-supervised encoders, offering a cohesive explanation for the geometry of latent representations in modern neural models.
Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
Thomas Nicosanti; Pavel Putrov; Johann Quenta-Raygada

We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.
Optimal polynomial decay and nonlinear stabilization for an indirectly damped wave-MGT system

We study a conservative wave equation coupled to a dissipative Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation by a zero-order interaction that is symmetric in augmented variables. A general modal proposition relates the exact resolvent and semigroup asymptotic constants through an asymptotically unitary diagonalization. Its application to this system yields the optimal fourth-order resolvent estimate and the exact linear decay constants. These estimates lead to nonlinear stabilization from small regular initial data. On smooth bounded domains, a weighted composition estimate that accommodates a singular third derivative of the source at zero gives the optimal state rate $t^{-3/4}$ and energy rate $t^{-3/2}$ for power and logarithmic sources. In dimension three, the result includes $f(u)=|u|^q u$ with $3/2<q<2$ and $f(u)=|u|^{γ-2}u\log|u|$ with $7/2<γ<4$, within the source ranges of the companion general-source theory. Dimension-dependent extensions hold through dimension seven in the same data space, and in arbitrary dimension with higher regularity and a higher order of vanishing at zero. A lower-regularity graph-norm theorem and a conditional transfer theorem for general sources are also proved. Each nonlinear small-data decay exponent is optimal among uniform estimates with the stated dependence on the initial-data norm.
Periodic orbits of quadratic polynomials of periods six and seven

The dynamics of quadratic polynomials is commonly studied by using the family of maps f_{c}(x) = x^{2} + c, where c include C. In this paper we form equations of periodic orbits of periods six and seven on a new (u,v)-plane and consider also the corresponding equations on the (x,y)-plane. The new (u,v)-model produces equations for the periods six and seven with significantly lower degree than the ones obtained by the previous models which enables us to find their solutions.
New Results on the Subfield Metric
Ana Kosovac; Jeanette Plechinger; Nikola Spirovski; Violetta Weger

In this paper, we further develop the theory of the recently introduced $λ$-subfield metric. We investigate extremal codes, classical bounds and asymptotic densities in this setting. We first study codes attaining a Singleton-type bound, called Maximum $λ$-subfield Distance (M$λ$D) codes. We establish structural restrictions on their parameters and extend the theory to sublinear codes. We then investigate the asymptotic density of M$λ$D codes in several parameter regimes and compare their behavior with that of MDS and MRD codes. We then turn to a Plotkin-like bound, where we construct a family of constant-weight codes attaining the bound and classify all non-degenerate linear constant-weight codes for $λ>1$. Finally, we complement the collection of classical coding-theoretic bounds available for the $λ$-subfield metric by deriving Griesmer-, Elias- and Johnson-type bounds.
Causal and conditional tail coefficients: asymptotics, inference and graph recovery

The causal tail coefficient (CTC) measures the influence of an extreme value of one variable on another variable and has been proposed as a tool for causal discovery in heavy-tailed models. Despite its popularity, the asymptotic behavior of its empirical counterpart has not been well understood. We develop an asymptotic theory for the rank-based CTC estimator with an intermediate threshold under nonparametric conditions that are satisfied by all standard copula models. A key observation is that the CTC is determined by the mean of a conditional tail limit distribution, which clarifies its interpretation and determines the asymptotic variance of the estimator. We establish joint asymptotic normality for the entire CTC matrix and prove consistency of a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference. For heavy-tailed linear and recursive max-linear structural equation models, we show that the CTC equals one if and only if the first variable is an ancestor of the second, which leads to confidence graphs for the ancestral graph with asymptotic coverage guarantees. All results extend to general conditional tail coefficients, defined as further functionals of the conditional tail limit distribution. A simulation study and an application to dietary intake data illustrate the methods.
Motivic Invariants of Automorphisms and the Plane Cremona Group
Ran Azouri; Anubhav Nanavaty; Jesse Pajwani

Recent work of Campbell and Zakharevich studies the $K$-theory spectrum of varieties. In previous work, the second author constructs a derived version of the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic, giving a map out of this spectrum. We analyse the morphism that the derived $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic induces out of $K_1(\mathrm{Var}_k)$. We obtain an explicit description of this map, which encodes information about automorphisms of varieties. We use Hermitian $K$-theory to obtain a geometric description for part of this morphism in terms of Hodge cohomology. This allows us to obtain structural results about the group $K_1(\mathrm{Var}_k)$. As an application, we use the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant minimal model programme for surfaces to construct an arithmetic invariant of a large class of involutions in the plane Cremona group. We use this to construct two non-conjugate de Jonquières involutions with isomorphic positive genus fixed curves over any perfect field $k$ of characteristic not $2$ with at least 6 elements which admits a quadratic extension.
Destabilization of Abelian-Higgs vortices at large Chern-Simons coupling
Emir Syahreza Fadhilla; Mulyanto; Hadi Susanto; Fiki Taufik Akbar; Bobby Eka Gunara

We study the effect of the Chern--Simons (CS) coupling on the radial spectral stability of axially symmetric vortices in the $(2+1)$-dimensional Abelian--Higgs model. From the linear stability approach, we obtain the dispersion relations of gauge field perturbations, which signal the existence of a critical CS coupling $k_{\rm c}$ that depends on Maxwell's coupling constant. For $k<k_{\rm c}$, the continuous spectrum is purely imaginary and the modes remain gapped. At $k=k_{\rm c}$, one of the modes becomes gapless, while for $k>k_{\rm c}$ real eigenvalues appear, corresponding to exponentially growing radial modes. Direct time-evolution simulations are consistent with the spectral analysis, which shows instability for $k>k_{\rm c}$. Below the threshold, the perturbed vortex relaxes toward its stationary profile, whereas above the threshold, growing fluctuations deform the core and propagate outward. These results show that the CS coupling controls radial spectral stability of Abelian-Higgs vortices, and destabilization occurs for sufficiently large CS coupling, relative to the Maxwell coupling.
The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory

We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},Σ},U_n^\mathrm{ét}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{ét}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric étale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $Σ$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.
On weakly m-convex sets, m=1,...,n-1, in n-dimensional Euclidean spaces

We study general topological properties of open and closed weakly $m$-convex sets, $m=1,\ldots, n-1$, in the real $n$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geqslant2$. An open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called weakly $m$-convex if, through every boundary point of the set, there passes an $m$-dimensional plane that does not intersect the set. A closed set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is weakly $m$-convex if it can be approximated from the outside by a countably decreasing family of open weakly $m$-convex sets. The set of all points in the complement of a given subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ through each of which every $m$-dimensional plane intersects the subset is called the $m$-nonconvexity-point set corresponding to the given subset. We prove that the nonempty $m$-nonconvexity-point set corresponding to an open weakly $m$-convex set is itself open and weakly $m$-convex, and that the interior of every closed weakly $m$-convex set with nonempty interior is weakly $m$-convex for every $m=1,\ldots, n-1$.
Frobenius and perfection in framed motives

We develop explicit Frobenius and perfection arguments for framed motives over imperfect fields. In positive characteristic, power framing homotopies and local framed transfers make relative Frobenius invertible after inverting the characteristic. Descent through successive Frobenius twists then gives a proof of strict homotopy invariance for homotopy invariant quasi-stable additive framed presheaves and identifies the canonical comparison with the perfect closure as a stable Nisnevich local equivalence of framed motives. We extend the comparison to E-framed motives for every motivic Thom spectrum E. It also yields the cancellation theorem and the cone theorem. For commutative symmetric Thom ring spectra, we identify triangulated categories of effective E-framed motives and effective E-modules and prove perfection invariance of these triangulated categories. All comparisons are made after inverting the exponential characteristic.
Painlevé quadrics and their confluence for the dispersionless Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
Benoit Huard Lewis Patterson; Anh-Asma Koheeallee

We construct and study a distinguished class of solutions of the dispersionless Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (dKP) equation whose geometry is governed by the first and second Painlevé equations. The level surfaces of these solutions correspond to three geometric families of central quadrics, and we determine when their level surfaces degenerate into planes. In the parabolic family parametrised by $\mathrm{P_I}$, degenerate levels occur at the stationary points of the transcendent. For the hyperbolic family parametrised by rational solutions of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$, we show that degenerate levels occur at points where consecutive solutions intersect and we give a precise count of such degeneracies. In the homogeneous elliptic family, the Hastings--McLeod solution of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$ is characterised, up to sign, as the unique non-trivial real pole-free solution with Airy asymptotics whose quadric has no finite degenerate level. Finally, under critical scaling, the quadrics generated by the $n$-th rational Painlevé-II solution converge locally, and away from poles, to the parabolic quadrics associated with the Painlevé-I tritronquée solution, with error $O(n^{-1/5})$.
Consensus-Based Optimization of Path-Integral Free Energy for Model Predictive Control
Daisuke Inoue; Yuyang Huang; Dante Kalise

We propose CBO-MPPI, a sampling-based predictive controller that applies consensus-based optimization (CBO) to the free energy underlying model predictive path integral control (MPPI). Under hard constraints, this objective rewards sampling neighborhoods containing feasible, low-cost trajectories under perturbation. Standard MPPI performs a local stochastic search by updating one nominal control sequence from Gaussian perturbations around it. In CBO-MPPI, we estimate the free energy at multiple nominal centers from local rollouts. These estimates define a shared consensus that guides drift and diffusion, and the final selected center supplies an MPPI weighted-mean output. For the associated mean-field model, we establish well-posedness and, under additional assumptions, convergence toward a free-energy minimizer. In simulations of obstacle navigation, pendulum swing-up, and planar-arm manipulation under equal rollout budgets, at high temperatures, CBO-MPPI attains lower free energy than MPPI and multi-start MPPI and maintains greater obstacle clearance than CBO-MPC.
The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth

We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. For the full water wave system, we derive an explicit instability index and rigorously classify its sign throughout the depth-vorticity plane. With gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber normalized to one, we identify a unique minimum depth $h_{\text{crit}}\approx1.36271$, below which Benjamin-Feir instability is absent for every vorticity. Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents. In particular, at each fixed finite depth, constant vorticity of sufficiently large magnitude suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability. Moreover, any constant vorticity $γ\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schrödinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.
Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs

Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.
Movable Antenna-Aided ISAC: A Time- and Frequency-Division Framework
Yuyan Zhou; Haocheng Hua; Jie Xu; Rui Zhang

This paper investigates movable-antenna (MA)-enhanced integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) under time division duplex (TDD) and frequency division duplex (FDD) protocols, where sensing and communications occupy orthogonal time and frequency resources, respectively. A wideband target-position Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) is derived under a pulse-radar framework with pulse compression, incorporating delay and angle estimation error bounds in Cartesian coordinates. Both bounds depend on sensing power; the delay bound also depends on sensing bandwidth, while the angle bound depends on the effective aperture determined by the antenna position vector (APV). A worst-case position CRB over a prescribed target region ensures robust sensing performance. For multiuser downlink communication, joint APV and resource-allocation problems are formulated for TDD and FDD to maximize the minimum achievable user rate subject to the sensing requirement. An alternating optimization algorithm is developed for FDD, while TDD is addressed by searching over feasible sensing pulse numbers combined with APV optimization. Representative scenarios clarify how MA improves channel orthogonality and enlarges the sensing aperture, and how these effects shape the TDD/FDD rate comparison. Numerical results show that APV optimization enlarges the communication-sensing tradeoff region over fixed-position antenna benchmarks. The optimized configurations exhibit distinct tendencies: TDD favors a larger antenna position variance, whereas FDD favors better channel orthogonality among users.

We establish stability results for internal homs of $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets, a framework motivated by nerves of Frobenius monoids in the category of relations. Rotations are modelled through edge witnesses and horn-filling conditions, without requiring unique fillers. For $\varepsilon$-fibrant objects $X$ and $Y$, we prove that the internal hom $\mathrm{Fun}(X,Y)$ satisfies the $\varepsilon$-coherence conditions and admits fillers for all $\varepsilon$-horns of dimension at least two. Its subobject consisting of simplices whose vertices correspond to $η$-edge-preserving maps is $\varepsilon$-fibrant. We also introduce $η\varepsilon$-simplicial sets by adding explicit $η$-witnesses and prove that the internal hom of two $η\varepsilon$-fibrant objects is again $η\varepsilon$-fibrant. Our proofs use adjunctions relating $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets and paracyclic sets. We characterise the $\varepsilon$-horn filling property by requiring the corresponding counit to be a trivial Kan fibration. Consequently, for every object satisfying this property, coherent choices of rotations of each simplex form a contractible Kan complex.
The Möbius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor

The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular Möbius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the Möbius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$. As a consequence, the sum of the absolute values of the Möbius function over this interval equals twice the number of ordered factorizations of $n/q$.

Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslantμ_2/(μ_n-δ)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $μ_2$ and $μ_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $δ$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component. Equivalently, its algebraic connectivity and independence number sum to its order. We also determine all vertex cuts attaining the toughness, and show that for regular graphs, the equality graphs are exactly the complete multipartite graphs with parts of equal size.
Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors

The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.
Representing in Low rank II: Virtual structure and Isomorphism problem
Robynn Corveleyn; Geoffrey Janssens; Doryan Temmerman

We group theoretically characterise the finite groups $G$ and number fields $F$ such that all $F$-representations of reduced degree at least $2$ are so-called exceptional. If $G$ is not a $2$-group, we obtain a full classification. Secondly, we determine whether such groups are uniquely determined by their group algebra $FG$.
