The proposed constraint-sampling technique maintains a set of recently violated constraints and draws the constraint used in each iteration uniformly either from this set or from the set of all constraints. This keeps its per-iteration arithmetic overhead independent of the number of constraints. In simulations on synthetic convex optimization problems and in the synthesis of a control barrier function for the Dubins Car, the constraint-sampling technique is shown to significantly outperform uniform constraint sampling.
The structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups of the real projective plane

In this paper we study the structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups $B_n(RP^2)$ of the real projective plane $RP^2$. It is known that the isomorphism classes of these subgroups are comprised of cyclic, dicyclic and binary polyhedral groups. Using specific elements of $B_n(RP^2)$, we construct embeddings of the cyclic and dicyclic subgroups, we show that there is a single conjugacy class of the maximal dicyclic groups, and for small values of n, we also construct embeddings of the bin- ary tetrahedral and octahedral groups. One interesting phenomenon that occurs is the existence of isomorphism classes of finite subgroups that admit embeddings in $B_n(RP^2)$ as both maximal finite and non-maximal subgroups. Up to conjugacy, we describe completely the lattice of the finite subgroups of $B_n(RP^2)$ for n = 3, 4, 5. Some of our results regarding the number of conjugacy classes of finite subgroups are obtained using the relation between $B_n(RP^2)$ and the mapping class group of $RP^2$ relative to n points. We also provide a new presentation of $B_n(RP^2)$ which has some interesting properties with respect to the classical presentation of Van Buskirk.
Discrete unique continuation for Schrödinger equations
Torunn S. Jensen; Didier Pilod; João P. G. Ramos

We study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional Schrödinger equations. We prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^α$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^β$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a Schrödinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of Gevrey class $σ\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,σ\}\big(α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, provided that $α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)<1$. Unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. We first show that, whenever $α+β<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the Schwartz class at all times. We then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $Γ=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from Fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the Morgan-type uncertainty principle of Escauriaza, Kenig, Ponce and Vega.
Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities

The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.
Asymptotic transportation cost of the optimal matching subject to different boundary conditions

We establish equality between several asymptotic limits of the transportation cost between stationary random measures, with respect to the Euclidean distance cost raised to the $p$-th power, with different boundary conditions. Our approach relies on a comparison with the optimizer of the mean transportation cost between the two random measures, which is defined on the whole space. In particular we do not use any PDE techniques related to the regularity theory for optimal transport maps.
Spectrum of non-Hermitian self-normalized random matrices with heavy tails

We study non-Hermitian matrices $Y_n$ obtained by normalizing each row of an $n\times n$ matrix with i.i.d. entries to Euclidean norm one. We consider regularly varying radial tails of index $α\in[0,2]$, with $α=0$ denoting slowly varying tails, and the broader normal domain of attraction. For $0<α<2$, assuming angular tail convergence, we prove convergence in probability of the empirical singular value measures of every shift $Y_n-zI$ to deterministic laws characterized by the root resolvent of a column-normalized directed Poisson weighted infinite tree, extending the framework of Bordenave, Caputo and Chafai (arXiv:1006.1713). Under a bounded density assumption, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges in probability to a deterministic law $μ_α^{\mathrm{SN}}$ on $\mathbb{C}$. This law is rotationally invariant, is supported in the closed unit disk with outer radius one, and has neither point atoms nor mass on the unit circle. The laws interpolate between $δ_0$ as $α\downarrow0$ and the circular law as $α\uparrow2$. These also describe the limiting eigenvalue distributions of $Y_n$ for real entries with slowly varying tails and for centered entries with bounded density in the normal domain of attraction, respectively. For real symmetric entries with bounded density, the spectral radius converges to one in probability for $0<α\le2$, using the upper bound of Francois, Heiny and Hu (arXiv:2608.28169). We also give a general criterion identifying the outer support radius of rotationally invariant laws from fractional moments of fresh cavity weights, under explicit trace and radial-recovery assumptions.
On a PDE-ODE-ODE model for meniscus tissue regeneration with space-dependent, possibly degenerate diffusion tensor
Nishith Mohan; Ahmad Hussein; Bernd Simeon; Christina Surulescu

We investigate a tissue regeneration model that describes the coupled dynamics of human mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), chondrocytes, and newly formed extracellular matrix (ECM). The system features motility terms only for the mesenchymal stem cells, more precisely myopic diffusion and haptotaxis towards increasing ECM; all of those terms involve a space-dependent, possibly degenerating tensor. The chondrocytes are obtained from MSCs by differentiation and provide positive feedback to MSCs via dedifferentiation. The considered macroscopic model was obtained by upscaling from a formulation within the kinetic theory of active particles. Under appropriate assumptions we prove global existence of classical solutions in 2D and 3D in the case of a nondegenerating tensor and global existence of weak solutions in 2D when the diffusion tensor is allowed to degenerate. Numerical simulations are performed in 2D in order to illustrate the solution behavior.
Semiclassical Scaling Laws of Magnus Quantum Algorithms under Harmonic Confinement

The simulation of semiclassical Schrödinger dynamics is often hindered by rapid oscillations, where classical numerical methods and quantum simulation algorithms can suffer severe precision loss as the semiclassical parameter $\varepsilon \to 0$. In this work, we uncover a surprising robustness of high-order Magnus quantum algorithms in the semiclassical regime. We establish two important results. First, we extend the theory of Magnus superconvergence from free-particle reference dynamics to a general class of Schrödinger operators whose reference Hamiltonian includes harmonic confinement. Second, and more importantly, we reveal a nontrivial semiclassical scaling law: while the expansion remainder term bound suggests an error prefactor of $O(\varepsilon^{-(p+1)})$ for a $p$th-order method, we prove that the loss is in fact order-independent and collapses to $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ for all $p$. The key analytical mechanism is the exact Egorov transport associated with quadratic flows in semiclassical Weyl quantization, which enables a symbol-level analysis of the interaction-picture Hamiltonian and its Magnus commutators. Our results show that high-order Magnus quantum algorithms remain far more robust in the semiclassical regime than naive series remainder term counting would suggest.
First Order Convergence of Representative Volume Element with Mixed Boundary Condition

We study the cell problem with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann boundary condition to reconstruct the effective matrix for two-dimensional scalar divergence-form equations with bounded measurable, and possibly nonsymmetric coefficients. We prove uniform invertibility of the mean-gradient matrix. Moreover, we derive the first-order error estimate when the medium is periodic.
Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
Erwin Luesink; Archishman Saha; Tanya Schmah; Cristina Stoica

For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.
Integer Decomposition Property of Edge Polytopes of Weighted Oriented Graphs
Jennifer Biermann; Kuei-Nuan Lin; Augustine O'Keefe

We classify the lattice polytopes arising from vertex-weighted oriented graphs that have the integer decomposition property (IDP). Allowing vertex weights and edge orientations introduces non-vertex lattice points in the polytope which need to be accounted for when studying the IDP. We can then identify forbidden induced subgraphs in the sense that their presence obstructs the IDP for the supergraph. We establish positive results for several families of graphs under suitable orientation and coprimality conditions, including weighted oriented paths and cycles, and show that any weighted oriented tree with a unique sink has the IDP.
Hinge comparison and excess estimates via modified Hessian bounds on manifolds with density

We study geometric consequences of modified Hessian estimates on Riemannian manifolds with density. For general radial functions, we derive tensorial, spectral, and trace identities for the modified Hessian in the original metric. We also establish a comparison identity relating the modified Hessians of two radial functions and characterize when they are proportional. We then prove a hinge comparison theorem under an upper bound on the modified Hessian, yielding a weighted law of cosines and lower bounds for the excess function. Finally, under nonnegative weighted sectional curvature and suitable density control assumptions, we obtain an Abresch-Gromoll-type upper excess estimate.
Accelerated Transformed Primal Dual Methods for Smooth Convex Optimization Problems with Affine Equality Constraints

Accelerated transformed primal--dual (ATPD) methods are proposed for smooth convex optimization problems with affine equality constraints. The methods combine primal--dual dynamics with a transformation designed to accelerate convergence. In the strongly convex case, ATPD achieves an accelerated linear convergence rate and matches the known lower bounds on first-order oracle complexity in terms of gradient evaluations and matrix--vector products. The analysis distinguishes these two types of computational work when assessing the complexity of the method. For general convex objectives, a homotopy perturbation strategy is introduced, and an accelerated sublinear rate for the modified Lyapunov energy is proved under a uniform boundedness condition on the primal iterates at all homotopy stages. The acceleration mechanism is based on an exponentially stable ATPD flow and a modified discrete Lyapunov function. This continuous-time perspective guides the construction and analysis of the discrete methods. Numerical experiments on policy evaluation and constrained signal reconstruction problems support the theory and illustrate the efficiency of the proposed methods.
Spin-Boson Hamiltonians as Generators of Spin-Dressed Bogoliubov Dynamics

Following Bach, Lieb and Solovej, quadratic Hamiltonians can be defined as generators of unitary groups implementing one-parameter groups of Bogoliubov transformations. We develop an analogous dynamical definition of generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians. For a single spin level, we review results of Guichardet and Dereziński: the van Hove Hamiltonians, including the renormalized ones, are exactly the generators of affine Bogoliubov dynamics that do not mix creation and annihilation operators. For several spin levels, there is no analogue of this group, and we introduce spin-dressed implementations, that is to say the free flow of the fields is implemented up to bounded operator-valued displacements, which vanish at a rate measured by a so-called regularity scale and have a spin observable, the coupling map, as derivative at time zero. The one-particle Hamiltonian $Υ$ and the coupling map are determined by the Hamiltonian, and the field obeys a quantum Langevin equation. Spin-dressed implementations in Fock space, at the finest scale and for form factors in $D(Υ^{-1/2})$, are exactly the generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians, unique up to the spin Hamiltonian. At the roughest scale, the renormalized spin--boson Hamiltonian of a two-level system with ultraviolet-singular form factor and arbitrary tunnelling is a spin-dressed implementation, and the definition alone yields asymptotic Weyl operators on the test functions along which the coupling map is integrable, a dense set under standard assumptions.

Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2μ$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + μ$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $μ$ and maximum degree $Δ$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures. Our constructions have reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{3}{2}μ-2$. We also provide counterexamples that are $Δ$-regular, we show that every graph has reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{1}{2} μ$, and we advertise an extension to hypergraphs. It is now much more mysterious how the diameter behaves, so we propose a number of open problems.
Continuum space hierarchical Cannings process: II. Genealogies and ancestral web

The present paper is the second in a series of three papers in which we consider a \emph{spatial multi-type population model} arising as the many-individuals-per-site limit of individual-based models. The evolution mechanisms in this model are: migration, Fleming-Viot resampling, $Λ_0$-Cannings resampling, and $(Λ_k)_{k \in \N}$-Cannings block-resampling. This evolution leads to a collection of \emph{measure-valued} processes indexed by a continuum geographic space $Ω_N^\infty$, called the \emph{continuum hierarchical group}, obtained as the limit of a discrete hierarchical group $Ω_N^L$ as $L\to\infty$, where $Ω_N^L = \oplus_{k \geq -L} Z_N$ with $Z_N$ the cyclical group of order $N$. On this geographic space, each component is a probability measure on a type space $\K$. In the first paper \cite{gh1}, we \emph{constructed} the measure-valued process on $Ω_N^\infty$ describing the type frequencies in the population and identified its main properties. We found a \emph{dichotomy} between this process being \emph{stochastic} (= locally monotype) or \emph{deterministic} (= locally multitype). In the present paper we turn to the \emph{genealogies} of the population on $Ω_N^\infty$.
Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
Louison Bocquet-Nouaille; Jérôme Morio; Benjamin Bobbia; Philippe Naveau

Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.
Poincaré polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
Marco Aldi; Samuel Bevins; Eleftherios Chatzitheodoridis; Sergio Da Silva; Quincy Frias; Tomás Mejía Gómez

We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincaré polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.

We obtain infinite spin representations of the super-Poincaré algebra from a higher-derivative superparticle action on a super-Minkowski background in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions. Super-twistor transforms are performed, and used to deduce first-quantised spectra.
Real log canonical thresholds and real log canonical thresholds with signs

In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.
Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets

For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.
Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation

We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. Localizing this functional inequality to radially aligned velocity cells with the critical weight $\la{v}^{3/2}$ and coupling it with a weighted truncated entropy identity across nested exterior domains yields a superlinear De Giorgi recurrence that bounds the velocity tail uniformly in $\R^3$.
The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
Bonan Chen; Xiang Fang; Feng Guo

We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.
Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
Christa Cuchiero; Francesca Primavera; Sara Svaluto-Ferro

We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature. We show that their expected signature can be computed by solving linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, providing a tractable foundation for learning procedures. Specifically, the learning of a generalized score function for jump diffusions, a key ingredient of our generative modeling framework, can be reduced to solving linear ODEs and a deterministic optimization problem. We further prove that polynomial jump-diffusions can be embedded into this framework, and that their expected signature reduces to a finite-dimensional system of linear ODEs. Building on this result, we develop an alternative approach for finite-dimensional data, based on inverse signature matching, a method that learns the score by matching the expected signature of the reverse process with that of the inverse forward signature.
How to arrange four points in the plane

Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[ D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[ \begin{cases} \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1, \text{a rhombus with angle }θ\in(π/3,π/2),&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}<1. \end{cases} \]
A lift of Baxter's cyclic summation identity with applications to quantum topology

While studying the chiral Potts model Baxter discovered a cyclic analogue of Ramanujan's ${}_1ψ_{1}$ summation identity. This identity was subsequently interpreted by Faddeev and Kashaev as a pentagon relation for the quantum dilogarithm function, a key ingredient in cyclic quantizations of Teichmüller theory. Existing forms of the identity involve multivalued functions so one must either accept overall phase ambiguities or keep track of branches on a complicated covering space. In this paper we show how to remove the phase ambiguities with a much simpler choice of covering space. As an application we compute the Fourier transform of the holonomy $R$-matrices of the author and Reshetikhin. A corollary is a simpler proof that Kashaev's $R$-matrix is a specialization of the colored Jones $R$-matrix, which was first shown by Murakami and Murakami.
Direct Search meets Frank-Wolfe: Inexact Derivative-Free Bilevel Optimization over Polytopes
Matteo Pernini; Francesco Rinaldi; Gabriele Sanguin; Marco Viola

In this work we propose BLDS-SIMPLEX, a derivative-free direct search method for the solution of bilevel optimization with polytope constraints at the upper level. The proposed method reformulates the feasible set using barycentric coordinates and explores it using Frank-Wolfe-type directions, relying on a fixed-accuracy black-box oracle for the upper-level objective function. We analyze its convergence properties and complexity in the case of smooth reduced objective; additionally, we analyze a variant for the case of nonsmooth objectives and show its convergence to a specific kind of stationary point that we introduce as a natural generalization to the classic stationarity notions in this setting. Numerical tests on modified instances from BOLIB support the viability of our new approach.
Certified Hierarchical Planning and Tracking: A Learning-Based Approach
Weijian Li; Vince Kurtz; Panos J. Antsaklis; Hai Lin

In this paper, we develop a hierarchical control framework for nonlinear dynamical systems with safety constraints. Specifically, a low-fidelity model is introduced for trajectory planning, while a tracking controller is designed for the high-fidelity system. We first characterize the tracking error bound (TEB) using a storage function. Then, we formulate the synthesis of the tracking controller, the storage function, and the TEB as an optimization problem. Following that, we develop an offline learning approach to approximately solve the optimization problem, by incorporating behavior cloning and satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solver. We further integrate the learned controller and the TEB into online tracking of the high-fidelity system. This framework enables the control of high-dimensional nonlinear systems with safety guarantees, while maintaining computational efficiency for real-time implementation. Finally, experiments are provided for illustration.
Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion

We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.
Non self-similar solutions to the Ricci flow coming out of metric cones
Alix Deruelle; Tristan Ozuch; Felix Schulze

Given an asymptotically conical unstable expanding gradient Ricci soliton, we provide the existence of a family of Ricci flows starting at the same metric cone up to isometry. Moreover, the family of solutions we construct is shown to be parametrized by positive modes of the weighted Lichnerowicz operator associated to the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton. Each solution of this family is shown not to be induced by an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. If the background expander has no non-trivial infinitesimal deformations, we show furthermore that the solutions we provide are not self-similar. We finally prove that solutions are distinct up to isometries preserving the potential function of the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton.
A binomial-adjusted $θ$-trapezoidal tau-leaping method for chemical kinetic systems
Maximilian Scott; Sam McCallum; James Foster

In Hu, Li and Min (2011), the authors propose a weak second order accurate $θ$-trapezoidal method as an improvement to the classical tau-leaping method. However, for complex chemical kinetic systems their model's underlying analytical assumptions can fail to hold in practice, leading to a significant reduction in its computational effectiveness. Here we introduce a modification to the method which allows it to regain desirable convergence characteristics, both given the original and a relaxed version of the underlying assumptions. We confirm this improvement through a local error analysis and present numerical examples showing it consistently performs either better or comparable to the $θ$-trapezoidal method.
Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
Tattwamasi Amrutam; Diptesh Saha; Xumin Wang

We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
Rainbow matchings in non-uniform hypergraph systems

Let $s\geq 1$, $r_1, r_2,\dots, r_{s+1}$ be given positive integers and $r=\max\{r_1, r_2,\ldots, r_{s+1}\}$. We prove that if $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ is a family of hypergraphs on a ground set of $n$ vertices, $n\geq 4r^2(s+1)$, such that $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$ and $|\mathcal{F}_i|>\binom{n}{r_i}-\binom{n-s}{r_i}-\binom{n-s-r}{r_i-1}+1$, for all $i \in [s+1]$, then $\mathcal{F}$ admits a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ or there exists $W \in \binom{[n]}{s}$ such that $W$ is a vertex cover of $\mathcal{F}_i$, for all $i \in [s+1]$. This improves upon the previously known range $n>2r^3s$ to $n>4r^2(s+1)$. Moreover, for a given family $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ of hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$, we give a best possible Ore-degree condition for $\mathcal{F}_{i}$'s that guarantees the existence of a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ for $\mathcal{F}$.
Characterizations of Pettis Integrable Multifunctions in Locally Convex Spaces

In this paper, we present characterizations of Pettis integrability in $bcc(X)$ and $cwk(X)$ of a multifunction $Γ: Ω\to cc(X)$, where $(Ω, Σ, μ)$ is a complete finite measure space and $cc(X)$ $(bcc(X), cwk(X))$ is the family of all nonempty convex closed (bounded convex closed, convex weakly compact) subsets of a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space $X$. Incidentally, a convergence theorem for scalarly integrable multifunctions is proved. As an application, we are going to prove full characterizations of Pettis integrability for fuzzy maps defined on $Ω$ and taking values in the generalized fuzzy number hyperspace $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$.
Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
Sushovan Majhi; Atish Mitra; Žiga Virk

We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for $n,m\ge2$ over an uncountable field, the classes that contain these families admit no such embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance $2(n+m)$ is a lower bound, attained for one generator and for two generators with at most one relation; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.
A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$

We exhibit a congruence subgroup $Γ\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_Γ$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.

Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators. Our central example is a closed Majorana chain, a 1-dimensional topological superconductor, embedded in 3 dimensions. We construct a loop-flip process with phase $+i$, refining the usual $\pm 1$ loop-flip invariant through intermediate transfer of fermion parity between the chain and physical fermions. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two $\mathbb Z_4$ toric codes enriched by $\mathbb Z_2$ charge-conjugation symmetry, with identical anyon statistics but distinct gauged theories: the quantum doubles of the dihedral group $D_4$ and the quaternion group $Q_8$. We provide two complementary constructions of statistical processes. The first extends the Smith normal form algorithm in [Phys. Rev. X $\textbf{16}$, 011010 (2026), arXiv:2412.01886] to higher groups, generating processes from lattice geometry and prescribed local moves. For a finite higher group $\mathbb G$, we prove that statistical processes on a $d$-sphere are classified by $H_{d+2}(B\mathbb G,\mathbb Z)$. The second constructs processes directly from homology classes without examining exponentially many defect configurations, enabling us to study statistics for complex higher-group structures where the previous method is computationally prohibitive. These processes detect boundary anomalies of higher-group symmetry-protected topological phases. For example, we distinguish 2-group anomalies in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions. Higher-group statistics provide new invariants for characterizing coupled defects in quantum many-body systems.
Non-existence of closed embedded magnetic geodesics
We give a counterexample to S. Novikov's 1982 conjecture that every Riemannian $2$-sphere contains a closed embedded curve of curvature $c$ for every $c>0$.
An algorithm for solving the Burgers equation based on rational approximations and the collocation method
I. A. Bugoets; B. V. Semisalov

We propose a numerical method for solving initial-boundary value problems for the Burgers equation that takes into account the presence of singularities of the analytic continuation of the solution into the complex plane. The algorithm uses rational approximations, a collocation method and a new scheme for time discretization combined with the relaxation method. An adaptive strategy is developed to account for the location of the singular point of the solution. Solutions to the well-known benchmark problem with a sine-shaped initial condition are obtained for the values of the viscosity as low as nu = 10^-8. Verification of the numerical results in such an extreme parameter regime makes it necessary to modify a classical formula for the exact solution so as to avoid floating-point overflow during its computation. The developed method is compared with an algorithm employing the Runge-Kutta scheme, and the conditions under which each approach yields superior results are outlined. An important feature of the proposed method is its capability to track the singular point of the solution. To verify this, we consider a problem whose solution has a simple analytical form and demonstrate that the exact and approximate coordinates of the singular point of the solution agree with high accuracy, even when the singularity comes extremely close to the domain of the problem. Taking the location of the singular point into account yields significant gains in both accuracy and run time relative to other methods.
Ramsey numbers of loose triangles versus cliques
Ayush Basu; Abhishek Dhawan; Abhishek Methuku

An $r$-uniform loose triangle $C_3$ consists of three edges that intersect pairwise in exactly one vertex and have no vertex common to all three. For graphs, this is the usual triangle, and the Ramsey number $R(C_3,K_t)$ has order of magnitude $t^2/\log t$ by celebrated results of Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi and of Kim. Kostochka, Mubayi, and Verstraëte proved that $R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})=O_r(t^{3/2})$ for every fixed $r\ge3$ and showed that this bound is sharp up to a logarithmic factor. Motivated by the logarithmic saving in the graph case, they conjectured in 2013 that the upper bound could be improved to $o(t^{3/2})$.This conjecture has since received significant attention and has been reiterated in several papers. We prove the conjecture by showing that, for every fixed $r\ge3$, \[ R(C_3,K_t^{(r)}) =O_r\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\log\log t}}\right). \]
On real-analytic non-degeneracy of left-symmetric algebras in dimension 3

In this paper, we show that any three-dimensional differentially non-degenerate left-symmetric algebra over $\mathbb R$ is non-degenerate both in the formal and real-analytic categories via the correspondence with Nijenhuis operators.
Stability Conditions on Twisted Derived Categories I: Existence and Full Numerical Support

We prove that for every nonempty smooth projective variety $X$ over an arbitrary field and every Brauer class $α$, the twisted derived category $D^b(X,α)$ admits a Bridgeland stability condition with full numerical support. Based on Chunyi Li's construction and its extension to arbitrary fields, we establish uniform phase control under tensoring by an Azumaya algebra and calibrate the resulting slicing to the induced central charge. We further show that the constructed stability condition is geometric and satisfies a mass--Hom bound, which persists throughout its connected component.
Gradient stability for the Sobolev inequality with optimal dimensional dependence

Figalli and Zhang [29] established gradient stability for the sharp Sobolev inequality with the optimal exponent $r_p=\max\{2,p\}$. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$, the corresponding optimal stability constant $\mathsf C_{n,p}$ admits effective upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-1}$ for all integers $n>p$. In particular, the dimensional dependence $n^{-1}$ is optimal. Our result extends the optimal dimensional dependence established for $p=2$ by Dolbeault, Esteban, Figalli, Frank, and Loss [18] to every $p>1$.
On the packing-dimension analogue of Bourgain's constant

For every $n\geq 2$, we construct a domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose harmonic measure has packing dimension $n$. That is, the packing analogue of Bourgain's constant is zero, in contrast with Bourgain's constant, which is positive. Moreover, the elliptic measure of the same domain also has packing dimension $n$ for every uniformly elliptic matrix.
Permutation polynomials of given index up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence

Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\ell$ be a divisor of $q-1$. We classify the permutation polynomials of $\mathbb F_q$ of polynomial index exactly $\ell$ up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence $G(X)\equiv uF(vX^d)\pmod{X^q-X}$, where $u,v\in\mathbb F_q^*$ and $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$, and we count the classes. For polynomials vanishing at $0$, the classes are the orbits of an explicit finite group on vectors of values at the $\ell$-th roots of unity. Through the permutation it induces on the roots of unity, each orbit lies over a double coset of the symmetric group $S_\ell$ with respect to its translation subgroup and an explicit affine group, and the stabilizers are explicit. For polynomials with nonzero constant term the action is free. Burnside's lemma, Möbius inversion over the coefficient support and congruences along the cycles of affine permutations give an exact formula for the number of classes. For fixed $\ell\geqslant2$ these numbers are quasi-polynomials in $s=(q-1)/\ell$ of degree at most $\ell-1$, with period dividing $\ell$ for odd $\ell$ and $2\ell$ for even $\ell$; for polynomials vanishing at $0$ the degree is exactly $\ell-1$, and we determine the leading coefficient. For odd prime $\ell$ and for $\ell=4$ the counts are given in closed form. For index four we also count the binomials and trinomials at each admissible coefficient support. The sums of two binomial counts that occur are expressed through quartic Jacobi sums and Frobenius traces of elliptic curves and of a curve of genus two; one of the elliptic curves is the reduction of the curve $Y^2=X^3+8X^2+32X$, which has no complex multiplication over $\mathbb Q$. The trinomial counts are expressed through quartic cyclotomic numbers and these sums. All these terms cancel when the counts with a fixed residue of the vanishing order modulo $s$ are added.
GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris

We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $β>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $θ_1,θ_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). We establish GFF limits sequentially, in particular resolving the analogous problem for the $(2+1)$D SOS. A crucial ingredient is an improved RG analysis for interacting dimers, which is of independent interest: it relaxes the assumptions on interactions from being uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ to only being typically small.

Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. In fact, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $h$, and all nonnegative real numbers $α_1,\ldots,α_h$ with $α_1+\cdots+α_h=1$, there are subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_h\subseteq G$ satisfying \[ G=A_1\cdots A_h, \qquad |A_1|\leq |G|^{α_1}, \qquad |A_i|\leq C|G|^{α_i}\quad(2\leq i\leq h). \] Consequently, for every $h$ there is a constant $c_h$ such that every finite group $G$ has a subset $A$ with \[ A^h=G\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A|\leq c_h|G|^{1/h}. \]
Optimal strong convergence rates of explicit stabilized method for the Galerkin finite element discretization SPDEs driven by multiplicative noise
Junwei Huang; Aiguo Xiao; Xiao Tang

Explicit stabilized methods provide an efficient approach to stiff systems arising from deterministic parabolic equations, yet rigorous convergence theory for their application to stochastic partial differential equations remains scarce. To the best of our knowledge, the only prior fully discrete strong convergence analysis of explicit stabilized integrators for SPDEs is due to [A. Abdulle et al. IMA J. Numer. Anal. 43(1)(2023), pp. 258--292] and it is restricted to additive noise. The present work addresses the extension to multiplicative noise, by coupling Galerkin finite element spatial discretization with explicit stabilized time integrators. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and appropriate spatial regularity conditions, we derive the strong error bound $\mathcal{O}(h^{1+r}+τ^{1/2})$ with $r\in[0,1)$, which achieves the optimal temporal strong convergence rate $1/2$ for the considered family of methods. One- and two-dimensional numerical tests with multiplicative noise validate the predicted convergence rates and compare the computational performance of explicit stabilized methods against the linearly implicit Euler method.
Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise

In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.
Finite multiple harmonic sums and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values

We introduce lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values and construct their harmonic regularizations. We show that they are independent of the branch of the $p$-adic logarithm and satisfy harmonic product relations. We express finite multiple harmonic sums as alternating convolutions of harmonic-regularized $p$-adic multiple zeta values and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values. This gives a $p$-adic analogue of the classical truncation identity, which reduces to the inversion relation between ordinary and star harmonic-regularized values when the truncation point is $1$. For truncation point $p$, it relates finite multiple zeta values to $p$-adic multiple zeta values.
When can local unitaries generate a complete orthogonal basis?
Julian Eisfeld; Hermann Kampermann; Nikolai Wyderka

The question of local encodability asks: can a given, multipartite pure quantum state be completed to an orthonormal basis using only local unitary rotations? If any such state in a given system has this property, it is called universally locally encodable (ULE), a feature, which has applications in quantum information theory, engineering and math. Despite its easy formulation, the answer to this question depends nontrivially on the local dimensions of the system: While universal local encodability is known for $2\times 2$, $4\times 4$ and $8\times 8$-dimensional systems, it was so-far only conjectured to hold in $3\times 3$, and non-ULE was recently proved for systems of four and more qubits by Pauwels and Gühne. Furthermore, we construct (among others) universal local encodings in dimensions $d\times2$ for $d\ge2$, in dimensions $d\times3$ for $d=3,4$ and $d\ge6$, and in every bipartite system with one or two infinite-dimensional subsystems. For finite-dimensional multipartite systems, we turn a heuristic parameter count into a necessary condition for universality, which excludes universal local encodability in infinitely many cases. Finally, we give universal local encodability an operational interpretation by showing that non-ULE is equivalent to whether general measurements yield an advantage over projectively simulable ones in discrimination tasks where unknown, random local unitary rotations have to be detected.
CF-UAMG: A Coarse/Fine Splitting-Based Parallel Unsmoothed Aggregation Algebraic Multigrid Method
Zhibo Fan; Shaoliang Hu; Silu Huang; Xiaowen Xu

In this paper, we propose a coarse/fine splitting-based parallel unsmoothed aggregation algebraic multigrid (AMG) method, referred to as CF-UAMG. The proposed method utilizes the strong-connection structure identified by classical AMG (C-AMG) coarse/fine splitting to guide the selection of aggregate roots and the formation of aggregates, aiming to improve the quality of the aggregation-based coarse space and thus the convergence of unsmoothed aggregation AMG (UA-AMG). We also prove uniform two-grid convergence of CF-UAMG with a convergence bound independent of the matrix size for symmetric positive definite M-matrices with nonnegative row sums. Numerical experiments on three classes of three-dimensional problems, including Poisson-type equations, radiation diffusion equations, and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, demonstrate the robustness both in convergence and parallelism of CF-UAMG. Compared with UA-AMG methods employing four commonly used aggregation algorithms, CF-UAMG achieves average speedups of 1.29x, 2.04x, and 1.94x for the three classes of problems, respectively.
On the minimum energy required to trigger a spike

We formulate and numerically study the problem of finding the minimum energy required to trigger a spike in a three-dimensional conductance-based excitable model. The variational formulation seeks a state trajectory that reaches the boundary of the spiking region with the least \textit{peak} cumulative work supplied through the membrane port. We approximate voltage histories by sums of real exponentials, reducing the problem to a finite-dimensional optimization. The best-found voltage waveform consists of a hyperpolarization phase followed by a depolarization phase, which seems to match the experimentally determined optimal stimulus in squid giant axons.
Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note

This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.
Weak stability of Ricci flow with almost WPIC1 curvature
Pak-Yeung Chan; Lucas Lavoyer; Man-Chun Lee

We prove weak $L^\infty$ stability for complete, non-collapsed Ricci flows with almost WPIC1 curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds. Small $L^\infty$ perturbations of the initial metric admit Ricci-DeTurck flows which remain uniformly close to the background flow and depend Lipschitz continuously on the initial data. This extends an earlier stability theorem of the first and third authors with Lai.
Differential properties of Drinfeld modular forms

We study the action of vector fields on the Drinfeld symmetric spaces on de Rham classes of the generic Drinfeld module. The resulting Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism, and is described by the Jacobian matrix \(J := (\frac{\partial g_{j}}{\partial ω_{i}})_{1 \leq i,j \leq r}\), where the \(g_{j}\) are the basic coefficient modular forms of rank \(r\). We show that \(J\) is the matrix inverse of the period matrix \(P\) that results from the de Rham theory of Drinfeld modules. We define the notion of Drinfeld modular differential form, which generalizes the transformation behavior of Drinfeld modular forms from functions to differential \(n\)-forms on the Drinfeld symmetric space \(Ω^{r}\). The algebra \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)} = \bigoplus_{0 \leq n < r} \mathbf{M}^{(n)}\) of all such is provided with a Serre derivation \(D \colon \mathbf{M}^{(n)} \to \mathbf{M}^{(n+1)}\) from \(n\)-forms to \((n+1)\)-forms, where \(\mathbf{M}^{(0)} = \mathbf{M}\) is the algebra of customary modular forms for \(\mathrm{GL}(r, \mathbb{F}_{q}[T])\). We determine the structure of \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)}\), which turns out to be the exterior algebra \(\bigwedge (\mathbf{M}^{(1)})\) of the \(\mathbf{M}\)-module \(\mathbf{M}^{(1)}\).
A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
Michael R. Douglas; Javier Gómez-Serrano; Fabian Lehmann; Daniel Platt; Yidi Qi

We give a rigorous, constructive proof that there exists a Ricci-flat Kähler metric on the Fermat quartic hypersurface, independently of Yau's famous theorem, along with an explicit and accurate analytic approximation to the metric. The proof combines numerical techniques to obtain the approximately Ricci flat metric, a fixed point theorem to prove existence, and verified numerics to get the bounds used by the fixed point theorem. The method is general and we discuss the computational issues in applying it to other manifolds.
Akbar Davoodi; Christoph Flamm; Daniel Merkle; Peter F. Stadler

Pairwise graph ``alignments'', usually defined as maximum common subgraphs, have been considered in many application domains, including the comparison of molecular structures. Most commonly, the problem is formulated as maximum common induced subgraph (MCIS) or maximum common edge subgraph (MCES) problems. Sometimes these formulations are restricted to connected common subgraphs. Common subgraph problems readily generalize to more than two input graphs. However, this concept is fundamentally distinct from the notion of multiple sequence alignments. Abstractly, alignments are defined as super-structures from which the individual input objects are recovered via structure-preserving projections. While the mathematical construction readily applies to common induced subgraphs, it does not fully encompass the common edge subgraph problem, which is the variant more commonly employed in cheminformatics applications. In order to consistently define multiple edge-based alignments of graphs we represent a graph $G$ as E-graph $(E,\mathscr{V})$, where $E$ is the edge set of $G$ and $\mathscr{V}$ is the set of sets of incident edges. This representation implicitly encodes the vertices in terms of edge data. Alignments of E-graphs are themselves E-graphs that contain the input (E-)graphs as subgraphs. Maximum edge subgraphs correspond to maximum induced sub-E-graphs, and they can thus be computed using a slightly modified version of the VF2 algorithm without the need to switch from graphs to line graphs. Furthermore, multiple alignments of (E-)graphs yield a natural definition of a consensus graph that is ``on average'' present in the input without having to be a subgraph of every (and in fact of any) input graph.
Braided module categories from small braidings
Tyler Franke; Ingo Runkel; Volker Schomerus

We introduce small braidings on inclusions of monoidal categories $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}$, which allow one to braid objects in $\mathcal{C}$ with objects in $\mathcal{D}$. A small braiding makes $\mathcal{C}$ a braided monoidal category, and turns $\mathcal{D}$, as well as certain subcategories of $\mathcal{D}$, into braided module categories over $\mathcal{C}$. We prove versions of previously known reconstruction results for braided module categories which do not rely on finiteness assumptions. We construct a number of new examples coming from quantum groups, as well as the associated quantum moment maps.
Counterexamples to flagged LLT and nonsymmetric Macdonald atom positivity

We give a key polynomial of degree fourteen whose expansion in Demazure $t$-atoms has a coefficient with a negative term. This computation disproves the conjectured Demazure atom positivity of flagged LLT polynomials and the corresponding stable atom positivity assertion for modified nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.
A complete solution to the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture
Su Mengwei; Sun Qiang; Xiong Ge

For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subseteq\R^n$, we prove that there exists a volume-preserving linear transformation $T\in\SL_n(\R)$, such that for every $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ there is an origin-symmetric convex body $L$ with $(1-\varepsilon)TK\subseteq L \subseteq TK$ and the isoperimetric quotient $\iq(L)\le 40\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt n$. This resolves the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture.
Covering the Square Lattice and the Honeycomb with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
Teeradej Kittipassorn; Nattawut Phetmak; Kirati Sriamorn

For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{S}_d$ be the square lattice and $\mathcal{H}_d$ the honeycomb point set with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ these sets can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors; the periodic constructions of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol cover them only from $d=1/2$ and $d=2/\sqrt{37}$ on, with gaps. At their right endpoints the bound is attained; there $\mathcal{S}_d$ is never coverable, and $\mathcal{H}_d$ is not coverable at nine of the twelve endpoints. We also give new periodic coverings, of $\mathcal{S}_d$ at $d=2/\sqrt{34}$ and of $\mathcal{H}_d$ for $2/9\le d\le1/\sqrt{19}$. Consequently, the smallest coverable spacing lies in $(0.2581,\,2/\sqrt{34}]$ for the square lattice and in $(0.1781,\,2/9]$ for the honeycomb point set, and coverability is not monotone in $d$ for either set.
Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
Emily M. Palmer; Anil V. Rao

A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.
Alexis Langlois-Rémillard; Mia N. Müßig; Helmut Podhaisky; Erika Roldan; Günter Rote; Maximilian Brömme; Matthes Norden; Maximilian Prietzel; Daniel Yu; Mykhailo Lyader

The $n$-omino fence problem asks how many cells can be surrounded by placing every $n$-omino exactly once in the grid. We present a new dynamic programming approach for this problem, allowing us to prove optimality for the pentomino and hexomino fence and to classify all possible pentomino orders by optimal area. For the first time we also provide strong heuristic solutions and upper bounds for all fences up to $n = 15$, after which we even approximate the $500$-omino fence with computational experiments. Finally, we generalize the problem to 3D, where we prove optimality for pentacubes and derive heuristic solutions for hexacubes and heptacubes.
Context Graph: Explainable Multi-Agent Decision Chains in AI-RAN
Xijun Wang; Zhaoyang Liu; Xiang Chen; Howard H. Yang; Chenyuan Feng

AI-RAN distributes network control across multiple autonomous agents, namely xApps and rApps operating over shared radio resources. When an alert or degradation appears, operators currently lack a structured way to trace which decision caused it, what context triggered that decision, and how other agents interacted. Existing explainability tools focus on single-model feature attribution or linear event logging, neither of which captures cross-agent decision chains. We propose the Context Graph, a heterogeneous directed graph that organizes policies, measurements, decisions, and alerts into a queryable explanation layer. Its foundational primitive is the Decision-Event node acting as a causal junction, where incoming edges capture triggering context and outgoing edges track downstream consequences that are progressively upgraded through counterfactual verification. Instantiated over existing E2, A1, and O1 data flows, our proof-of-concept demonstrates that compliance and diagnosis queries are resolved at sub-millisecond latency over graphs of tens of thousands of nodes, while reliably distinguishing true causal impacts from spurious correlations.
An FBSDE Approach to the Two-Dimensional Abelian-Higgs Model

We develop an iterated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) approach to the two-dimensional infinite-volume Abelian-Higgs model in Coulomb gauge. We prove tightness of the joint renormalized lattice gauge-Higgs laws, after continuum extension, as the lattice spacing tends to zero and the volume tends to infinity. We represent the lattice measure as the joint terminal law of the FBSDEs and establish uniform moment bounds for the corresponding terminal shifts. For the Higgs field, we combine a low-high frequency decomposition with covariant energy estimates to obtain bounds with sufficiently mild dependence on the gauge shift. For the gauge field, we establish high-frequency estimates for the effective force and combine them with quantitative diamagnetic control in the infrared.
Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference

When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph. We extend the characterization to nonzero means and show that freely varying correlated noise forces a fixed linear log-odds decoder to retain the full quadratic feature span even for two distinct centered regimes. At fixed quality, a three-regime example has no sufficient two-energy basis. Its smallest Bayes log-loss gap over bases of condition number at most $κ$ has sharp order $κ^{-1}$. Exact Bayes energy posteriors supply numerical gap estimates for specified bases. Additional bounds relate feature compression, independently learned mode spans and sensor-noise error to log loss. Two controlled experiments with 64 independent panels each show that signed information can improve prediction over energy summaries, while integration gives small gains over strong signed controls and depends on how the competing point rule is calibrated and how accurately observation noise is measured.
Cavity collapse and vorticity gradient blow-up in free-boundary Euler flow

We construct smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations with surface tension whose vorticity remains bounded while its full spatial gradient blows up in finite time. The solutions are axisymmetric without swirl and occupy bounded domains in which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at time $T$, while the outer free surface converges smoothly. The vorticity $ω$ can be chosen arbitrarily small in $L^\infty$, uniformly up to collapse, and satisfies $\|\nablaω(t)\|_{L^\infty}\asymp (T-t)^{-1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{1/4}$ as $t\uparrow T$. A nonconstant material trace of the relative vorticity on the shrinking surface determines direction-dependent limits of the terminal vorticity, which therefore has no continuous extension across the collapse circle. The kinetic energy measure converges to the sum of a uniform line measure on this circle and a nonzero bulk part carried by a bounded rotational field. The construction couples vorticity transport to the boundary dynamics through weighted estimates in the collapsing collar and a cancellation in the normal acceleration.
ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
Jieqiang Wei; Fahad Ali; Jonny Reichwald; Silun Zhang

LLM agents, i.e., language models run by a harness, can now write, run and debug software autonomously. This raises the question of whether they can also carry out control system design. In this paper, we consider control system design as a task for LLM agents and grade the designed controller as control engineers do: the controller is given in a single Python file mapping measurements to actions, evaluated on held-out seeds against an ordered set of requirements, under specified physical perturbations and structural certificates, without using neural networks. We formulate the task as a chance-constrained feasibility problem and instantiate it in ControlHarbor, a benchmark of 44 tasks over 13 plants, which includes network consensus, vehicle platooning, the MuJoCo hopper, walker and humanoid. The tasks are packaged in the Harbor format, so that any agent harness can be run against them, and the same environments also serve learning algorithms other than LLMs, such as reinforcement learning (RL), under the same evaluation. With ControlHarbor, we observe that the controllers designed by three frontier coding agents, Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5, reach the RL return on every parity task, but only in a minority of sessions. We also observe that the controllers certified for return alone usually fail under perturbations. When robustness is part of the specification, a structured design meets it at the RL return on the humanoid task, where domain-randomised RL does not; under large pushes, domain-randomised RL succeeds and no designed controller does. The benchmark, the controllers, and their grades are released.
Completely Regular Growth of Transcendental Entire Solutions to Linear Difference Equations with Polynomial Coefficients
Xuxu Xiang; Jianren Long; Mingjin Li

Let $f$ be a transcendental entire solution of order less than 1 of the linear difference equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{j=0}^{m}P_j(z)Δ^j f(z)=0, \qquad P_m\not\equiv0, \end{equation*} where $P_0,\ldots,P_m$ are polynomials. Applying the inverse Newton transform $\Scal$, which sends $\fall{z}{n}$ to $z^n$, we obtain a function $g=\Scal f$ satisfying a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. We then show that the completely regular growth of $g$ transfers to $f$. Consequently, $f$ is of completely regular growth and the zeros of \(f\) are regularly distributed. An example involving the \(Γ\) function is given to shows that the condition order less than $ 1$ cannot be relaxed.
Incidence Geometry with Polarity and Tiled Surfaces
Peixuan Liu; Zhiyuan Liu; Yuanqi Jiang

In 2023, Fomin and Pylyavskyy introduced the master theorem to find and prove linear incidence theorems using quadrilateral tilings of oriented surfaces. Each face of the surface corresponds to an incidence condition, which they call a coherence condition. We extend their master theorem by incorporating polarity into coherence and allowing nonorientable surfaces. Our new coherence condition can be interpreted as perpendicularity from the perspective of Cayley--Klein geometry. Moreover, a polarity incidence theorem on a nonorientable tiled surface gives rise to a self-polar linear incidence theorem on the orientation double cover. We also extend the master theorem to Hermitian polarities over division rings, with its validity depending on the topology of the surface. Finally, we determine which incidence presentations admit proofs using tilings. When such proofs exist, we express the minimum Euler genus of the corresponding tiling in terms of the fundamental group.
Exact Wasserstein Convergence Rate for Conditional Empirical Measures of Killed Diffusion Processes

Let $M$ be a $d$-dimensional compact connected Riemannian manifold $M$ with boundary $\pp M$, and let $X_t$ be the diffusion process generated by $L:=\DD+\nn V$ for some $V\in C^2(M)$ which is killed on the boundary. For any initial distribution $ν$ which is not fully supported on $\pp M$, let $μ_t^ν$ be the conditional empirical measure for the diffusion process under the condition that the process is not yet killed at time $t$, and let $μ_0$ be the associated quasi-stationary distribution. We derive the sharp convergence rate of $μ_t^ν$ to $μ_0$ in the quadratic Wasserstein distance $\W_2$ as $t\to\infty$. In particular, if $ν(B(x,r))\asymp r^k$ for some $k\in [0,d]$ and all $r\in [0,1]$ uniformly in $x\in {\rm supp}ν$, then for large $t>0$ $$ \W_2(μ_t^ν,μ_0)\asymp_ν\begin{cases} t^{-1},&d-k<6,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t},&d-k=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d-k+2}{2(d-k-2)}},&d-k>6. \end{cases} $$ Moreover, letting $\rr_\pp(x)$ be the distance of $x$ to $\pp M$, for large $t>0$ we have $$ \W_2(μ_t^{\dd_x},μ_0)\asymp \begin{cases} t^{-1},&d\le 3,\\ t^{-1}\log (1+\rr_\pp(x)^{-1}), & d=4,\\ t^{-1} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1}, & d=5,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1},&d=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d+2}{2(d-2)}}\rr_\pp(x)^{-\ff 4{d-2}},&d\ge 7. \end{cases} $$
Gamma-positivity of support enumerators of preorders

The support enumerator of a finite preorder counts lattice points of its polytope by support size. We prove Athanasiadis and Chapoton's conjecture that this polynomial is $γ$-positive. On an $n$-element preorder, the $j$th $γ$-coefficient counts points of the preorder polytope with entries in $\{0,1,2\}$, coordinate sum $n$, and exactly $j$ entries equal to $2$. Oh's correspondence for transversal matroids and Hall's theorem give a formula that records the support itself. For arbors, a separate proof gives a refinement by coordinate sum.
On the quasi-static growth of cavities in incompressible elastomers

For a variational model of incompressible elastomers exhibiting cavitation, we establish the existence of irreversible quasi-static evolutions driven by time-dependent boundary conditions. Our result extends previous work by Mora-Corral (2014) to incompressible materials under weaker regularity assumptions on the boundary datum. The proof employs the multiplicative splitting introduced by Francfort and Mielke (2006) to reduce the problem to time-independent boundary conditions and then invokes abstract results on the existence of energetic solutions to rate-independent systems. Specifically, the construction of mutual recovery sequences requires particular attention to accommodate the incompressibility constraint: to this end we employ the method by Moser (1965) to exhibit incompressible diffeomorphisms interpolating between localized translations and the identity.
The uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
Yishen Huang; Jiongyue Li; Junbin Li; Xi-Ping Zhu

We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. The method is to apply Harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of Einstein--Maxwell equations. Combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original ADM mass normalized to $M=1$. These identities imply the technical assumptions of Ionescu--Klainerman, yielding the identification with Kerr.
A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
Ronghao Cui; Jan Martin Nordbotten; Ivar Stefansson; Inga Berre

Numerical simulations of fracture propagation require accurate computation of stress intensity factors (SIFs) to determine whether a pre-existing fracture will propagate. Even though displacement solutions from well-established numerical methods generally converge with mesh refinement, the convergence behavior of SIF estimates remains less understood. In this work, we propose a scaling law to improve the performance of SIF extraction using two-point displacement correlation methods. This scaling law relates sampling distance from the fracture tip to mesh resolution. It is developed by balancing the asymptotic truncation error against the numerical discretization error. Three numerical discretization methods--standard quadratic finite elements, quadratic finite elements with quarter-point elements, and a multi-point stress approximation finite volume method--are employed to validate the proposed scaling law on fracture benchmark problems under pure-mode and mixed-mode loading. We find that the conventional nearest-tip sampling strategy fails to compute convergent SIF estimates. In contrast, the proposed scaling-based approach yields decreasing errors in the SIF estimates as the mesh is refined. Across all three discretization methods, the proposed scaling law captures the sampling locations required for convergent SIF extraction, suggesting a general numerical characteristic of near-tip SIF extraction.
Constrained intersection representations and forbidden patterns
Laurent Feuilloley; Michel Habib; Amalia Sorondo

We study the interplay between two types of graph classes: the ones defined by intersections of geometric objects and the ones defined by the absence of a substructure. More precisely, we study intersection graphs that are grounded, that is, the objects lie above a horizontal line that they touch, and ordered graphs with forbidden patterns, that is, ordered graphs that avoid a set of ordered induced subgraphs. These two approaches are fundamentally different, but it is known that several interesting graph classes have both types of characterizations, and we aim to understand whether this is a general phenomenon. Our contributions are the following. First, we identify a family of patterns on four vertices and a natural hierarchy of intersection graphs of strings whose classes are nicely interleaved. This raises hopes to prove connections between the two perspectives. Second, we dampen these hopes by proving that a class of (ordered) intersection graphs that we study cannot be characterized by a finite set of forbidden patterns. Third, we show a dual impossibility result: there exists a pattern-defined class of our hierarchy that admits no intersection representation, if we require this representation to be closed under natural operations such as translation and scaling. However, it turns out that if we allow slightly more exotic intersection representations, then we can find one for this pattern-defined class.
Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map

The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''. Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter. For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.
An upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron
A. Yu. Chirkov; S. I. Veselov; D. V. Gribanov; D. S. Malyshev; N. Yu. Zolotykh

We establish the first nontrivial upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron, resolving a long-standing open question.
