To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to extend the applicability of BSDE-based stochastic numerical methods to this class of PDEs. Specifically, inspired by the approach of learning the random variables (LRV)~\cite{BeckerJentzenMullerWurstemberger2024}, BQL incorporates learnable quadrature for Brownian increments at each time level into the backward recursion of BSDEs, enabling more efficient layerwise approximation of local conditional expectations. Furthermore, BQL introduces a continuation surrogate to facilitate the transfer of value-function information from subsequent to preceding time levels, avoiding nested quadrature while controlling the propagation of local approximation errors. Our main theoretical contribution is the derivation of a global error bound that explicitly characterizes the decomposition of the total error, together with a proof of first-order mean-square convergence under suitable approximation and integrability assumptions. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate that BQL achieves competitive solution accuracy while substantially reducing the amortized computational cost per query. For the HJB benchmark across the tested dimensions, with $Q=7$ parameter queries, BQL achieves computational cost reductions of approximately 40-fold and 4-fold compared with P$^2$INN~[2] and FBSNN~[3], respectively.
A congruence-group counterexample to Kourovka Problem 21.7

For every prime $p>24$, let $H$ be the kernel of $\SL_2(\Z/p^9\Z)\to\SL_2(\F_p)$. We prove that $H$ is not IYB, whereas $H\times C_{p^8}$ is IYB. The proof excludes a pre-Lie multiplication on the rank-three Lie ring with bracket $p[x,y]$ over $\Z/p^8\Z$ using three trace identities. It follows that the supersoluble group $H\times(C_{p^8}\rtimes C_2)$, with the involution acting by inversion, has IYB Sylow subgroups and is not IYB. Its nilpotent residual is cyclic and its Sylow $p$-subgroup has nilpotency class eight. For $p=31$, an action of order three gives a supersoluble counterexample of odd order $3\cdot31^{32}$. The same construction gives an IYB $p$-group with a specified central cyclic direct factor such that the quotient of the whole group by the unique subgroup of order $p$ in that factor is non-IYB.
On the proof of Falconer distance conjecture
Kotaro Inami; Jianbin Li; Yudong Liang; Bochen Liu; Francisco Romero Acosta

We are able to catch the main idea from OpenAI's recent release and present a proof of Falconer distance conjecture in our own words. Arguments are judiciously simplified and carefully designed for graduate-level readers.
Limit theorems for dispersing billiards with infinite cusps
Marco Lenci; Françoise Pène; Hong-Kun Zhang

Extending Lenci's work in CMP (2002), Chaos (2003), we present new insights into semi-dispersing billiards with infinite cusps. We investigate the Convergence to Stable Processes (CSP) and Functional Central Limit Theorems (FCLT) both for the collision map and for the billiard flow. Whereas the billiard map always preserves an infinite measure equivalent to Lebesgue, the billiard flow preserves the Lebesgue measure, which is either finite or infinite depending on the finiteness of the area of the billiard table. When the reference measure is infinite, the usual LLN fails, but we are able to prove the CSP and FCLT. We also prove classical FCLT for the flow when the area of the billiard table is finite. These results are obtained through a precise study of the properties of the billiard map, combined with a general approach based on induction and on coupling involving point processes.
Besicovitch-like Pseudo Almost Automorphic Stochastic Processes: Theory and Applications to Semilinear SDEs

This paper introduces, for the first time, the concept of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic stochastic processes. As a meaningful application, we investigate a class of semilinear stochastic equations driven by Brownian motion in a separable Hilbert space. By combining the Banach fixed point theorem with refined inequality techniques, we establish sufficient conditions guaranteeing the existence, uniqueness, and global exponential stability of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic solutions in distribution for the considered equations. An example is provided to show the validity of the obtained results.
The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
Yi Gao; Jinghao Huang; Ran Xu

We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. This answers questions due to several open problems in the literature.
Unified Far-field and Near-field Codebook Design for XL-array Systems
Chao Zhou; Changsheng You; Liujia Yao

While extremely large-scale antenna arrays (XL-arrays) hold immense promise for next-generation wireless networks, the paradigm shift encompassing new near-field communications renders conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based Type-I codebooks inefficient. Meanwhile, existing near-field alternatives usually impose prohibitively high storage and/or feedback burdens. To tackle these challenges, we propose in this letter a unified codebook applicable to both far-field and near-field XL-array systems. Our key idea is to express the near-field channel steering vector in an equivalent form, which is a Hadamard product of an angular vector and a curvature-related vector. This new representation allows direct reuse of the legacy Type-I codebook for angle quantization, while only a lightweight auxiliary codebook is newly added for additional curvature quantization. Subsequently, we optimize the auxiliary curvature codebook by maximizing the average beamforming gain given the information of user distribution. By leveraging the local monotonicity of the beamforming gain with respect to curvature mismatch, the optimization problem is further reduced to a quantization-error minimization problem, for which suboptimal curvature codewords are obtained. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed unified codebook achieves near-optimal beamforming performance that approaches its upper bound based on perfect channel state information (CSI), while significantly reducing the required feedback overhead as compared to various benchmark schemes.
The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in short intervals

For any real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $α$ be any irrational number. We prove that there exist infinitely many $X$ such that for $Y=X^γ/2$ with $7/12<γ\le 1$ and $0<θ<\min \{(12γ-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there is a prime $p$ satisfying $$ \|αp\|<X^{-θ},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. In particular, if $α$ has a continued fraction expansion with bounded partial quotients, then this asymptotic holds for all sufficiently large $X$. Our result extends the admissible range of short intervals in the corresponding theorem of Baier and Roy from $2/3<γ\le 1$ to $7/12<γ\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals, and also improves the exponent $θ$ for $2/3\le γ\le 3/4$. The improvement is obtained by adapting a recent result of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwiłł on exponential sums over primes.
Finite Numerical Joyce Transport and Derived Hall Scattering Groupoid

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category over a finite field $k$ satisftying certain finiteness conditions. Let $Σ$ be a connected component of the space of numerical stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}$ with one element $σ\inΣ$ satisfying the support property and the finite counting condition. We prove that each of the Joyce elements with respect to $σ_1\inΣ$ is a finite rational Lie polynomial in those of any other $σ_0\inΣ$, so the generated Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}_σ,σ\inΣ$ in the uncompleted derived Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{D})$ is constant on $Σ$. Our proof combines completions on strict sectors with a uniform mass bound for successive local substitutions. We use the method of Hall scattering diagrams on phase categories to provide a realization of the transform of Joyce elements. For the finite-length case, we also give an alternative proof using finite-length hearts instead of phase categories. As an application, we explicit the generators of the Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}$ in the Dynkin case.
Recursive memory for prediction and generation

Recurrent and state-space language models compress the past into a state of fixed size. The state must answer questions about the future now, and it must remain useful as new tokens arrive, including tokens the model samples itself. We show that the second requirement can cost far more memory than the first. For a known hidden Markov source with positive transition probabilities, a state of $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bits answers every question about the future to accuracy $\varepsilon$, however far ahead it looks, because the Bayesian filter forgets its rounding errors. Generating the future is different. When a model feeds each sampled token back into its state, the small errors in its next-token distributions add up, and $T$ tokens can require a state of order $\log(T/\varepsilon)$ bits. The lower bound comes from the KL chain rule: at every step, a model with $K$ states pays for approximating the true next-token distribution by one of only $K$ distributions. The argument applies to any source, including a language model continuing a prompt, and a small-ball estimate makes it tight for two-state sources. The extra $\log T$ disappears if the model keeps private randomness, or if error is budgeted per token, as in perplexity. Statistics of the recent past show the same gap between describing and maintaining. The number of ones among the last $n$ bits takes $\log n$ bits to write down. But if each bit is a noisy copy of the one $n$ steps earlier, tracking that count to a mean-square error $E^2$ well below its variance costs order $n/(1+E^2)+\log n$ bits. Information about each bit must be kept until the bit leaves the window, and a queue holding the counts of recent blocks keeps just enough of it.
Gaussian limits for non-cyclic and elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of the multiplicative group

We study the number of non-cyclic Sylow subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^\times$. Pollack suggested investigating whether this count has a limiting distribution after suitable normalization. For uniformly chosen $n\le x$, we prove a Gaussian limit with variance asymptotic to $\tfrac12\log_2x/\log_3x$. Motivated by the fixed-rank normal-order results of Morales, Polanco, and Pollack, we further prove joint Gaussian limits for this count and the numbers of elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of any fixed finite collection of ranks at least two. We give explicit prime-sum centers and asymptotics for all arithmetic covariances. The same joint theorem includes the number of common prime divisors of Euler's and Dedekind's functions. The proof uses the integer Kubilius model, estimates for the dependence between distinct output primes, and mean-square bounds for arithmetic truncation.
A remark on Liouville-type theorems for the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ under pointwise conditions on the head pressure
Hideo Kozono; Yutaka Terasawa; Yuta Wakasugi

We study the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the three-dimensional whole space and the Liouville-type problem under the condition of finite Dirichlet integral. We give a remark on the recent result by Chae [7, Theorem 1.2], in which an upper bound of the gradient of the head pressure and a lower bound of the head pressure with certain rates were assumed to prove triviality of solutions. In this paper, we extend the range of admissible rates by two different arguments. One relies on the pointwise decay of head pressure and the classical argument of Galdi [11]. The other is similar to the argument of Chae [4, 6] and is based on the maximum principle for the head pressure, the integral identity between the vorticity and the gradient of the head pressure on the upper level set of the head pressure, and the coarea formula. This also gives a more refined proof for [7, Theorem 1.2].
Beyond Frankl's conjecture: Maximum sum of sizes of cross-intersecting families with restricted conditions
Zhen Jia; Qing Xiang; Jimeng Xiao; Huajun Zhang

Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be two families of subsets of $[n]$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are \emph{cross-intersecting} if $F \cap G \neq \emptyset$ for all $F \in \mathcal{F}$ and $G \in \mathcal{G}$. Let $n, k_1, k_2, m, r, t$ be positive integers satisfying $n > k_1 + k_2$. Suppose that $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k_1}$ and $\mathcal{G} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k_2}$ are two cross-intersecting families such that $\left\{F \in \binom{[n]}{k_1} : |F \cap [m]| \geq r\right\} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is $t$-intersecting. In this paper, we determine the maximum sum $|\mathcal{F}| + |\mathcal{G}|$ under these assumptions. By taking $k_1=k_2+t-1$, $m = k_2+t+s-1$ and $r=k_2+t-1$ for $s\ge 0$, our result recovers a conjecture of Frankl \cite{frankl2016new}, which was recently confirmed by Wu, Feng, and Li \cite{wu2025proof}. Further, we establish a complete characterization of all extremal families. Our approach extends the Ahlswede--Khachatrian generating set method to handle the simultaneous constraints of cross-intersection and $t$-intersection, subject to additional structural conditions.
Essential $p$-dimension of simple algebras and noncrossed products of prime exponent

Let $p$ be a prime and $F$ a field of characteristic different from $p$. For integers $n\ge2$ and $1\le m\le n$, we complete the determination of the essential $p$-dimension of the class of central simple algebras of degree $p^n$ and exponent dividing $p^m$. In particular, we have $\operatorname{ed}_p(\operatorname{PGL}(p^n))=p^{2n-2}+1$, extending a result of Merkurjev for $n=2$. Using the comparison theorem of Chernousov and Merkurjev, we also determine the essential $p$-dimension of every split simple group of type $A$. To obtain the lower bounds, we apply a theorem of Ofek to block centralizers. As an application, we prove the existence of division algebras of exponent $p$ over field extensions of $F$ which remain noncrossed products after any field extension of degree prime to $p$, and answer in the negative a problem in the survey by Auel, Brussel, Garibaldi, and Vishne. The algebras can be chosen to have degree $p^n$ for every $n\ge3$ if $p$ is odd and every $n\ge4$ if $p=2$. For $p=2$ and every $n\ge3$, we also determine the essential $2$-dimensions of the classes of central simple algebras of degree $2^n$ with orthogonal involution and with symplectic involution.
The anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$
Lu Chen; Jiali Lan; Haolin Liu

We establish the anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$ under the limiting assumption. More precisely, every entire solution of the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation satisfying $u_{x_4}>0$ and $u(x,x_4)\to\pm1$ as $x_4\to\pm\infty$ for each $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$ is one-dimensional. We show that every nontrivial generalized subgraph globally minimizing the anisotropic perimeter in $\mathbb{R}^4$ is a halfspace. Combining an anisotropic tilt-excess decay estimate with a Liouville argument, we then deduce one-dimensional symmetry.
Non-existence of solutions to a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equations

We consider the Cauchy problem for a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equations introduced by M. Colin and T. Colin (2004) as a model of laser-plasma interaction. Under a coefficient condition, we prove that there are initial data admitting no solution in Sobolev spaces, both on the torus and on the Euclidean space.
Uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states for the pure-power Born-Infeld equation

For \(N\ge3\) and \(p>2N/(N-2)\), we study the Born--Infeld equation \[ -\diver\!\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\R^N . \] We prove that the positive ground state \(Q\) is unique up to translation. We also prove that the kernel of the linearized operator at \(Q\) is spanned by \(\partial_{x_1}Q,\ldots,\partial_{x_N}Q\), and determine all nonzero optimizers of the sharp Born--Infeld Sobolev inequality. To prove nondegeneracy, we first rule out nonzero radial kernel functions using the Morse index and a Wronskian identity. We then treat the angular modes by spherical harmonics. To prove uniqueness, we compare radial solutions for large \(p\), and extend the result to all \(p>2N/(N-2)\) by compactness and continuation.
Local well-posedness, wave breaking and ill-posedness for the unidirectional non-local wave model
Jian Chen; Shaojie Yang; Zhaoyang Yin

In this paper, we first establish local well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence) for the Cauchy problem associated with the unidirectional non-local wave model in the Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>1+\frac{1}{p}$ and $1\leq p,r\leq\infty$, as well as in the critical Besov spaces $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,1}$ with $1\leq p<\infty$. Next, by exploiting the fine structure of the equation and performing a delicate analysis of the commutator terms, we establish a new sufficient condition for wave breaking without using any conservation law. Finally, we prove that the model is ill-posed in $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,r}$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $1<r\leq\infty$. Our analysis further clarifies the well-posedness theory and wave-breaking behavior of the unidirectional non-local wave model arising from the motion of a cold plasma in a magnetic field, which refines and improves previously known related results.
Multivariate Bernstein duality for tournament Wright--Fisher diffusions

We give a probabilistic proof of a multivariate Bernstein duality for a multivariate Wright--Fisher frequency process with selection encoded by a finite tournament. The construction includes nontransitive interactions, such as rock--paper--scissors selection. Its dual is a pure-jump process of coefficient functions in the multinomial Bernstein basis. Selection increases the Bernstein degree through a winner--loser averaging operator, whereas neutral resampling decreases it through a duplication operator. For the proof, we construct a continuous forward process independently of duality, use duality to establish uniqueness, and obtain a weak stochastic differential equation representation and invariance of the simplex faces. This provides a sampling-based treatment of the tournament specialization of multitype Bernstein duality, extending an open problem in the binary Kingman setting of Cordero, Hummel, and Schertzer (2022).
Two Types of Cards in Kelly-Ulam Conjecture
We consider the case in Kelly-Ulam conjecture where there are only two types of cards in deck. It was possible to prove that graphs with this property are uniquely reconstructed by their card deck.
Quasisymmetric rigidity of self-similar square carpets

Let $S$ be a self-similar square carpet obtained by subdividing the unit square into $n^2$ congruent cells, deleting a nonempty collection of strictly interior open cells with pairwise disjoint closures, and repeating the same pattern with the same orientation in every retained cell. We prove that every quasisymmetric self-homeomorphism of $S$, equipped with the Euclidean metric, is a Euclidean isometry. The result holds for every integer $n\ge3$ and imposes no symmetry condition on the deletion pattern. Consequently, the quasisymmetric and isometric groups coincide with the stabilizer of the first-generation holes in the symmetry group of the square. The proof combines round uniformization and Schottky-map stabilization with a propagation argument across retained cells. This produces global homothety relations for conjugates of cell contractions and forces preservation of the outer peripheral square. Periodic points on its sides then yield preservation of the corners, reducing the conclusion to the four-corner rigidity theorem for square carpets.
Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
Shiping Cao; Haiping Jiao; Hua Qiu

We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,α}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,α}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.
Periods and CM motives of abelian type

We associate algebraic Hecke characters to certain invertible motives for absolute Hodge cycles with coefficients in a number field $K$, reversing a viewpoint of Schappacher. These motives $N$ include abelian motives and a new notion of algebraic motive. This Hecke character determines the complex and the $p$-adic periods of $N$, and is determined by the latter; this gives a proof of the Mumford-Tate conjecture for $N$. When $K$ and $N$ are abelian, we prove a refinement of the Gross-Deligne conjecture, as well as $l$-adic and $p$-adic variants. We also formulate a version of the algebraic relations between rational values of the gamma function given by Koblitz and Ogus in terms of a distribution with values in the Picard group of the category of (abelian) Chow motives.
On the equidistribution of eigenfunctions of higher dimensional cat maps modulo prime powers

The so-called $\mathit{Cat\ Map}$, which is a linear map generated by symplectic matrices $A \in \operatorname{Sp}(2d,\mathbb Z)$ modulo an integer $N\ge 1$ is a classical discrete model of quantum ergodicity. For $d=1$ it has been investigated by P. Kurlberg and Z. Rudnick (2001), J. Bourgain (2007) and A. Ostafe, I. E. Shparlinski and J. F. Voloch (2023). The significantly more difficult case of $d>1$ has been studied by P. Kurlberg, A. Ostafe, Z. Rudnick and I. E. Shparlinski (2025). All these works apply only to almost all $N$ and are unable to provide an explicit sequence of such ``good'' values of $N$. The authors (2026) have given such a construction with a polynomial decay on the corresponding matrix coefficients. Here we use some new ideas and improve this bound.

Inspired by recent work of A. Njamcul and A. Pavlović, we study topological spaces expanded by ideals of sets. We investigate the relationship between the cardinal invariants of the ideal topological space $(X, τ_\mathcal{I})$, the underlying topology $(X, τ)$, and the cardinal characteristics of the ideal $\mathcal{I}$. Furthermore, we analyze continuous maps between standard Polish spaces and their ideal expansions. We establish rigidity phenomena showing that continuous functions from $(X, τ)$ into $(X, τ_\mathcal{I})$ are severely constrained (e.g., taking at most countably many values on Polish spaces and being strictly constant on $\mathbb{R}$), whereas continuous functions from $(\mathbb{R}, τ_\mathcal{I})$ to $(\mathbb{R}, τ)$ collapse to standard continuous functions under mild conditions on the ideal.
Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher

Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial data in $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$. No restriction on the noise intensity is needed for $d=2$, while a smallness condition is required for $d\geq3$. The key new challenges arise from the thermal noise, which has a $(1+|
abla u|^2)^{1/4}$-type coefficient. This coefficient gives rise to an irregular Stratonovich-to-Itô correction term of the form $
abla u\cdot D^2u
abla u/(1+|
abla u|^2)^{3/2}$. Our main innovation is a compactness argument tailored to the structure of the correction. By combining a factorization of this term with $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$ and area estimates, we establish strong convergence of the normalized gradients and reconstruct the weighted Hessian, which allows us to define the correction at energy regularity and identify its approximation limit.
Berry phase and Hannay angle as Taylor coefficients of the minimal action

For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom whose parameters are varied slowly around a closed loop, with slowness $δ$, we study the minimal action $β_δ$ of the resulting time-periodic system and its convex conjugate, Mather's $α$-function $α_δ$, both normalized per unit time. The cycle map of such a system is an area-preserving map of the cylinder which in general is not integrable. We prove that $β_δ(ρ)$ and $α_δ(c)$ have asymptotic expansions in $δ$ to every finite order, locally uniformly in the rotational regime of the frozen systems, and we identify the coefficients geometrically. The zeroth coefficient of $α_δ$ is the average of the frozen effective Hamiltonians, as shown by Evans and Gomes. The first coefficient is the classical Berry phase: at fixed rotation number $ρ$, the first Taylor coefficient of $β_δ(ρ)$ is, modulo periods, Weinstein's Berry phase of the loop of frozen invariant curves of the class whose averaged frozen frequency is $ρ$, each curve weighted by its Mather measure. In particular, the minimal action selects the weighting in Weinstein's construction. The Hannay angle, the derivative of the Berry phase, governs the rotation numbers of all minimizing measures, including those supported on Aubry--Mather sets of the cycle map, where no invariant curve exists; and the intervals of classes on which a rotation number is locked have length $O(δ^\infty)$. Since the expansions concern exact convex functions, no adiabatic approximation is involved. A transformation rule under loops of point transformations explains why the Berry phase is defined only modulo $2πc\mathbb{Z}$. Linear oscillators, treated by the same method, recover Berry's formula for the generalized harmonic oscillator and show that the expansions are asymptotic only.
The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
Chengshuo Qiao; Zhijun Lu; Huimin Song

In 1997, Alon and Kim proposed an asymptotic edge-coloring bound motivated by a bound on the number of edges in intersecting uniform hypergraphs. The Alon--Kim conjecture asserts that, for fixed integers $k\ge t\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every $k$-uniform multihypergraph $H$ in which any two distinct edges intersect in at most $t$ vertices satisfies $χ'(H)\le(t-1+\frac{1}{t}+\varepsilon)Δ(H)$ whenever $Δ(H)$ is sufficiently large. In this paper, we prove the Alon--Kim conjecture. Our method combines finite-dimensional convex optimization with probabilistic methods.
Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems in Grounded Arithmetic

Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic in which every term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation. RGA discharges a hypothesis only when it proves the hypothesis decided. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, how Gödel's incompleteness theorems hold for RGA and for systems built on it. RGA's implication is material and RGA has the disjunction property, so the implications the textbook proof of the second theorem uses fail while its entailments and rules hold: Gödel's proof survives as entailments. RGA does not prove its consistency sentence Con, and RGA derives its own second theorem as the entailment $\mathit{Con}\vdash\neg\mathit{Pr}(\ulcorner\mathit{Con}\urcorner)$ and as one sentence quantified over proofs. The second theorem is then proved once, for every Gödel extension of RGA: an entailment relation on RGA's language, closed under RGA's rules, with a checker that meets three structural conditions, NEC, D3 and EXPL as proof transformers, D1 as closed acceptance, and consistency. D2 is not among the conditions. RGA with its checker is one instance. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA), RGA with ground induction, is another, its checker adding one rule detector, and IGA does not derive its consistency sentence for it. Adoption, a reflection rule whose premise is a derived warrant that the checker accepts computed proofs of every instance of a universal, gives consistent extensions RGA$^+$ and IGA$^+$. RGA$^+$ derives RGA's consistency sentence and IGA$^+$ derives RGA's and IGA's, so each strictly extends its base, and IGA$^+$ both. The second theorem holds at every adopted notation claim, and adopting Turing's code for that claim's checker derives its consistency sentence, so no claim certifies itself. Whether IGA alone derives RGA's consistency sentence is open, and the paper names what two routes to an answer need.
Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Battery-Assisted Grid-Import Smoothing in AI Data Centers
Xinda Zheng; Canchen Jiang; Frits de Nijs; Edward Lam; Markus Wagner

Rapid AI data-center power fluctuations challenge grid integration. Sustained grid-import smoothing requires allocating limited battery power and energy under uncertain demand. We formulate risk-aware BESS scheduling that coordinates advance reserve commitments and demand-responsive dispatch, accounting for operating costs, grid-ramp penalties, and their conditional value-at-risk. We develop battery scheduling decision-focused learning (BS-DFL) with a constraint-aware neural optimization layer trained directly from this objective without optimal-solution labels. The trained layer is then frozen to guide demand-predictor learning through scheduling costs and ramping risk, enabling solver-free rolling-horizon scheduling. In a 10,000-minute simulation using loads derived from measured AI workloads, BS-DFL reduces mean absolute minute-to-minute grid-import changes by 71.70% and total scheduling cost by 18.01% relative to an MSE-trained predictor coupled with a mixed-integer linear programming solver, with an average decision time of 18.77 ms.
Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks

Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.
Proximal gradient method for multiobjective interval valued optimization problem with application in portfolio selection

In this article, we consider a class of unconstrained multiobjective interval-valued optimization problems in which each objective function is a sum of a generalized Hukuhara(gH)-differentiable interval valued function and a proper, convex and gH-lower semicontinuous interval valued function, which is possibly non-gH-differentiable. Within this framework, we introduce the notion of a proximal gradient direction and characterize the Pareto critical points of the considered problem through a strongly convex auxiliary subproblem. Based on these characterizations, we develop a proximal gradient algorithm with an Armijo-type line search that ensures sufficient descent with respect to the interval partial order. We then establish the existence of an uniform lower bound on the admissible step length, the global convergence of the generated sequence to a Pareto critical point followed by a global rate of convergence in the general nonconvex setting. The theoretical findings of the proposed method are validated through some test problems and further illustrate its applicability on portfolio selection problems involving interval-valued data.
Unstable Entropy and Volume Growth for Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms

Let $f$ be a $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism on a compact manifold $M$ admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting $TM=E^{cs}\oplus E^{u}$ where $E^{u}$ is uniformly expanding. We establish a lower bound for the unstable topological entropy (w.r.t. $E^{u}$): $$h^{u}_{\rm top}\left(f\right)\geq\limsup_{n\to+\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log\int_{M}\left|\det \left(Df^{n}_{x}|_{E^{u}}\right)\right|\,dx.$$ Moreover, if there exists a measure of maximal unstable entropy whose Lyapunov exponents along $E^{cs}$ are all non-positive, then equality holds and the $\limsup$ is in fact a limit.
An automated approach to structure theorems for minimally repetitive rich words
Lubomíra Dvořáková; Lucas Mol; Edita Pelantová

Recent work on repetitions in rich words has led to the intensive study of the family of infinite rich words $\{{\mathbf u}_d:d\geq 2\}$, where ${\mathbf u}_d$ is the fixed point of the morphism $φ_d:Σ_d^*\rightarrow Σ_d^*$ defined by $φ_d(i)=\tt{0}(i+1)$ for $i\in\{\tt{0},\ldots,d-2\}$ and $φ_d(d-1)=\tt{0}(d-1)(d-1)$. For $d=2$ and $d=3$, it is known that the repetition threshold for infinite $d$-ary rich words is equal to the asymptotic critical exponent $E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$. Moreover, the structure of ${\mathbf u}_{2d-1}$ underlies the structure of all ``minimally repetitive'' $d$-ary rich words: there is a real number $t_d>E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$ such that every infinite $t_d$-power-free $d$-ary rich word contains the language of $π({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$ for one of finitely many morphisms $π:Σ_{2d-1}^*\rightarrow Σ_d^*$. We conjecture that a similar situation holds for all $d\geq 2$, and prove this for the first unknown case $d=4$. To do this, we develop a new approach for proving such structure theorems. Two key new concepts are ``compatibility'' of return words to palindromes in recurrent rich words, and ``$t$-persistent repetitions''. They facilitate the automation of several aspects of the proofs which were previously done laboriously by hand. We first demonstrate our approach by giving a much shorter proof of the known structure theorem for infinite $\tfrac{16}{7}$-power-free ternary rich words. Then we prove a new structure theorem: every infinite $2.12$-power-free quaternary rich word contains the language of one of seven distinct words of the form $π({\mathbf u}_7)$, up to permutation of the letters. We prove that all seven words are rich and have critical exponent $E^*({\mathbf u}_7)$, so the repetition threshold for quaternary rich words is $E^*({\mathbf u}_7)\doteq 2.1197196907$.
Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Ground States for Critical-Hardy Fractional Equations
YuJin Guo; Shuang Wu; Hongfei Zhang

We study ground states of nonlinear fractional Schrödinger equations with the critical Hardy potential in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $d\geq3$. We prove the existence and qualitative properties of ground states, based on which we analyze the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states. As a byproduct, we also investigate the optimizers of the critical Hardy--Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality, from which a sharp Keller--Hardy--Lieb--Thirring inequality is analytically derived.

Gauge-invariant representatives of massless gauge fields generally involve inverse differential operators. We trace this non-locality to the homotopy contracting the free gauge complex and replace it, at field level, by a local map using an independent scalar and a differential constraint. We discuss the BRST completion needed to preserve the physical content and the relation to the Stückelberg theory. We finally comment on the extension of this approach to non-Abelian gauge groups via the extension to interactions through $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.
Proximal point algorithm for interval valued optimization problems with application to lasso problem

In this paper, we consider a class of unconstrained interval valued optimization problems and using a suitable scalarization technique, we formulate an associated scalarized optimization problem and establish the relationships between the optimal solution of the scalarized problem and the $LU$-nondominated solution of the considered optimization problem. Based on this framework, we propose a proximal point algorithm and derive the global convergence of the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm along with the sublinear and linear rate of convergence for convex and strongly convex cases, respectively. Finally, we provide suitable numerical experiments along with comparative analysis with an existing method and applicability of the proposed algorithm on an interval valued lasso regression problem, highlighting its potential in machine learning models with uncertain data.
Tail Asymptotics for Gaps in Unitary Ensembles and the Airy Point Process

We derive tail asymptotics for the gap between the $k$th and $(k+1)$st largest particles, with $k$ fixed, in unitary ensembles and in the Airy point process. For the finite-$N$ ensembles, we consider the probabilities of a rescaled gap larger than $a_N$ and of a rescaled gap smaller than $b_N$, in the joint limits $N\to\infty$, $a_N\to\infty$ with $a_N=o(N^{2/3})$, and $N\to\infty$, $b_N\downarrow0$, respectively. For the Airy point process, the right and left tails are analyzed as the gap size tends to infinity and zero, respectively. More precisely, in both models, we obtain logarithmic right-tail asymptotics up to the constant term and cubic left-tail asymptotics with coefficient $k/6$. As an application, we also derive the limiting conditional laws of the leading particles given the existence of an abnormally large or small gap. In particular, for $k=1$, large-gap conditioning leads to a transition from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian fluctuations of the largest particle, similar to the BBP transition. Further, among any fixed number of leading gaps, we also determine the limiting probabilities of which gap attains a large maximum or a small minimum.
Convex monohedral tilings: a sharp neighbor bound and rigidity in the equality case

We study both side-to-side and non-side-to-side convex monohedral tilings of the Euclidean plane in which every tile has the same number of neighbors. Reflections are allowed, point contacts count as neighbors, and no periodicity assumption is imposed. Combining boundary estimates for sums of face curvatures, angle-incidence counts and side-length matching, we prove that the common neighbor number satisfies $N\le21$ and classify all equality cases. Equality holds precisely when the prototile is a $30^\circ$-$30^\circ$-$120^\circ$ triangle and the entire tiling is similar to the central subdivision of the standard equilateral triangular tiling. This resolves the open problem on the maximum common number of neighbors recorded in Adams's The Tiling Book.

Bollobás and Thomason conjectured that every $r$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges admits an $r$-partition such that each class meets at least $rm/(2r-1)$ edges. In this paper, we establish a lower bound of $(11-\sqrt{13})m/18$ for every $r\ge 2$. This improves Haslegrave's bound $rm/(3r-4)$ for every $r\ge 8$.
Global existence and blow-up for a fractional wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity and strong damping

This paper studies a fractional strongly damped wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity. Based on local well-posedness of weak solutions via the Galerkin approximation, we employ the potential well theory to derive the existence of global solutions under subcritical and critical initial energy conditions. Moreover, infinite time blow-up phenomena are obtained under subcritical, critical, and arbitrarily high supercritical initial energy conditions.
Uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with large maximum degree
Yuying Li; Weiyuan Zhang; Kexiang Xu

A graph $G$ is \textit{uniquely $H$-saturated} if it contains no copy of $H$ as a subgraph, but adding any edge to $G$ creates exactly one copy of $H$ in the resultant graph. In this paper, we consider the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs and characterize the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $Δ\geq n-5$. We prove that if $G$ is a uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graph with universal vertex $x$, then $G-x$ is either a star or a Moore graph of diameter 2. The uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with maximum degrees $n-3$ and $n-5$ are $\overline{C_{7}}$ and $G_{10}$ in Figure 2, respectively. But there are no uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with maximum degree $n-2$ or $n-4$.
On Lévy type subgroups of the symmetric group of $ω$ associated with simple density functions

The Lévy group, introduced by Lévy in (Lévy (1951)), is defined by \[\mathcal{L} = \left\{σ\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : σ(k)\notin n\}|}{n} = 0\right\},\] where $aut$ denotes the group of all permutations of $ω$. This group happens to be closely connected with the notion of asymptotic density as it consists of permutations that map sets with an asymptotic density back to sets with the same density. Our aim is to replicate the construction by replacing $n$ in the denominator by $g(n)$ for a function $g:ω\to [0,\infty)$ with $g(n)\to \infty$ (weight), which leads us a class of Lévy type groups. Specifically we define simple Lévy group with weight $g$ as \[\mathcal{L}_g = \left\{σ\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : σ(k)\notin n\}|}{g(n)} = 0\right\}.\] As a natural consequence we first study its relationship with the notion of simple density functions (which had been introduced in \cite{gd2} as a general class of density functions by similar manner) paving way for the class of simple density functions and ideals $\mathcal{I}_g$. We have $\mathcal{L}_g = aut$ if and only if $n/g(n)\to 0$ (just like $\mathcal{I}_g = 2^ω$ if and only if $n/g(n)\to 0$). The relation between simple density functions and simple Lévy groups is in expected line. What seems more interesting is the comparative study of these groups. We start with the relation between $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{L}_g$ and constructing suitable examples it is shown that strict inclusions and incomparability may occur. Finally we come up with an interesting observation that there are continuum many pairwise incomparable simple Lévy groups, each of which is incomparable with $\mathcal{L}$.
Classical solvability of the Cauchy problem for multi-order time-fractional systems with full matrices of differential operators

This article investigates the Cauchy problem in the whole space for a system of linear time-fractional partial differential equations with an arbitrary fixed number of components and a full matrix of constant-coefficient spatial differential operators. Each component is governed by its own Caputo derivative, and no rational relation between the fractional orders is required. We assume that the diagonal spatial symbols are homogeneous, positive and elliptic, while the off-diagonal entries have strictly lower order than the diagonal operator in the corresponding column. Using spatial Fourier and temporal Laplace transforms, we construct solution operators through convergent series of time convolutions involving scalar Mittag--Leffler kernels. These series account for all coupling paths, including repeated interactions between components. A fractional Duhamel representation incorporates nonhomogeneous source terms. We establish uniform convergence on bounded frequency regions and weighted multiplier estimates by separating low and high spatial frequencies. Under suitable Sobolev regularity assumptions on the initial data and continuously differentiable source terms, we prove existence and uniqueness of a classical solution, together with continuity and regularity properties in the appropriate Sobolev spaces. The general result includes two-component systems and is illustrated by fully coupled examples.
The Fermat--Torricelli problem under isosceles orthogonality-type conditions

The location problem studied by Weber \cite{Weber} leads to the Fermat--Torricelli problem of minimizing sums of distances. Benítez, Fernández and Soriano \cite{BFS} proved that a real normed space of dimension at least three is an inner-product space if and only if every triple of points has a Fermat--Torricelli median in its convex hull. Pakhrou \cite{Pakhrou} showed that it suffices to test equilateral triangles. We establish a characterization using triangles $\{0,x,y\}$ satisfying \[ \|x+y\|=λ\|x-y\|,\qquad \forall\,λ>2/3, \] with the parameter fixed in each characterization. The case of parameter one gives an isosceles orthogonality criterion. The proof combines radial rescaling with the transfer of planar minimality to the ambient space, without completeness or regularity assumptions on the norm.
Robustness of controllability scores for stable linear network systems

Controllability scores quantify node importance in linear network systems by optimizing the allocation of input strength. Although the volumetric controllability score (VCS) and average-energy controllability score (AECS) are uniquely defined for Hurwitz systems, their sensitivity to perturbations of the system matrix remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate the robustness of these scores to such perturbations. We first prove that both scores are locally Lipschitz continuous in the system matrix and establish a robustness bound for Hurwitz comparison matrices. We then characterize the directional derivative of the optimal allocation along a differentiable matrix path as the unique solution of a critical-cone quadratic program, whose linear term is computed using differentiated Lyapunov equations. For single-edge weakening, the norm of the resulting response vector provides a robustness-based measure of edge importance. Numerical experiments show that the response, and hence the edge importance, depends on both the criterion and the dynamics, not only on the network topology.
Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlevé II
Sibasish Banerjee; Babak Haghighat; Jie Sun

We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlevé II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlevé II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.
On Isomorphic Embeddings of Noncommutative Lorentz Spaces
Chenhao Gao; Jinghao Huang; Fedor Sukochev; Zhizheng Yu

It is shown that for $0<p_1,p_2,q_1,q_2<\infty$, the Lorentz operator ideal $C_{p_1,q_1}$ embeds isomorphically into $C_{p_2,q_2}$ if and only if (1) $p_1=q_1=2$ or (2) $p_1=p_2$ and $q_1=q_2$, which is in contrast to the classical result that $\ell_{q}$ embeds into $\ell_{p,q}$ as a (complemented) subspace. We also study the isomorphic embeddings between operator ideals generated by the weighted Lorentz sequence spaces $d(w,p)$ ($0<p<\infty$). We characterize those (commutative/noncommutative) Lorentz function spaces $L_{W}^p$ that are isomorphic to subspaces of noncommutative $L_p$-spaces for $1\leq p<2$ over some noncommutative probability spaces, which is a noncommutative version of Schütt's theorem.
Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
Vivian Zhang; Tomoki Koike; Atticus Rex; Elizabeth Qian

Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.
First-order asymptotic expansions for spectral convergence of normalized graph Laplacians constructed from samples on manifolds

Under i.i.d. uniform sampling from a closed Riemannian manifold embedded in Euclidean space, we derive first-order asymptotic expansions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetrically normalized graph Laplacians constructed via Gaussian kernels and provide concentration inequalities for the remainder terms. As a direct consequence, we establish the corresponding weak convergence results. Unlike most related works, our analysis does not impose a multiplicity-one assumption on the eigenvalues, thereby extending the applicability of the framework to general manifolds with potentially nontrivial eigenvalue multiplicities.
The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem for cycle lengths $3$ and $n$
Ugur Odabasi; Dan Roberts; Richard M. Low

The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem asks for a factorization of the complete symmetric digraph $K_v^*$ into directed $2$-factors, each of which is isomorphic to one of two given directed $2$-factors. In its uniform version, one seeks a decomposition of $K_v^*$ into $r$ factors consisting of directed $m$-cycles and $s$ factors consisting of directed $n$-cycles, where $r+s=v-1$. Let $m=3$, and let $n \geq 5$ be odd and not divisible by $3$. We show that, for every such $n$, the problem reduces to four decompositions of order at most $12n$: factorizations of $K^*_{3n}$ and $K^*_{6n}$ with every admissible number of factors of each kind, and two factorizations of the complete symmetric equipartite digraph with four parts of size $3n$. We construct these decompositions for $n=7$, and thereby give a complete solution for $(m,n)=(3,7)$: the obvious necessary conditions are also sufficient, with the single exception of $(v,r,s)=(6,5,0)$.

Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, $t(G)$ triangles, and adjacency spectral radius $λ(G)>\sqrt m$. Li, Feng and Peng (2025) conjectured that $t(G)\ge\sqrt m-O(1)$ if no vertex belongs to every triangle of $G$. We prove the stronger bound $t(G)\geλ(G)-C$ for an absolute constant $C$, and give an explicit choice of $C$. The proof bounds the sum of the squared adjacency eigenvalues other than the largest and smallest. Interlacing and matrix perturbation estimates then restrict the neighbourhood of a vertex corresponding to a largest entry of a Perron vector to two disjoint edges and isolated vertices. A weighted count of the triangles completes the proof.
A Threshold-Crossing Condition for the Least Colossally Abundant Counterexample to Robin's Inequality

We study the constraints that a hypothetical least Colossally Abundant (CA) counterexample to Robin's Inequality would place on the non-trivial zeros of $ζ(s)$. In the single-prime case we express the least CA counterexample $N$ as $M\cdot p$, where $M$ is its CA predecessor and $p$ is prime. Using the von Mangoldt explicit formula for $ψ(x)$, we express $\ln p$ in terms of a sum over the non-trivial zeros of $ζ(s)$ and split that expression into its baseline contribution $\mathcal{R}_0(p)$ and its off-line distortion. When both converge, we show that the off-line distortion is negative whenever $1+1/(e^{\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+e^{2\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+\cdots+e^{(v+1)\mathcal{R}_0(p)})\le\ln(\ln M+\mathcal{R}_0(p))/\ln\ln M$, where $v$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $M$. In the case where the least CA counterexample is the product of its CA predecessor and two primes (the semiprime case), the logarithm of the product of the two primes is the sum of two von Mangoldt expansions. An analogous inequality implies that at least one of the off-line distortions of the two expansions is negative.
Existence and uniqueness of asymptotic traveling waves in a time-fractional bistable reaction-diffusion equation

We study asymptotic traveling waves for a reaction-diffusion equation with a Caputo time derivative. For general $C^1$ bistable imbalanced nonlinearities, we prove the existence of an asymptotic traveling wave connecting the two stable states. The asymptotic wave speed is unique, and the asymptotic profile is strictly increasing and unique up to translation. The proof uses continuation from a stationary front and the sliding method. For a cubic nonlinearity, we also derive an asymptotic formula for the speed near the balanced case, with an explicit leading coefficient. Finally, we perform numerical simulations to compare the speed predicted by the asymptotic formula with the front propagation speed in the original equation.
A counterexample to the Erdős--Mahler conjecture

We disprove a 1939 conjecture of Erdős and Mahler by constructing, for every real $τ\ge4$, a Cantor set of numbers of irrationality exponent $τ$, each having infinitely many regular continued-fraction convergents of the form $2^a/3^b$.
Relative Derived Torsion in Categories of Reduced Modules: Comparison and Non-Noetherian Examples

Let $I$ be an ideal of a commutative ring $R$. We use relative derived torsion in exact full abelian subcategories of $I$-reduced modules to study ambient derived ideal-power torsion. Exact inclusion forces $IM=I^2M$ whenever $I^2$ is finitely generated. Over a Noetherian ring, every finite object consequently decomposes into its torsion part and $IM$, and its positive-degree ambient cohomology vanishes. For $R=S[t]$ and $I=JS[t]+(t)$ with $J^2=J$, we compute every stage of the canonical Ext system and its transition maps, obtaining a comparison with $\Ext_S^q(S/J,-)$. Valuation-domain and product-of-fields examples yield nonzero cyclic first cohomology. A further construction has cyclic coefficients and cyclic ambient cohomology in every positive even degree, while its positive-degree relative cohomology vanishes. Applications determine kernels of canonical Ext maps for these coefficient modules and identify the obstruction to ring-valued specialization in the questions of Eisenbud, Mustaţă, and Stillman.
Regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level

For split groups, we prove that centralizers act transitively on regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level. As an application, we prove Chi's conjecture on the number of top-dimensional irreducible components of affine Lusztig varieties.
Weak $L^{2/3}$ bounds for the bilinear Hilbert transform

For Schwartz functions $f_1,f_2$ on $\mathbb{R}$, define the bilinear Hilbert transform by $$ \mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)(x) =\operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-t)f_2(x+t)\,\frac{dt}{t}. $$ We prove the weak-type estimate $$ \left\|\mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)\right\|_{L^{2/3,\infty}} \lesssim_{p_1,p_2} \|f_1\|_{p_1}\|f_2\|_{p_2} $$ for $1<p_1,p_2<2$ with $1/p_1+1/p_2=3/2$. The key ingredient is a new local supremum estimate for packet sums, which we use to establish the forest estimate.
Nonnegative weak tilings and the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T2)
Gergely Kiss; Caleb Marshall; Máté Matolcsi; Gábor Somlai

We develop a general method, in finite cyclic groups, for constructing nonnegative rational functions $f$, normalized by $f(0)=1$, that satisfy the Coven-Meyerowitz condition $(T1)$ but fail $(T2)$, such that $f$ is a weak complement for a set tile $A$. Motivated by the unsupported-divisor questions in arXiv:2507.11672, we show that if a set tile $A$ admits an unsupported divisor, then a suitable dilation of $A$ admits such a rational weak complement $f$. Using this method, we construct an explicit example in the group $\mathbb{Z}_{180}$. The weak complements in our explicit perturbative constructions are not positive definite because of restrictions on the Fourier support of the perturbations. Thus these constructions do not resolve the proposed extension of the Coven-Meyerowitz conditions to positive-definite weak tilings (arXiv:2411.03854, Problem 1.2).
Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
Md Babul Hossain; Mohammad Shah Alam

Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $α\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Grünwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $α=1$. Our main theoretical result shows that for $α<1$ the influence of the unknown initial infectious count vanishes, but no faster than $t^{-α}$; after 332 daily steps it is about $4.4\times10^{8}$ times larger at $α=0.9$ than at $α=1$. In out-of-sample forecasting over 27 weekly origins, the effect of memory depends on the setting. In Bangladesh the integer order gives the lowest error for linear and constant-rate forecasts in 47 of 48 settings. In the United States, where reported cases reached about 18% of the population, a fractional order lowers the linear forecaster's error in all 12 comparisons in 2021 but raises the constant-rate forecaster's, with no difference significant after Holm adjustment. Against standard baselines, the SIR-based linear forecaster was more accurate than the classical SIR model and a neural network without SIR structure, and competitive with ARIMA: in the United States the fractional linear forecaster had the lowest error of all methods (seven-day MAPE 7.54% against 9.14% for ARIMA), whereas in Bangladesh ARIMA had the lowest MAPE, with no significant difference from ARIMA in either country. The choice of a fractional order should rest on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit.
Two nodally bound-preserving and mass-conservative discontinuous Galerkin methods for reaction-diffusion problems

We propose and analyze two high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods that preserve prescribed nodal bounds and total mass for reaction-diffusion problems with anisotropic and heterogeneous diffusion. Both methods combine a weighted interior-penalty prediction step with a convex correction in either the dG energy or the $L^2$ metric. We construct a pointwise bound-preserving and cellwise mass-preserving comparison function with optimal local approximation properties. This construction yields optimal dG-energy error estimates for the energy correction and, under a dual regularity assumption, optimal $L^2$ and dG-energy error estimates for the $L^2$ correction on quasi-uniform meshes. We further establish a general a posteriori estimate that combines a predictor estimator with the computable correction norm. The resulting estimators are globally reliable and efficient up to data oscillation, with parameter-dependent efficiency constants. Numerical experiments compare the two corrections and illustrate their use in adaptive computations.
Maximal Triply Even Binary Codes from Elliptic Orthogonal Graphs

For a finite set $X$, a binary linear code $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^X$ is called a triply even binary code if $\operatorname{wt}(c)\equiv 0\pmod{8}$ for every $c\in C$. Let $q$ be an odd prime power and $n$ be an integer with $n\ge 2$. Let $E^-_{2n+2}(q)$ denote the binary code spanned by all pairwise sums of rows of the adjacency matrix of the elliptic orthogonal graph arising from a $(2n+2)$-dimensional elliptic quadratic space over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that $E^-_{2n+2}(q)$ is a triply even binary code if and only if $n=2$ and $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. In this case, we also prove that $E^-_6(q)$ is a maximal triply even binary code.
Swati Gupta; Mehrdad Sohrabi; Levent Tunçel

We give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour of length at most $\frac{89}{64}=\frac{7}{5}-\frac{3}{320}$ times the value of the subtour relaxation. This improves the long-standing ratio $\frac75$ of Sebő and Vygen and shows that the integrality gap of the subtour LP on graphic instances is at most $\frac{89}{64}\approx 1.3906$. We optimize a non-linear objective function over an odd-join polytope, which uses (i) a new removable system of edges, and (ii) reconnection of subtours if the graph is disconnected. This approach gives a $\frac{13}{10}$-approximation algorithm for $4$-regular $4$-vertex-connected graphs, improving the $\frac43$ of Newman, and a $\frac43$-approximation for $k$-vertex-connected graphs of maximum degree at most $k+1$, for every $k\ge 3$. For the general graphic TSP, we construct a feasible point in the odd-join polytope, using an optimal vertex from the Subtour linear programming relaxation of TSP, which helps us bound the approximation factor by 89/64.

Momentum methods with the same slow dynamics can have different worst-case rates on smooth strongly convex functions. We identify a half-step phase barrier in the gradient query that governs this difference. For momentum with extrapolation $τ_κ\toτ$, $β=1-θ/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$ and $hL\to y$, where $κ=L/μ$ and $θ,y>0$, the exact uniform distance factor is $1-c/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$, with $c=\min\{θ/3,c_Q(θ,y)\}$, when $τ>1/2$ and $y(1+2τ)<4$; $c_Q$ is the slowest quadratic decay exponent. Quadratically accelerated families with $\limsupτ_κ<1/2$ have divergent trajectories on the full function class. Upper bounds use finite-lag certificates: nonnegative combinations of inequalities for values and gradients at finitely separated query points, together with comparisons to the minimizer. For any prescribed accuracy, spiral mixtures or quadratic trajectories of one finite-dimensional objective give matching lower bounds at all iteration horizons. We resolve the parameter layer near $τ=1/2$ and classify all tunings of this family attaining the optimal leading constant 1. The flow also bounds the leading constant of every second-order stationary linear family with the same slow parameters $(θ,y)$ and fixed finite memory.
On Distinct Powers in Finite Groups

Sun conjectured that if a group $G$ has no elements of orders $2,3,...,n+1$, then every $n$-element subset $A$ can be ordered as $a_1,...,a_n$ so that $a_1,a_2^2,...,a_n^n$ are pairwise distinct. We prove the conjecture for finite groups when $n=4,5,6$. The proofs combine collision-counting arguments with reductions to finite-field assignment problems; the remaining finite cases for $n=6$ are verified exhaustively. We also prove the conjecture for every $n$ when no four elements of $A$ generate the same cyclic subgroup.
The minimum number of cycles of length $0$ modulo $k$ in graphs with no proper $k$-coloring

Consider an integer $k\geq 3$. Toft and Tuza observed that every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has a cycle of length $0$ modulo $k$. Brewster, McGuinness, Moore, and Noel conjectured the following quantitative strengthening: every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has at least $\frac{(k+1)!}{2k}$ cycles whose lengths are divisible by $k$. The conjecture is sharp, as demonstrated by the complete graph on $k+1$ vertices. Kim and Picollelli confirmed the conjecture for $k=3$. We establish the conjecture for every $k\geq 3$. In other words, we determine the minimum number of cycles of length $0$ modulo $k$ in a graph with no proper $k$-coloring.
Third-Order Asymptotics for Fixed-Length Lossy Compression of Discrete Memoryless Sources

This paper determines the third-order asymptotics of the logarithm of the minimum codebook size for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete memoryless sources. For an excess-distortion probability constraint $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and every interior distortion level, we establish a third-order correction of $\frac12\log n+O(1)$, where $n$ is the blocklength. This sharpens the general bounds of Kostina and Verdú [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 2012]. The main technical innovation lies in the converse for positive dispersion. Under a reverse change of measure, we retain the exponential weights associated with tilted information and distortion slack and control them jointly using the multivariate weighted-strip estimate of Scarlett, Martinez, and Guillén i Fàbregas [Proc. IEEE ISIT, 2015]. A pairing argument verifies the required covariance nondegeneracy uniformly over all reconstruction words whose distortion balls meet a typical set, yielding the matching converse.
Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence

Evaluating a learned AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) surrogate on one grid serialization cannot show whether its accuracy depends on that encoding. We test this dependence with thirteen metamorphic relations, each specifying when a transformation is valid and how to compare its outputs. Our audit covers 17 model and pipeline configurations: two released trained checkpoints and 15 random-weight architecture or mechanism controls. Every configuration violates at least six relations, even at reporting tolerances ten times tighter or looser. For GridSFM-Open v1.1, source inspection and intermediate-tensor interventions point to an indexing bug and three noncanonical or numerically unstable preprocessing choices; a repaired checkpoint remains untested. In a separate case500 training experiment, augmentation lowers transformed-view error in three of four models and median discrepancy and constraint-violation P95 in all four. These benefits depend on the training protocol: some relations worsen, and every evaluated prediction remains AC infeasible. A GPU/CPU eigensolver mismatch accounts for most of the large raw-Laplacian-baseline gain. We recommend reporting representation consistency alongside accuracy, feasibility, and cost. These results establish neither deployment readiness nor universal invariance.
Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Benders Decomposition for Security-constrained Transmission Expansion Planning
Jeffrey Christiansen; Andreas T. Ernst; Terrence Mak

Energy grids worldwide rely on efficient, effective and resilient transmission networks to deliver power from generators to geographically distant destinations. The optimisation problem of designing these networks is made very difficult by the non-linearity and non-convexity of the equations which govern AC power flow. In this paper we propose the Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Benders Decomposition (AMFBD) algorithm, which is capable of solving to global optimality the Security-Constrained Transmission Expansion Planning problems with N-1 redundancy, using the non-convex AC power flow equations. We demonstrate the practical capability of this algorithm by solving security-constrained expansion problems based on the Garver 6-bus problem and the 14-bus IEEE test case. Given the large costs generally associated with energy grids, globally optimal investment decisions that can be found using AMFBD have the potential to provide significant practical benefits over suboptimal solutions produced by approximations or heuristics.
A Variable-metric Inexact Progressive Hedging Algorithm with a Lagged Stopping Criterion for Multistage Stochastic Variational Inequalities
Min Zhang; Lei Yang; Jie Sun

The progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) solves multistage stochastic variational inequalities (SVIs) by independently solving regularized scenario subproblems and enforcing nonanticipativity through primal-dual updates. Since these subproblems are often solved iteratively, practical implementations need stopping criteria that control errors while preserving convergence. We propose iVMPHA-Lag, a variable-metric inexact PHA with a lagged stopping criterion for monotone SVIs. The method allows scenario block metrics to vary across outer iterations while remaining compatible with nonanticipativity. For each scenario, an error budget combines a positive fraction of the previous budget with a progress measure from the preceding outer iteration. This gives a stopping tolerance fixed before the inner iterations begin, so each scenario can check its criterion independently without a prescribed summable tolerance sequence. With positive initial budgets and a positive inexactness parameter, we prove finite inner termination provided the inner solver produces valid approximations whose residual and enlargement errors tend to zero. Under suitable conditions, we establish global convergence of the primal-dual iterates and local $R$-linear convergence under metric subregularity at the limit point. Numerical experiments on synthetic strongly monotone box-constrained SVIs show that iVMPHA-Lag with adaptive metrics uses fewer scenario evaluations and less time on average than exact PHA and the competing inexact methods among the tested configurations in all four baseline regimes. Its average time advantage over the competing inexact methods persists across the tested problem sizes. Further comparisons show that metric adaptation improves efficiency over the fixed scalar configuration, while lagged stopping and positive budget retention reduce inner computational work.
Statistical Analysis of the Structure from Noise Phenomenon in Generalized Procrustes Problems

In cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), observations are highly noisy, and scientists often use reference templates to guide matching, alignment, and averaging to reconstruct the molecular structure. However, these procedures can produce an output resembling the template even when the observations contain only noise, a phenomenon known as Einstein from noise (EfN). This phenomenon has attracted attention in statistics, where simplified observation models involving group actions have been studied to understand the resulting model bias. Characterizing the bias in the full cryo-EM pipeline remains challenging. We study template matching and averaging in the generalized orthogonal Procrustes problem, which provides an analytically tractable setting involving continuous orthogonal group action and lower-dimensional projections of ordered point clouds. We show that, for pure Gaussian noise, the mean of the aligned-and-averaged estimator admits the same left and right singular-vector bases as the template but its singular values may be distorted. This identifies the subspace structure imposed by the template even in the absence of signal. We characterize the singular values and bound their distortion, establish finite-sample operator-norm bounds, and give sufficient sample sizes for the population mean to dominate random fluctuations. In fact, this bias still exists under weak signals: when the template rank is at least the observation dimension, the change from the pure-noise mean is $O(η^2)$ in signal amplitude $η$. Our results provide an explicit characterization of model bias in a registration problem motivated by cryo-EM and show why averaging more observations can stabilize structure imposed by the template without removing the bias.
Covering the Triangular Lattice with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
Teeradej Kittipassorn; Nattawut Phetmak; Kirati Sriamorn

For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{T}_d$ be the triangular lattice with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ the set $\mathcal{T}_d$ can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors, a question left open by Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol for $2-\sqrt3\le d<2/\sqrt{37}$ and on several gaps between their constructions. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points of $\mathcal{T}_d$ in a closed unit disk, we show that $\mathcal{T}_d$ cannot be covered whenever $\mathcal{N}(d)<4/d^2$, and we determine this set of spacings exactly as a union of fifteen intervals; combined with their constructions, this shows that coverability is not monotone in $d$. At the right endpoints $d=2/\sqrt k$ of these intervals the density bound is attained, and we show that such a spacing is coverable if and only if $k$ is the norm of an Eisenstein integer. We also give two new coverings, at $d=1/\sqrt{13}$ and $d=2/\sqrt{21}$, in which the disks form a hexagonal packing. Consequently, together with an earlier result of Okayama, Kiyomi and Uehara, the smallest coverable spacing $d_{\min}$ exists and satisfies $2/\sqrt{55}<d_{\min}\le1/\sqrt{13}$, which answers a question of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol.

We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.
Gradient regularity without gap conditions for parabolic double phase systems with coefficients depending only on time

We study degenerate parabolic double phase systems with growth exponents $p<q$ whose modulating coefficient depends only on time. In this case, the operator on each time slice has Orlicz growth with structural constants independent of the coefficient, and the system is invariant under spatial translations. Using these features, we prove second order estimates and local bounds for the gradient when the coefficient is merely bounded and measurable, and $C^{1,α}$ regularity when it is Hölder continuous in time. For weak solutions with gradients in $L^q$, these results hold without any gap condition between $p$ and $q$.
Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models
Ian Christopher Tanoh; Scott W. Linderman

Nonlinear state space models are typically evaluated sequentially, limiting their ability to exploit modern parallel hardware. Recent work has shown that state space models can be evaluated in parallel by reformulating evaluation as a root-finding problem, which can be solved with a parallel form of Newton's method. However, exact Newton methods require expensive multiplication of dense Jacobian matrices, and quasi-Newton methods based on diagonal approximations, while more scalable, are often slow to converge because they neglect interactions across state dimensions. We introduce a novel quasi-Newton approach based on Broyden's method, which captures coupling terms with diagonal-plus-low-rank approximations to blocks of the Jacobian. We construct the approximations from trajectory secants, avoiding automatic differentiation while retaining the favorable scaling of diagonal approximations and remaining compatible with parallel scan through rank compression. We prove finite-step recovery of the exact trajectory under the compressed scan, and show that convergence is tracked by the compression error and by the block approximation error along the current trajectory error, rather than in spectral norm. Empirically, we show that our method is advantageous when interactions are approximately low rank or when Jacobian evaluation is expensive: on low-rank RNNs, parallel MCMC algorithms, and denoising diffusion models, it converges in fewer iterations than other quasi-Newton methods and is the fastest parallel method when Jacobian evaluation is expensive or state dimensions are large.
A Fast Proximal-Gradient Algorithm for Decentralised Optimisation
Ye Pu; Matthew K Tam; Liam Timms

We consider a connected multi-agent network where agents coordinate to minimise a finite sum of convex functions. Each function in the sum can be further expressed as the sum of a smooth and nonsmooth component and is known only to a single agent in the network. We propose a decentralised proximal-gradient-type algorithm for solving this problem, which we term Fast PG-EXTRA. In each iteration, agents evaluate the gradient of the smooth component of their local objective functions and the proximal operator of the nonsmooth component, followed by communicating the results with neighbouring agents in the network. Fast PG-EXTRA can be viewed as an accelerated variant of PG-EXTRA, in the sense that it enjoys non-ergodic $o(1/k^2)$ convergence rates in terms of the first-order optimality residual, successive iterates, and consensus error, compared to PG-EXTRA's ergodic $O(1/k)$ convergence rates. Our analysis of Fast PG-EXTRA is based on an accelerated variant of the Condat--Vũ algorithm for non-distributed convex minimisation, which has similarly improved convergence rates compared to the Condat--Vũ algorithm. We validate our convergence results for Fast PG-EXTRA and demonstrate its potential advantages compared to PG-EXTRA with numerical experiments for power state system estimation and $l_1$-regularised logistic regression.
Multiscale LegONet: Learning Coefficient-Dependent Local Spaces for Composable Multiscale Finite Elements with Localized Error Bounds
Yueqi Wang; Cindy Xiangrui Kong; Guang Lin

We introduce multiscale LegONet (Ms-LegONet), a plug-and-play learned block for heterogeneous elliptic problems. One network per spatial dimension is trained once on local coefficient patches and reused, without retraining, across coefficient layouts, sources, boundary data and domain sizes within the trained coefficient class. On a fixed primitive patch the network maps the local coefficient to a zero-boundary space, the only learned object. The multiscale basis functions are the harmonic extensions of a fixed set of boundary traces, each a Galerkin solve in that space.
