We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.
Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
Bienvenido Barraza Martínez; Robert Denk; Jairo Hernández Monzón; Max Nendel

We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.

Heffter arrays are combinatorial structures that can be used to construct orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions of complete graphs. A square Heffter array $H(n;k)$ is a partially filled $n \times n$ array with $k$ filled cells in each row and column. Its entries are distinct and nonzero, form a half-set of the group $\mathbb{Z}_{2nk+1}$, and sum to zero in every row and column. If the natural orderings of the rows and columns of an array are simple, the array is called globally simple. The globally simple property guarantees the orthogonal cycle decompositions constructed from the Heffter array consist of simple cycles. While existence results are known for most congruence classes of the parameters $n$ and $k$ modulo 4 for square globally simple Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$, the existence for $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ has remained largely open. In this paper, we present a construction for globally simple integer Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$ covering all admissible values of $n$ when $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$. This settles the existence question across all congruence classes.
A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
Mykola Pratsiovytyi; Yaroslav Vynnyshyn; Oleh Vynnyshyn

The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained. An example of applying the criterion to a series whose Cantorval property was previously unknown is given. A more general object of study of topological properties is the set of numbers whose representations in a numerical system with a natural base and a redundant alphabet are subject to restrictions on the use of digits. It is for this object that the above statements are proved.
Branch points and natural boundaries of Poincaré functions and of solutions of nonlinear functional differential equations

In this paper, we study the singularity structure of the analytic continuation of solutions to the equation $g(λw)=R(g(w))$, where $|λ|<1$ and $R$ is a rational function. We show that the analytic solution \(g\) near zero is branched, and that its analytic continuation yields an infinite-sheeted Riemann surface with various patterns of branch points. In one specific pattern, some branch points are delayed: they appear only when the analytic continuation reaches a particular Riemann sheet. Using this functional-equation framework, we extend the study to first-order nonlinear functional differential equations. We show that the continuation of certain special solutions near an attracting fixed point yields either single-valued or multivalued functions, with the unit circle as a natural boundary on every sheet.
On operators with many spectral components

For a complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ with unit and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\sup\{n;\;\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing\}$ be the spectral depth of $\mathscr A$. We characterize nonemptiness of $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ in terms of orthogonal idempotents, compute $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ for finite-dimensional algebras, and show that every class $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ is open. For operators on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ these classes are dense in $\mathscr B(X)$, which implies that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr B(X))$ is a dense $G_δ$-subset of $\mathscr B(X)$. By contrast, we exhibit a commutative Banach algebra whose spectral classes are all nonempty and none of which is dense. For self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, we obtain sharper perturbation results, with positive semi-definite perturbations of prescribed rank producing spectra with exactly $n$ components. We show that a quasinilpotent weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $X$ admits a nilpotent rank-one operator $F$ such that the spectrum of $S_w+αF$ has infinitely many components for every nonzero $α$.
Geodesic connectedness of globally hyperbolic spacetimes with a causal Killing vector field

We characterize the existence of a geodesic joining two prescribed points of a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ admitting a complete causal Killing vector field $K$ and a complete smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $S$. We prove that two points $p,q\in M$ are joined by a geodesic if and only if there exists an $H^1$ curve $γ$ from $p$ to $q$ such that $g(\dotγ,K)$ is constant almost everywhere. The statement is intrinsic and allows $K$ to be timelike at some points and lightlike at others. A global splitting induced by the flow of $K$ is used in the proof, but no global bounds on the metric coefficients are imposed. The proof relies on stationary perturbations of $(M,g)$, whose relevant compactness properties follow from global hyperbolicity of $g$, and on uniform estimates based on an integral admissibility condition and a Glaeser-type inequality. Two examples illustrate geodesic connectedness and the obstruction detected by the characterization.
Minimum cumulative power divergence estimation with applications to copulas

Parametric inference based on distribution functions is useful when a model is naturally specified through its cumulative distribution function or when a tractable density is unavailable. We study minimum cumulative power divergence estimation, obtained by comparing a parametric distribution function with its empirical counterpart. For a fixed positive tuning parameter and a fixed finite integration measure, we establish the existence of a consistent sequence of local solutions to the estimating equations and derive its asymptotic normality. The resulting covariance has a sandwich form whose components involve derivatives of the distribution function and the covariance kernel of the multivariate empirical process. We specialize the construction to copulas using Lebesgue measure on the unit cube, and distinguish estimation with known margins from estimation based on ranks. In the latter case, the covariance incorporates the effect of estimating the marginal distributions. The relationship with the copula divergences of Eguchi and Kato is made explicit: the power loss is closely related, whereas the integration measure determines a different estimation criterion. A simulation design for Gumbel, Clayton, and Frank copulas examines the estimation of Kendall's tau under correct specification, family misspecification, and contamination by independence. The simulations show competitive clean-data accuracy but no general robustness advantage over the empirical-copula-weighted alternatives under independence contamination.
Pascal Fong; Matilde Maccan; Ludvig Modin

We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbolα_p$, respectively. As a special case of $G = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, we recover Igusa's classical example. Finally, we compute all infinitesimal group schemes which appear as $\operatorname{Pic}^0_S/(\operatorname{Pic}^0_S)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for all (quasi)-bielliptic surfaces $S$. This completes the description of the singular Picard schemes of smooth projective surfaces of Kodaira dimension zero.
Hilton's Conjecture on Uncomplemented Incomparable Families
Yuejian Peng; Zilong Yan; Cheng Zhao

A family ${\mathcal A}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is \emph{uncomplemented} if it contains no set together with its complement. Families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t$ are \emph{strongly incomparable} if every set in one family is incomparable with every set in another family. In 1976, Hilton conjectured that if ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ are uncomplemented and strongly incomparable, then $$\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|\le 2^{n-1}.$$ We confirm this conjecture by a matrix rank argument that encodes incomparability and uncomplementedness in the same matrix, which is quite different from the earlier methods on this problem. We also study weak incomparability, in which the same set may occur in different families. Goldwasser, Hilton and Zheng conjectured an upper bound in this setting and claimed that their conjecture is equivalent to Hilton's conjecture. We give counterexamples to their conjecture for every $t\ge3$ and identify the error in the claimed equivalence. We then propose a replacement conjecture and confirm it when $t$ is large. The upper bound $2^{n-1}$ in Hilton's conjecture can be attained if some families are allowed to by empty. It is natural to consider the maximum size of $\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|$ for uncomplemented and strongly incomparable families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ when all families are required to be non-empty. Denote this maximum number by $M(n,t)$. We show that \[ 2^{n-1}-1\le M(n,t)\le 2^{n-1} \] for $n\ge3$ and $3\le t\le n$.
Negative normal degree and holomorphic sectional curvature pinching

We obtain an upper bound for the local holomorphic sectional curvature pinching of a Kähler manifold containing a smooth rational curve of negative total normal degree. As an application, we prove that a compact Kähler surface with positive holomorphic sectional curvature and local pinching constant at least $1/9$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$, $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$, or the first Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_1$. For pinching strictly greater than $1/9$, only the first two possibilities occur, confirming a conjecture of Yang and Zheng. We also determine the optimal local pinching constants on $\mathbb F_1$ and $\mathbb F_2$.
Amortized Transport-Map Likelihoods for Hierarchical Inverse Problems with Application to Wetting

Hierarchical Bayesian models pool measurements, but with the forward model in the likelihood every posterior evaluation costs one forward solve per cell. To reduce this cost, we introduce a simulation-based inference framework in which a triangular transport-map likelihood, trained once per design, serves every cell. We apply it to infer wetting properties from photographs of a stable hole in a thin liquid film. The hole's radius depends, through the nonlinear Young-Laplace equation, on the contact angle and capillary length. One photograph gives rank-one information about them, so we pool many in a hierarchical model whose cells, each a substrate at one volume setting, share the apparatus geometry and the noise scale. A design fixes the number of substrates, the volume settings and the photographs per cell. The map's posteriors agree with direct sampling of the forward model in the wetting properties at a synthetic validation design, and less closely at a larger synthetic scaling design. At the validation design, simulation-based calibration detects no departure for any parameter. There, the map needs several hundred times fewer forward-model evaluations than direct sampling with a gradient-free ensemble sampler for a single posterior, and about five orders of magnitude fewer over a calibration study of 200 posteriors. On real photographs its posterior agrees with direct sampling and is consistent with the measured radii. Trained offline, the amortized map turns new photographs into a posterior with no forward solve. It is thus a major step toward measuring wetting properties in situ without disturbing the liquid.
The multiplicity bound for near-group fusion categories of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$. We show $k\in\{0,3,4\}$, which then gives a complete characterization of near-group fusion categories determined by $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$.
Involution-Preserving schemes through constrained mesh motion: a novel Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian framework
Sacha Cardonna; Elena Bernardelli; Walter Boscheri

We introduce a novel structure-preserving finite volume method that exploits mesh motion to enforce differential involutions arising in hyperbolic systems of conservation laws. The key idea is to leverage the geometric degrees of freedom of an Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) framework to construct a constrained mesh motion that is intrinsically compatible with the involution constraints embedded in the governing equations. The method is developed within a cell-centered formulation on moving quadrilateral meshes, where discrete divergence and curl operators are constructed from vertex-based differential operators. Particular care is devoted to the consistent evolution of the mesh geometry and the satisfaction of the Geometric Conservation Law (GCL). The proposed framework is applied to two representative hyperbolic systems featuring distinct involution constraints: the ideal magnetohydrodynamics equations, endowed with the divergence-free condition on the magnetic field, and the hyperbolic Euler-Heat equations, subject to a curl-free constraint on the thermal impulse. Second-order accuracy in time is achieved through a Runge-Kutta discretization, with the geometric constraints consistently enforced at each stage. A comprehensive set of classical benchmark problems is presented to assess the accuracy and effectiveness of the method. The numerical results demonstrate that appropriately constrained mesh motion provides an effective mechanism for preserving differential involutions, establishing a novel connection between mesh geometry and the structure-preserving discretization of hyperbolic systems.
On Relative Smoothness in Dually Flat Geometry

We study the geometric meaning of relative smoothness on dually flat manifolds and its implications for the convergence analysis of mirror descent. Our main result yields one-sided counterparts of the classical Levi--Civita characterizations of Lipschitz Riemannian gradients, each equivalent to relative smoothness. We further investigate the stationarity of mirror descent iterates for possibly nonconvex objectives and show that relative smoothness alone does not guarantee convergence of the Riemannian gradient norm to zero. We identify a one-sided condition on the cubic tensor that ensures such convergence and yields an $O(1/N)$ stationarity bound. Examples based on the negative entropy potential illustrate the role of metric variation.
Whitney-Type Real-Analytic Approximation on Banach Spaces I: The $C^0$ and $C^1$ Cases

The classical Whitney theorem on real-analytic approximation is a fundamental result in finite-dimensional analysis and geometry. Extending this theory to general infinite-dimensional Banach spaces involves longstanding open problems. This paper is the first part of our study of Whitney-type real-analytic approximation on Banach spaces, focusing on the $C^0$ and $C^1$ cases. We prove that a real Banach space admits a separating polynomial if and only if it admits a polynomial topological embedding into a real Hilbert space. We also introduce classes of mappings that locally factor through polynomial maps into finite-dimensional spaces and develop methods of real-analytic approximation for these classes. Using these tools, we establish fine $C^0$ and $C^1$ real-analytic approximation theorems for broad classes of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As applications, we resolve several open problems, including those concerning Whitney-type extensions with real analyticity off closed sets, real-analytic approximation preserving Lipschitz constants, and the real-analytic equivalence of diffeomorphic open subsets of Hilbert spaces.
From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras

We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.
Functions with finite energy on the Sierpinski gasket

This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpiński gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min--max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework. It is further shown that finite energy does not necessarily imply membership in the domain of the Laplacian. The framework is then applied to a class of fractal interpolation functions on the Sierpiński gasket, for which necessary and sufficient conditions for finite energy are established under suitable contractivity assumptions.
Scalar curvature deformation of isoparametric tubes

We resolve Ge's local scalar curvature rigidity conjecture for spherical isoparametric tubes. The conjecture fails throughout its stated radius range for families with at least two distinct principal curvatures, via arbitrarily small smooth deformations supported in any regular annulus. Geodesic balls of radius less than $\fracπ{2}$ are locally rigid under $C^2$ smallness. We also prescribe sufficiently small smooth nonradial scalar-curvature increments with fixed compact interior support, under antipodal symmetry for families with 2, 4, or 6 distinct principal curvatures and without symmetry for families with 3 distinct principal curvatures.
A Rooted Structure Theorem for $5$-Connected Graphs and $K_6^-$-Minors

Jorgensen conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$-minor is apex. For a $6$-connected graph containing a $K_4$ on vertices $a_1,\dots,a_4$, being apex is equivalent to $G-a_i$ having a planar embedding with the other three roots on a common face for some $i$, so that for such graphs the conjecture becomes a rooted planarity statement. Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas showed that the failure of the corresponding three-rooted planarity is witnessed by a legless tripod. We introduce a four-root structure, called a frame, that extends this certificate, and prove a structural theorem: every $5$-connected graph containing a frame rooted at four prescribed vertices contains a subgraph of one of five explicit types, denoted $A$--$E$. This theorem does not depend on the edges among the roots. As an application, we show that when the four roots span a $K_4^-$, each of the five configurations yields a $K_6^-$-minor. Together with a planar argument for the case without a frame and an induction based on a theorem of Kawarabayashi, this gives a proof that every non-planar $5$-connected graph contains a $K_6^-$-minor. This statement also follows from a recent theorem of Lo; our proof is independent and is driven by the rooted structure theorem, whose method we expect to apply to Jorgensen's conjecture with other target configurations.
Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds

We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.
Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation

Lei Shu; Zizhou Huang; Yunuo Chen; Yifei Li; Tao Du; Minchen Li; Tuur Stuyck; Miles Macklin; Kui Wu; Bo Zhu; Yin Yang; Ming C. Lin; Alberta Longhini; Rika Antonova; Leonidas Guibas; Gordon Wetzstein; Jeannette Bohg; Chenfanfu Jiang

Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The model classes, systems techniques and applications are surveyed through this lens, and we close with a reporting checklist, a released diagnostic that computes it, and a research agenda.
The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models
Julian Brandon; Bruno Loureiro; N Alex Cayco-Gajic; Arthur Pellegrino

Over the past decade, a growing body of work has established that implicit biases in learning dynamics fundamentally shape the solutions found by neural networks, governing their learned features and generalisation performance. However, despite these strides in deep learning theory, far less is known about representation learning in generative models based on dynamical systems, from normalising flows to diffusion. Importantly, empirical evidence suggests that continuous-time generative models can be prone to mode collapse, yet a learning theory explaining such biases remains elusive. To address this, we use tools from dynamical systems and operator theory to express the gradient flow of a general class of stochastic differential equations as a composition of linear operators, allowing us to relate collapse to low-rank biases in generative models. In variational inference and flow-matching tasks, we show that this bias can manifest in two different mechanisms: i) where collapsed models are stable fixed points of the gradient flow, or ii) in sequential feature learning, where smaller modes take progressively longer to be learned, producing an effective collapse for a fixed training budget. Together these findings point to a trade-off between feature learning and collapse, suggesting an operator view as a step towards a unified framework for understanding the learning dynamics of dynamical systems-based generative models.
The strong cylinder conjecture over prime fields

Let $p$ be prime and let $S\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ have $p^2$ points, with every affine plane meeting $S$ in a multiple of $p$ points. We give a self-contained argument that $S$ is a union of $p$ parallel lines.

Let $χ$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character and let $Λ(χ, s)$ be its associated completed $L$-function. The super-positivity property, introduced by Yun--Zhang (2017), asserts that $Λ^{(m)} \left( \frac{1}{2}, χ\right) \geq 0$ for all $m \geq 0$. We show that a certain positivity property of its Dirichlet theta function $θ(t, χ)$, namely that $θ(t, χ)>0$ for all $t \geq 1$, implies the super-positivity property for $χ$. We then investigate a refined form of the above property: we conjecture that the sequence $\{ Λ^{(2m)}\left(\frac{1}{2}, χ\right )\}_{ m \geq 0}$ is always eventually increasing and has at most one turning point, and we prove these assertions again when $θ(t, χ)>0$ for $t \geq 1$.
On semigroups of order-decreasing partial isometries: presentations and ranks of certain ideals
Gonca Ayık; Hayrullah Ayık; Vítor H. Fernandes

Let $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the monoid of all order-decreasing partial isometries on a chain with $n$ elements, and let $\mathcal{ODP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the submonoid of $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ consisting of all order-preserving partial isometries. In this paper, for each $1\leq r\leq n$, we determine minimal generating sets of the ideals $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ α\in \mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(α) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ α\in \mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(α) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$, thereby determining their ranks. Furthermore, we give presentations for the monoids $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$.
Controllability with and without Dissipation - a Port-Hamiltonian Approach
Jochen Glück; Anthony Hastir; Birgit Jacob; Hannes Wagener

A port-Hamiltonian system with energy dissipation can be modelled by connecting a larger, non-dissipative system with a so-called closure relation. We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.
On necessary conditions for feedback stabilizability when the control space is a fiber bundle
Wouter Jongeneel; Martina Scolamiero; Karl Henrik Johansson

Within control theory, a question of great interest is to understand when a stabilizing feedback exists. Building upon Krasnosel'ski\uı and co-workers, necessary conditions for the existence of a continuous stabilizing feedback have been pioneered by Brockett and Coron, providing so-called adversarial and homological conditions, respectively. Kvalheim recently generalized their conditions from equilibria to compact attractors and---in line with earlier work by Coron---showed that when a control system can be identified with a vector bundle, the homology condition is stronger, that is, the homology condition implies the adversary condition. Kvalheim also showed that this comparison breaks when extending the case of vector bundles to fiber bundles. In this work, we propose and characterize an appropriate adversarial condition for control systems represented by fiber bundles. The homology condition, on the other hand, is already well-defined, showcasing its general applicability. With the generalized conditions at hand, we show that by appropriately relaxing the regularity of the feedback under consideration, that is, by allowing for mild discontinuities, the homology condition implies the adversarial condition for fiber bundles. Thereby, in this work, we extend these earlier comparative results.
Ride-time inequalities for the event-based formulation of the dial-a-ride problem

The paper investigates the model structure of the event-based mixed-integer programming formulation of the Dial-a-Ride Problem. We find that the design of events allows introducing new valid inequalities on the ride times. Time progression is modelled using Big M constraints which lead to a weak LP relaxation and deteriorate the solution process. The newly introduced valid inequalities deal with this issue and allow reducing the computation times by up to 99% for benchmark instances (a-X* instances) in comparison to the state-of-the-art event-based model formulation. To evaluate the potential of the new valid inequalities, we increase the time windows on the benchmark set by another 15 minutes and evaluate the model on the same instances with a time-related objective function where the Big-M-influenced time variables directly occur in the objective function. Even for the large time windows only two instances could not be solved to optimality within two hours (final gaps of at most 0.8%). With the time-oriented objective the largest average computation time with our valid inequalities was 74 seconds.
Almost complex structures on triple blow-ups

We show that for certain smooth 4-manifolds, almost complex structures on its triple blow-up induce all its spin$^c$ structures with a non-negative-dimensional Seiberg-Witten moduli space. Since this includes all basic classes, our result provides an approximation to the simple type conjecture. Moreover, we expand a result by Dieter Kotschick showing that every finitely presented group is the fundamental group of an almost complex 4-manifold. We show that it can furthermore be chosen to have every even integer as the virtual dimension of the Seiberg-Witten moduli space of a spin$^c$ structure.
Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
Vincent Boulard; Amaury Hayat; Benedetto Piccoli; Emmanuel Trélat

We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.
Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey

Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.
Jacopo Borga; Valentin Féray; Peter Winkler

Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.
Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations

We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.
Topology, geometry and fabrication of volumetric plain weaves
Samuel Poincloux; Lauren Carelli Dreier; Tian Chen

Plain weave is one of the simplest woven structures, formed by two sets of yarns that cross at right angles in an alternating over-under pattern. While such woven fabrics are usually confined to a 2D surface, here we propose a practical approach to fabricate volumetric plain weaves, entanglements featuring three mutually orthogonal families of yarns threaded through a cubic lattice. We develop an analytic framework that converts the crossing pattern topology into continuous yarn centreline geometries, which we then leverage to fabricate volumetric weave specimens. Each crossing is encoded by a matrix that defines the offsets of the three yarns at a vertex. These are formulated to preserve the plain weave topology in every plane, where each pair of yarn families interlaces as in a planar plain weave. Eight configurations in four opposite pairs exist, yet all are related by rotations and translations, so that the fully alternating volumetric plain weave has a single topology. We adopt sinusoidal yarn trajectories and show that the crossing matrix defines their phases. We select two solutions: in-phase planar zigzags and out-of-phase circular helices. Both are members of a family of elliptical helices that also admits a free choice of handedness for each yarn. We then derive the conditions under which yarns intersect between vertices. In-phase yarns never intersect, whereas helical yarns of equal handedness intersect at a critical offset of $\sqrt{2}λ/16$, with $λ$ the wavelength of the cubic lattice. No assignment of handedness avoids these intersections. Finally, we fabricate volumetric plain weaves by 3D printing and manual assembly from cotton cord. The framework provides a direct basis for generating weave geometries for simulation and fabrication.
Operational Interpretation of Controllability Allocation Scores via Randomized Interventions

Controllability allocation scores (CASs) assign weights to virtual input channels without specifying how interventions should be implemented. This paper provides an operational interpretation through randomized finite-duration interventions with prescribed, possibly candidate-dependent waveforms. Selection probabilities are fixed before a mean-output target is specified, while waveform amplitudes are optimized after the target is revealed. We derive the unique minimum expected-energy amplitude policy and formulate volumetric and weighted average-energy allocation criteria. We also establish a finite-trial mean-output error bound and show that waveform-based weighted AE-CAS minimizes an upper bound on the target-averaged mean-square error. We establish uniform convergence of normalized waveform-response Gramians and show that accumulation points of optimal allocations solve the limiting problem. With uniform timing, equal positive waveform efficiencies recover the original CAS in the short-duration limit, whereas unequal efficiencies yield waveform-weighted limits. Under the former conditions, the limiting error bound is proportional to the original weighted AE-CAS objective. For common waveforms, we further establish an exact finite-duration correspondence with the original full-state V-CAS under uniform timing.
A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
Angela Kunoth; Anna Weller; Tolunay Yilmaz

Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still not understood from a biological point of view. How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a neurodegenerative disease in a computer? In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory and partial differential equations.
Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz
Lakshitha Fernando; Eranda Dhananjaya; Rajitha Ranasinghe; Dinusha Priyadarshani

A good coloring of a sphere triangulation is a black-and-white coloring of its faces such that, at every vertex, the numbers of black and white faces differ by a multiple of~$3$. Good colorings correspond to proper vertex $4$-colorings. For a good coloring with fold count $\mathrm{f}$ (the number of black-white edges) on a triangulation with $F$ faces, R.~E.~Schwartz introduced the Eisenstein isoperimetric ratio $η=\mathrm{f}^2/F$. For triangulations with degree sequence $6,\dots,6,2,2,2$, he proved that $η\ge3$ and conjectured that every such triangulation has a good coloring with $η$ below a universal constant. These triangulations are indexed by the nonzero Eisenstein integers~$β$. We study the family $\T(n)$ given by $β=n$, a positive integer, which consists of the doubled equilateral triangles of side~$n$. We prove that every good coloring of $\T(n)$ has at least $3n$ folds, so $η\ge9/2$, and that this bound is attained for every~$n$. Thus the minimum of $η$ on this family is exactly $9/2$, and Schwartz's conjecture holds for it. We also prove that subdividing a good coloring of $\T(β)$ gives a good coloring of $\T(nβ)$ with the same value of $η$. Consequently, Schwartz's conjecture holds in general if and only if it holds for primitive Eisenstein integers.
Equality in the direction bound over prime fields

Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$. This extends the Lovász--Schrijver classification for $2m+1=p$.
Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
Moritz Poguntke; Eda Oktay; Yuanzhe Xi; Erin Carson; Martin Stoll

Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.
Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$

We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(ψ,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form \begin{align} ψ(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}}, n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right) \end{align} in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system. The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(ψ,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$. We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.
Variational principles for dissipative continua: transport theorems, inertia, and the minimum-maximum duality

Variational principles for dissipative processes come in two families: minimum principles at nonequilibrium stationary states (Helmholtz, Kirchhoff, Prigogine) and maximum principles for relaxation in continuum mechanics (Ziegler, Hackl, Fischer). We contribute to the understanding of the thermodynamic extremal principle (TEP) by investigating its extremal properties, and uncover the connection between the two families, whose distinction was recently made precise for diffusion: the extremal character is decided by the regime, which is either relaxation at frozen state, as in a closed system (maximum dissipation), or a driven stationary state in an open system (minimum dissipation), while the underlying Rayleighian functional is convex and minimized in both cases. We further examine the Reynolds transport theorem, a useful tool for fixing the energy rates of continua, and the role of inertia, recently argued to lie beyond the reach of Rayleighian principles. With inertia the driving force must be held fixed during the variation, which is less elegant than in the inertialess case, where it is a state function. Writing the energy rate as rates times driving forces still yields the correct equations, and an extremal statement survives whenever the frozen force does not depend on the varied rate. This holds directly for unsteady Stokes flow, and for Navier-Stokes flow after a change to material coordinates, in which the particle acceleration is the second time derivative of the state and the convective term, nonvariational in the Eulerian description, does not appear. The framework is tested on the Navier-Stokes family (Stokes, unsteady Stokes, and Navier-Stokes flow, in order of increasing complexity) and on dissipative Lagrangian mechanics.

We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $ϕ^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, we produce generic extensions $V_1\subsetneq V_2$ of the universe with the same cardinals, cofinalities, and bounded subsets of $\aleph_ω$, such that $V_2$ is generated over $V_1$ by a cofinal $ω$-sequence in $\aleph_ω$, and $V_2$ is a minimal generic extension over $V_1$, i.e., every set of ordinals in $V_2\setminus V_1$ generates $V_2$ over $V_1$.
Uniqueness of positive solutions of mixed Laplacian and fractional Laplacian in $\mathbb R$
Xifeng Su; Chengxiang Zhang; Jiwen Zhang

We establish the uniqueness and nondegeneracy for positive finite-energy solutions of the following one-dimensional mixed Schrödinger equation \begin{equation} -Q'' + (-Δ)^s Q + Q = |Q|^p Q \quad \text{in } \mathbb R, \end{equation} where $0<s<1$ and $p>0$. For every $0<s<1, p>0$, we obtain the corresponding results for positive solutions whose linearized operators have Morse index equal to one. We extend the nodal analysis developed by Frank-Lenzmann-Silvestre to the mixed operator establishing the monotonicity of the quotient of a hypothetical nontrivial even kernel element by $-Q'$. We then combine this monotonicity with oscillation estimates to prove nondegeneracy, and uniqueness follows by continuation. Moreover, for every $1/2\le s<1,p>0$, both uniqueness and nondegeneracy hold for positive solutions. Our novelty is to use the properties of Green kernel of the mixed operator to derive the upper bound and lower bound on the maximum of each solution. This peak estimate allows us to prove uniqueness by direct comparison and to establish nondegeneracy.
Spectral conditions for the existence of $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in $t$-tough graphs

For $t>0$, a graph $G$ is called $t$-tough if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ for every $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-S)\geq2$, where $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of components of $G-S$. Toughness is closely related to the existence of Hamiltonian cycles and factors in graphs. Chvátal [Discrete Math. 5 (1973) 215--228] conjectured that there exists a constant $t_0>0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph of order at least three is Hamiltonian. Bauer, Broersma and Veldman [Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000) 317--321] constructed $(9/4-\varepsilon)$-tough graphs without a Hamiltonian path for arbitrarily small $\varepsilon>0$. For the weaker requirement of a $2$-factor, Enomoto et al. [J. Graph Theory 9 (1985) 87--95] proved that every $2$-tough graph of order at least three has a $2$-factor and that the toughness threshold $2$ is best possible. A graph $G$ is said to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor if and only if $G$ contains a spanning subgraph consisting of components that are either cycles or single edges. A $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor can be viewed as a combination of a $1$-factor and a $2$-factor, motivating the study of such factors in tough graphs. In this paper, we establish sharp sufficient conditions in terms of the adjacency spectral radius, the distance spectral radius, and the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius for a $t$-tough graph to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor.
Quasipositive and almost positive sectional curvature on finite quotients of Wallach spaces

We construct nonnegatively curved metrics on the cyclic and full permutation quotients of the Wallach flag manifolds in dimensions $6$, $12$, and $24$. The metrics are quasipositively curved in all three dimensions and almost positively curved in dimensions $12$ and $24$. The cyclic quotients are orientable with fundamental group $C_3$, and their further full permutation quotients have fundamental group $S_3$; none admits any metric of everywhere positive sectional curvature. For the almost-positive metrics we describe every zero-curvature plane and prove that the zero-point loci have Hausdorff dimensions exactly $11$ and $23$, respectively. A one-step deformation has, in each dimension, an explicit zero locus with nonempty interior. Further nested deformations reduce it to a measure-zero set while leaving a common codimension-one stratum. The argument combines normal forms for horizontal commuting planes with quaternionic rank conditions and a dimension estimate for commuting compressions of skew-symmetric operators. We also determine the possible degrees of arbitrary free finite quotients of the three flag covers and derive order bounds for fundamental groups when the Euler characteristic is nonzero. We have used ChatGPT-6-astra for mathematical exploration and verified and rewritten all the results.
Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
Guglielmo Padula; Antonio Colanera; Gianluigi Rozza

We present SPOD-GPR, a non-intrusive, parametric, spatio-temporal reduced-order model (ROM) that combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Spectral POD (SPOD), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). A parametric POD first projects the high-dimensional state onto a low-dimensional subspace. The reduced trajectories are then divided into windowed sections, transformed into the frequency domain, and truncated to the most energetic frequencies. SPOD is then performed independently at each retained frequency, yielding temporally coherent modes and coefficients. The parametric dependence of the POD and SPOD bases is modelled by GPR on a local chart of the Grassmann manifold after Procrustes alignment. The SPOD modal coefficients are learned both as explicit functions of the parameters and through a parameter-conditioned autoregressive model that allows for temporal extrapolation beyond the training window. Gaussian processes are sampled jointly and pathwise via Matheron conditioning, ensuring that each predictive realization carries uncertainty quantification consistent with the posterior distribution. The method is tested on four parametric examples where the parameter values and the prediction horizon lie outside the training data: the two-dimensional anisotropic Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation in a time-periodic and a travelling-wave regime, each parametrised by one of its two coefficients; flow past a cylinder parametrised by the Reynolds number; and flow past an elliptic obstacle parametrised by its semi-axes. In all cases, SPOD-GPR reduces the normalised mean absolute error compared to a POD-GPR baseline, and improves the calibration of the predictive uncertainty, especially in the fluid flow cases, where POD-GPR is severely overconfident. This opens the way to spectral, uncertainty-aware reduced-order models for many-query and real-time applications, such as digital twins.
A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs

In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.
A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects

Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same Stäckel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.
Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups

In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $Γ$ and $Λ$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $Γ$ to $Λ$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.
Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
Tran Nam Trung; Hoang Le Truong

We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gröbner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.
Conformal Prediction for Multi-Step Forecasting: Conditional Coverage and Sharp Score Calibration Rates

Uncertainty quantification in prediction is a central problem in statistics and machine learning. Conformal prediction provides a flexible approach to constructing prediction sets with valid marginal coverage under exchangeability. In this paper, we investigate conformal prediction for both one-step and multi-step forecasting from a single stationary time series, addressing temporal dependence and the additional challenges of joint prediction across multiple horizons. We propose a kernel-based framework, called Time series Residual Analysis for Calibration with Kernels (TRACK), for estimating conditional quantiles of residual scores and constructing prediction sets from rolling-window forecasters. The framework accommodates heterogeneous uncertainty across horizons and accounts for dependence induced by rolling estimation, while allowing predictor memory and forecast horizons to grow with the sample size. Our finite-sample bounds quantify how temporal dependence and overlapping score windows affect calibration and coverage. We further derive bounds for conditional quantile estimation and pointwise conditional coverage discrepancy. The guarantees extend to more general predictors that admit an accurate rolling-window approximation. We also derive matching minimax bounds over classes of known score maps, clarifying how overlapping score windows affect calibration accuracy. Experimental results from simulations and applications to wind energy generation and bike sharing demand show that our methods improve regional conditional coverage while maintaining competitive interval widths.
Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus

We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincaré inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.
Online Digital Twins: Data Assimilation and Control

The online assimilation of data and the application of controls are essential ingredients of the digital twin paradigm. In this paper, we formalize the online interaction between the physical process and its virtual digital representation in the setting of continuously arriving data from the physical process and a receding horizon virtual planning process, which provides the control for the physical process. Our mathematical formulation relies on a mean field representation of the data assimilation process as well as a mean field Pontryagin minimum principle for the optimal control problem. Such mean field formulations are computationally attractive because they allow for simultaneous implementation in terms of Hamiltonian interacting particle systems. A more detailed discussion is included for the ensemble Kalman-Bucy filter in combination with affine approximations of the receding horizon control laws. This paper sets out the mathematical framework, while a computational study is left for future research.
A Mathematical Multiscale Framework for Nonlinear Modeling of the Heliosphere
Daniele Telloni; Sabrina Guastavino; Michele Piana

The inner heliosphere is a highly nonlinear continuous medium where macroscopic ideal magnetohydrodynamics is inextricably coupled with microscopic, fully developed stochastic turbulence. State-of-the-art global 3D numerical solvers, while proficient at capturing the large-scale propagation of extreme space physics phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, are computationally constrained by grid resolution and fundamental partial differential equation formulations. Consequently, they inherently do not resolve the local small-scale turbulent cascade, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. To bridge this fundamental scaleseparation gap, this paper presents a novel mathematical and numerical framework that harmoniously integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics. The framework generates a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. This cascade reproduces theoretical constraints for fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency via a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model). This multiscale continuous background is dynamically perturbed by analytical models of large-scale nonlinear transients, including kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta formalized as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. By generating exact spatio-temporal arrays across arbitrary distributed coordinates, this unified mathematical model overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions, which are currently in their feasibility study phase.
Pairwise correlation bounds for the random-cluster model with cluster weight at most one

We establish quantitative bounds on pairwise edge correlations for the random-cluster model with cluster weight $q\in[0,1]$ on arbitrary finite connected graphs. We give two explicit bounds that retain the dependence on the activities of the two specified edges and hold uniformly over the activities of all remaining edges. We also obtain a refinement of one of these bounds using connectivity information from the graph with the two specified edges removed. These results sharpen the bound obtained by a direct application of Lorentzian polynomial theory. At $q=0$, the model is supported on connected spanning subgraphs. In particular, for the uniform probability measure on these subgraphs, the joint inclusion probability of two distinct edges is at most $10/9$ times the product of their marginal inclusion probabilities.
Optimal last-iterate rates for the projected decentralized stochastic subgradient method
Hao Wu; Chao Yin; Yuhong Dai; Liping Wang

We study the projected decentralized stochastic subgradient (PDSG) method for minimizing the average of convex, possibly nonsmooth local objectives over a common closed convex constraint set and a fixed connected undirected network. We focus on the finite-time expected suboptimality of the last local iterate generated at each node, which is the actual output locally available without time averaging or network averaging. Under the standard stepsizes $α_t=α/\sqrt{t}$ and $α_t=2/(μt)$, we establish $\mathcal{O}(\log T/\sqrt{T})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\log T/T)$ last-local-iterate rates for PDSG when each local objective is convex and the aggregate objective is strongly convex, respectively. Optim., 2021) as a special case. For adapting to decentralized settings, we propose a long-range variation condition to make the stepsize schedule compatible with network contraction. Under this cooldown stepsize, we obtain $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ and $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ last-local-iterate rates for PDSG in both problem classes, matching the optimal centralized dependence on $T$. Experiments on a lower-bound instance and constrained hinge-loss problems illustrate the predicted terminal behavior of local iterates and the control of consensus error under the cooldown stepsize.
Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I

We introduce Forelli--Rudin-type integral operators on the open unit ball of \(\ell^2\). We completely characterize the boundedness of these operators between weighted \(L^p\) and \(L^q\) spaces for all \(p,q\in[1,\infty]\), as well as their membership in every Schatten class of operators between the corresponding weighted \(L^2\) spaces. We also establish trace formulas for these operators that cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by a formal passage to the limit as the dimension tends to infinity. Our results are not merely infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). Rather, they reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the fundamental geometric and measure-theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. A key ingredient in our proofs is the establishment of new Forelli--Rudin-type asymptotic estimates in infinite dimensions. These estimates also provide new insights into the development of function theory on the infinite-dimensional unit ball.
An invariant higher index pairing under Morita equivalence for proper étale groupoids
Yu Qiao; Bing Kwan So; Hang Wang

For suitable proper étale groupoids, we study a part of the higher index that is invariant under Morita equivalence. We capture this part by a pairing between cyclic homology classes associated with isotropy groups and cyclic cohomology classes of the groupoid convolution algebra. We show that the pushforward is compatible with the maps induced by essential equivalences. This gives a numerical invariant depending only on the Morita equivalence class of the groupoid. In the case of a finite group action, we relate the resulting pairing to the equivariant index and to the Atiyah-Bott fixed-point formula.
Polynomial Sample Complexity of Noninteractive Simulation over Finite Alphabets

We study noninteractive simulation from a finite correlated source. Alice and Bob observe independent copies of the source and generate outputs without communication. We give a quantitative construction for arbitrary finite output alphabets: for every fixed source, a joint law that is simulable with arbitrarily many samples can be approximated using a number of samples polynomial jointly in the output alphabet sizes and the inverse accuracy. We first study binary outputs. A one-sided Wright--Fisher comparison gives a source-dependent explicit exponent and a finite-head Gaussian-threshold representation. We then handle arbitrary finite output alphabets through averaged influence regularity, simplex-preserving Gaussian moment lifting, and a common Gaussian projection for all correlated-prefix states. The sample exponent is independent of the output alphabet sizes. For a concrete biased binary source we certify an explicit exponent below $19$.
